papers.title: German medical students’ learning environment during the fading COVID-19 pandemic
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The Medical School's learning environment (MSLE) is important for medical students' academic performance and mental well-being. COVID-19 disrupted medical education worldwide through restrictions on practical and in-person teaching. Although several studies have showcased the immediate effects on medical students' perceptions of MSLE and mental well-being, less is known about the changes during the transition to post-pandemic medical education. METHODS: Four cross-sectional online surveys were conducted at a German medical school between winter 2021/2022 and summer 2023. MSLE was assessed using three items from the Johns Hopkins Learning Environment Scale (JHLES) and three self-developed items. Various validated items assessed distress (DT), perceived stress (PSS-4), depression (PHQ-2), anxiety (GAD-2), and loneliness (R-UCLA-3). Analyses included group comparisons and binary logistic regression. RESULTS: Across four survey waves, 687 individual medical and dental students participated. Positive MSLE perceptions were more frequent in later waves, although differences were not significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Social connectedness and access to mentoring were reported significantly more frequently in later waves. Higher age, more advanced study years, greater perceived stress, and perceived lack of practical experience were associated with lower odds of positive MSLE. The proportion reporting decreased study motivation since the onset of COVID-19 was significantly lower in the final wave. Older students, those in more advanced study years, and those experiencing loneliness or distress more frequently reported decreased motivation. Mental burden showed varying patterns: loneliness was generally lower in later waves, distress peaked in summer 2022, depressive symptoms and perceived stress in winter 2022/2023, and anxiety in summer 2023. After correction for multiple comparisons, only differences in distress across survey waves remained significant. Female students reported higher anxiety, loneliness, and perceived stress than male students, but only the gender difference in anxiety remained significant after correction. CONCLUSION: Medical students reported a more positive perception of the MSLE in later survey waves during the transition from pandemic to post-pandemic medical education. However, these improvements were not matched by a uniform recovery in medical students' well-being. Medical schools are therefore encouraged to strengthen students' learning environments by ensuring learning opportunities, mentoring, and mental health support throughout training.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study investigates the impact of the fading COVID-19 pandemic on the learning environment of German medical students, focusing on their perceptions of the Medical School's Learning Environment (MSLE) and mental well-being. The central question is whether the transition to post-pandemic education has led to improvements in MSLE and student well-being.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on four cross-sectional online surveys conducted at a German medical school between winter 2021/2022 and summer 2023. The MSLE was assessed using three items from the Johns Hopkins Learning Environment Scale (JHLES) and three self-developed items. Mental health was evaluated using validated scales for distress (DT), perceived stress (PSS-4), depression (PHQ-2), anxiety (GAD-2), and loneliness (R-UCLA-3). Analyses included group comparisons and binary logistic regression.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Medical students reported a more positive perception of the MSLE in later survey waves during the transition from pandemic to post-pandemic medical education. However, these improvements were not matched by a uniform recovery in medical students' well-being. Higher age, more advanced study years, greater perceived stress, and perceived lack of practical experience were associated with lower odds of positive MSLE.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study found that while positive MSLE perceptions increased over time, the changes were not statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. The proportion of students reporting decreased study motivation was significantly lower in the final wave, but this was not consistent across all demographic groups. The evidence also highlights varying patterns in mental health indicators, with distress peaking in summer 2022 and anxiety in summer 2023, suggesting unresolved issues in student well-being.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Medical schools are encouraged to strengthen students' learning environments by ensuring learning opportunities, mentoring, and mental health support throughout training. The study suggests a need for targeted interventions to address the mental health challenges faced by students, particularly those in more advanced study years and those experiencing loneliness or distress.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the impact of the fading COVID-19 pandemic on the learning environment and mental well-being of German medical students. Four cross-sectional surveys were conducted between winter 2021/2022 and summer 2023, assessing the Medical School's Learning Environment (MSLE) using standardized and self-developed items. The findings indicate that while perceptions of MSLE improved in later survey waves, there was no uniform recovery in student well-being. Factors such as age, study year, perceived stress, and lack of practical experience were linked to lower odds of positive MSLE. The study highlights the need for continued support in learning environments and mental health resources for medical students, especially those facing higher stress or loneliness.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述基于2021/2022年冬季至2023年夏季期间在德国一所医学院进行的四次横断面在线调查。MSLE的评估采用约翰霍普金斯学习环境量表(JHLES)的三个项目以及三个自编项目。心理健康状况使用经过验证的量表进行评估,包括压力(DT)、感知压力(PSS-4)、抑郁(PHQ-2)、焦虑(GAD-2)和孤独(R-UCLA-3)。分析包括组间比较和二元逻辑回归。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在疫情向后疫情时代医学教育过渡期间,医学生在后期调查中对MSLE的感知更加积极。然而,这些改善并未与医学生整体心理健康状况的统一恢复相匹配。较高的年龄、更高级的学习阶段、较高的感知压力以及感知到缺乏实践经验与积极的MSLE感知概率较低相关。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 研究发现,尽管对MSLE的积极感知随时间有所增加,但经过多重比较校正后,这些变化并不具有统计学意义。学习动机下降的比例在最后一次调查中显著降低,但这一趋势并非所有人口统计学群体都一致。证据还表明心理健康指标呈现出不同的模式,压力在2022年夏季达到峰值,焦虑则在2023年夏季上升,这表明学生心理健康状况仍存在未解决的问题。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The study investigates the impact of the fading COVID-19 pandemic on the learning environment of German medical students, focusing on their perceptions of the Medical School's Learning Environment (MSLE) and mental well-being. The central question is whether the transition to post-pandemic education has led to improvements in MSLE and student well-being.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on four cross-sectional online surveys conducted at a German medical school between winter 2021/2022 and summer 2023. The MSLE was assessed using three items from the Johns Hopkins Learning Environment Scale (JHLES) and three self-developed items. Mental health was evaluated using validated scales for distress (DT), perceived stress (PSS-4), depression (PHQ-2), anxiety (GAD-2), and loneliness (R-UCLA-3). Analyses included group comparisons and binary logistic regression.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Medical students reported a more positive perception of the MSLE in later survey waves during the transition from pandemic to post-pandemic medical education. However, these improvements were not matched by a uniform recovery in medical students' well-being. Higher age, more advanced study years, greater perceived stress, and perceived lack of practical experience were associated with lower odds of positive MSLE.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study found that while positive MSLE perceptions increased over time, the changes were not statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. The proportion of students reporting decreased study motivation was significantly lower in the final wave, but this was not consistent across all demographic groups. The evidence also highlights varying patterns in mental health indicators, with distress peaking in summer 2022 and anxiety in summer 2023, suggesting unresolved issues in student well-being.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Medical schools are encouraged to strengthen students' learning environments by ensuring learning opportunities, mentoring, and mental health support throughout training. The study suggests a need for targeted interventions to address the mental health challenges faced by students, particularly those in more advanced study years and those experiencing loneliness or distress.

papers.title_zh: German medical students’ learning environment during the fading COVID-19 pandemic
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: The Medical School's learning environment (MSLE) is important for medical students' academic performance and mental well-being. COVID-19 disrupted medical education worldwide through restrictions on practical and in-person teaching. Although several studies have showcased the immediate effects on medical students' perceptions of MSLE and mental well-being, less is known about the changes during the transition to post-pandemic medical education. METHODS: Four cross-sectional online surveys were conducted at a German medical school between winter 2021/2022 and summer 2023. MSLE was assessed using three items from the Johns Hopkins Learning Environment Scale (JHLES) and three self-developed items. Various validated items assessed distress (DT), perceived stress (PSS-4), depression (PHQ-2), anxiety (GAD-2), and loneliness (R-UCLA-3). Analyses included group comparisons and binary logistic regression. RESULTS: Across four survey waves, 687 individual medical and dental students participated. Positive MSLE perceptions were more frequent in later waves, although differences were not significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Social connectedness and access to mentoring were reported significantly more frequently in later waves. Higher age, more advanced study years, greater perceived stress, and perceived lack of practical experience were associated with lower odds of positive MSLE. The proportion reporting decreased study motivation since the onset of COVID-19 was significantly lower in the final wave. Older students, those in more advanced study years, and those experiencing loneliness or distress more frequently reported decreased motivation. Mental burden showed varying patterns: loneliness was generally lower in later waves, distress peaked in summer 2022, depressive symptoms and perceived stress in winter 2022/2023, and anxiety in summer 2023. After correction for multiple comparisons, only differences in distress across survey waves remained significant. Female students reported higher anxiety, loneliness, and perceived stress than male students, but only the gender difference in anxiety remained significant after correction. CONCLUSION: Medical students reported a more positive perception of the MSLE in later survey waves during the transition from pandemic to post-pandemic medical education. However, these improvements were not matched by a uniform recovery in medical students' well-being. Medical schools are therefore encouraged to strengthen students' learning environments by ensuring learning opportunities, mentoring, and mental health support throughout training.

papers.title: Structural insights into subunit exchange inhibition and ligand‐induced dimerization of SARS ‐ CoV ‐2 main protease
papers.abstract: Abstract The SARS‐CoV‐2 main protease (M pro ) is an essential homodimeric cysteine protease that mediates viral polyprotein processing and represents a primary therapeutic target for COVID‐19 treatment. While peptidomimetic inhibitors such as nirmatrelvir have demonstrated clinical efficacy, their effects on M pro quaternary structure dynamics remain poorly understood. Emerging evidence suggests these compounds may paradoxically promote dimerization, a phenomenon termed ligand‐induced dimerization (LID), which could enhance catalytic activity at low inhibitor concentrations. Here, we employed an integrated mass spectrometry platform combining metabolic 15 N labeling with native mass spectrometry (nMS), hydrogen‐deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX‐MS), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to elucidate the dynamic nature of M pro dimerization and its modulation by peptidomimetic inhibitors. We demonstrate that apo‐M pro exists in a dynamic monomer–dimer equilibrium characterized by rapid subunit exchange. Remarkably, peptidomimetic inhibitors, including nirmatrelvir, GC376, and MPI8, kinetically trap the dimeric state, suppressing subunit exchange and stabilizing the dimeric form of M pro . Region‐resolved HDX‐MS revealed that inhibitor binding induces widespread conformational stabilization extending beyond the active site to the N‐finger (residues 1–17) and dimer interface (residues 291–302). A notable transition of exchange mode from bimodal (EX1) to unimodal (EX2) in the N‐finger region provided a sensitive structural marker of ligand‐induced dimerization. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed that the observed stabilization arises primarily from dimer formation rather than direct ligand contacts. These findings establish a mechanistic basis for inhibitor‐stabilized dimerization, identify the N‐finger as a dynamic reporter of quaternary structure transitions, and demonstrate the power of integrated mass spectrometry for dissecting complex protein assembly dynamics with therapeutic implications for antiviral drug development.

While peptidomimetic inhibitors such as nirmatrelvir have demonstrated clinical efficacy, their effects on M pro quaternary structure dynamics remain poorly understood. Emerging evidence suggests these compounds may paradoxically promote dimerization, a phenomenon termed ligand-induced dimerization (LID), which could enhance catalytic activity at low inhibitor concentrations. Here, we employed an integrated mass spectrometry platform combining metabolic 15 N labeling with native mass spectrometry (nMS), hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to elucidate the dynamic nature of M pro dimerization and its modulation by peptidomimetic inhibitors. We demonstrate that apo-M pro exists in a dynamic monomer-dimer equilibrium characterized by rapid subunit exchange. Remarkably, peptidomimetic inhibitors, including nirmatrelvir, GC376, and MPI8, kinetically trap the dimeric state, suppressing subunit exchange and stabilizing the dimeric form of M pro . Region-resolved HDX-MS revealed that inhibitor binding induces widespread conformational stabilization extending beyond the active site to the N-finger (residues 1-17) and dimer interface (residues 291-302). A notable transition of exchange mode from bimodal (EX1) to unimodal (EX2) in the N-finger region provided a sensitive structural marker of ligand-induced dimerization. Molecular dynamics simulations confirmed that the observed stabilization arises primarily from dimer formation rather than direct ligand contacts. These findings establish a mechanistic basis for inhibitor-stabilized dimerization, identify the N-finger as a dynamic reporter of quaternary structure transitions, and demonstrate the power of integrated mass spectrometry for dissecting complex protein assembly dynamics with therapeutic implications for antiviral drug development.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the effects of peptidomimetic inhibitors on the quaternary structure dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 main protease (M pro), as their impact on M pro dimerization remains poorly understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed an integrated mass spectrometry platform to analyze the dynamic nature of M pro dimerization and its modulation by peptidomimetic inhibitors. The research focused on SARS-CoV-2 and its variants, with no specific mention of study dates or centers.
analysis.methods: The study combined metabolic 15 N labeling with native mass spectrometry (nMS), hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to elucidate the structural and dynamic changes in M pro induced by inhibitors.
analysis.main_results: Region-resolved HDX-MS showed that inhibitor binding induces widespread conformational stabilization beyond the active site, affecting the N-finger (residues 1–17) and dimer interface (residues 291–302). A notable transition of exchange mode from bimodal (EX1) to unimodal (EX2) in the N-finger region was observed as a structural marker of ligand-induced dimerization.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings establish a mechanistic basis for inhibitor-stabilized dimerization and identify the N-finger as a dynamic reporter of quaternary structure transitions, offering new insights into the structural dynamics of M pro and its implications for antiviral drug development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide critical structural insights into the behavior of M pro under inhibitor influence, which can inform the design of more effective antiviral therapies targeting this enzyme.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to abstract-level evidence, and the findings are based on computational and structural analyses rather than direct clinical or biological outcomes. The evidence strength is moderate due to the reliance on in silico methods.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the structural dynamics of SARS-CoV-2 main protease (M pro) under the influence of peptidomimetic inhibitors. It highlights the dynamic monomer–dimer equilibrium of apo-M pro and demonstrates that inhibitors like nirmatrelvir, GC376, and MPI8 kinetically trap the dimeric state, stabilizing it and suppressing subunit exchange. The research employs an integrated mass spectrometry platform, including native mass spectrometry (nMS), hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS), and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, to reveal conformational changes in M pro that extend beyond the active site to the N-finger and dimer interface. The findings suggest that the N-finger region serves as a sensitive structural marker of ligand-induced dimerization, offering new insights into the mechanisms of inhibitor action and potential implications for antiviral drug development. However, the study is limited to abstract-level evidence and relies on computational methods, which may affect the strength of the conclusions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨肽模拟抑制剂对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2主要蛋白酶(M pro)四级结构动态的影响,因为其对M pro二聚化的作用仍不明确。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究采用整合的质谱平台来分析M pro二聚化的动态性质及其受肽模拟抑制剂调控的情况。研究聚焦于严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2及其变体,未提及具体研究日期或研究中心。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究结合代谢15N标记与原生质谱(nMS)、氢-氘交换质谱(HDX-MS)和分子动力学(MD)模拟,以阐明抑制剂诱导的M pro结构和动态变化。
elements_zh.main_results: 区域解析的HDX-MS显示,抑制剂结合可引起广泛构象稳定化,不仅限于活性位点,还扩展到N-指(残基1–17)和二聚界面(残基291–302)。在N-指区域中观察到交换模式从双峰(EX1)转变为单峰(EX2)的显著转变,作为配体诱导二聚化的结构标记。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现确立了抑制剂稳定二聚化的机制基础,并识别了N-指作为四级结构转变的动态报告基因,为M pro的结构动态及其对抗病毒药物药物开发的潜在影响提供了新的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了关于抑制剂影响下M pro行为的关键结构见解,有助于设计更有效的抗病毒药物疗法,以靶向该酶。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于摘要层面的证据,其发现基于计算和结构分析,而非直接的临床或生物学结果。由于依赖于计算机模拟方法,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Efficacy of Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir in High-Risk Adults with Preexisting SARS-CoV-2 Immunity: A Pooled Analysis of Two Randomized Controlled Trials
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir (NMV/r) is an oral antiviral treatment approved to treat mild-to-moderate COVID-19 among adults at high risk of severe disease. We conducted a pooled analysis of NMV/r efficacy among high-risk participants from two clinical trials who had evidence of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) immunity through vaccination or previous infection. METHODS: Data were pooled from a subset of participants from the Evaluation of Protease Inhibition for COVID-19 in High-Risk Patients (EPIC-HR) trial (high-risk, unvaccinated) who were baseline seropositive for SARS-CoV-2 antibodies and high-risk Evaluation of Protease Inhibition for COVID-19 in Standard-Risk Patients (EPIC-SR) participants who were vaccinated against SARS-CoV-2. In both trials, participants were randomized within 5 days of symptom onset to twice-daily NMV/r 300/100 mg or placebo for 5 days. Endpoints included coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19)-related hospitalization or all-cause death through day 28, number of medical visits, time to symptom alleviation, and percentage of participants with severe symptoms. RESULTS: Overall, 1600 participants were included in the pooled analysis (NMV/r, 807 [EPIC-HR, n = 490; EPIC-SR, n = 317]; placebo, 793 [EPIC-HR, n = 479; EPIC-SR, n = 314]). NMV/r significantly reduced COVID-19-related hospitalization or all-cause death by 73.7% compared with placebo (0.5% versus 1.9%, P = 0.0104). Relative to placebo, NMV/r was also associated with fewer medical visits (21 versus 53, P = 0.0076) and a 2-day reduction in time to symptom alleviation (12 versus 14 days, P = 0.0470). Participants treated with NMV/r were less likely to report severe targeted COVID-19 symptoms compared with placebo (22.1% relative reduction on days 2-6 [P = 0.0441]; 46.6% relative reduction on days 7-28 [P = 0.0011]). CONCLUSIONS: NMV/r reduced hospitalization and death, medical visits, time to symptom alleviation, and severe symptoms among high-risk participants with preexisting SARS-CoV-2 immunity. CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: NCT04960202; NCT05011513.

papers.title: Identificação in silico de mutações das variantes de preocupação do SARS-CoV-2 em sítios de anelamento e redesenho dos primers e sondas de RT-qPCR afetados In silico identification of SARS-CoV-2 variant-of-concern mutations in annealing sites and redesign of the affected RT-qPCR primers and probes
papers.abstract: COVID-19, caused by SARS-CoV-2, exhibits high genetic variability, and mutations in regions recognized by primers and probes may compromise the reliability of RT-qPCR tests. This study assessed the impact of variant-of-concern mutations on the annealing sites of diagnostic assays and proposed corrected sets for the affected assays. This is a descriptive-analytical in silico study. Six complete genomes, the Wuhan-Hu-1 reference and one representative of each variant of concern (Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta and Omicron), were retrieved from GenBank and aligned with Clustal Omega. Forty oligonucleotides from five protocols (CDC, Charité/WHO, China CDC, HKU and Institut Pasteur) were mapped onto the reference genome. After consolidating sequences identical across protocols, 37 unique oligonucleotides organised into 12 sets were analysed. Thirty remained intact across the five variants and seven displayed at least one mismatch, totalling 18 events, all non-synonymous, distributed over 11 genomic positions. The China CDC N set concentrated 12 of these events by overlapping the 28,881–28,883 cluster, the origin of the R203K and G204R substitutions. One event was classified as highly critical: the substitution at position 15,451 (ORF1b:G662S, Delta variant), located one base from the 3′ end of the forward primer of the RdRP_SARSr set. New sets were designed for the five affected assays, restricted to the 28,825 positions (96.4% of the genome) conserved across all six sequences, showing complete complementarity and adequate thermodynamic parameters. Specificity screening against the six reference human coronaviruses indicated no expected reactivity with MERS-CoV or with the seasonal coronaviruses, although the sets targeting ORF1b and the E gene retain recognition of SARS-CoV, a property inherited from the original pan-Sarbecovirus design. Global genome conservation does not ensure the integrity of diagnostic sites, and monitoring these regions should be integrated into routine genomic surveillance.

analysis.methods: The study retrieved six complete genomes from GenBank and aligned them with Clustal Omega. It mapped forty oligonucleotides from five protocols onto the reference genome and consolidated sequences identical across protocols to identify unique oligonucleotides.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the importance of integrating genomic surveillance of diagnostic sites into routine practices to ensure the accuracy of RT-qPCR tests for SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in silico analysis, which may not fully capture real-world performance. However, the evidence is strong as it is based on alignment of six complete genomes and specificity screening against six reference human coronaviruses.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of SARS-CoV-2 variant-of-concern mutations on the annealing sites of RT-qPCR primers and probes. By aligning six complete genomes, including the Wuhan-Hu-1 reference and representatives of Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, and Omicron variants, the authors identified 18 non-synonymous mutations across 11 genomic positions. One mutation at position 15,451 (ORF1b:G662S, Delta variant) was classified as highly critical. The authors proposed new primer and probe sets that maintain complete complementarity and adequate thermodynamic parameters, ensuring specificity against related coronaviruses. The study highlights the importance of monitoring diagnostic sites for mutations to maintain the reliability of RT-qPCR tests. The evidence is strong due to the use of complete genome sequences and specificity screening, but the in silico nature of the study limits its real-world applicability.

papers.title_zh: 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2关注变异株在环化位点的In silico突变鉴定及受影响的RT-qPCR引物和探针重新设计
papers.source_body_en: COVID-19, caused by SARS-CoV-2, exhibits high genetic variability, and mutations in regions recognized by primers and probes may compromise the reliability of RT-qPCR tests. This study assessed the impact of variant-of-concern mutations on the annealing sites of diagnostic assays and proposed corrected sets for the affected assays. This is a descriptive-analytical in silico study. Six complete genomes, the Wuhan-Hu-1 reference and one representative of each variant of concern (Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta and Omicron), were retrieved from GenBank and aligned with Clustal Omega. Forty oligonucleotides from five protocols (CDC, Charité/WHO, China CDC, HKU and Institut Pasteur) were mapped onto the reference genome. After consolidating sequences identical across protocols, 37 unique oligonucleotides organised into 12 sets were analysed. Thirty remained intact across the five variants and seven displayed at least one mismatch, totalling 18 events, all non-synonymous, distributed over 11 genomic positions. The China CDC N set concentrated 12 of these events by overlapping the 28,881–28,883 cluster, the origin of the R203K and G204R substitutions. One event was classified as highly critical: the substitution at position 15,451 (ORF1b:G662S, Delta variant), located one base from the 3′ end of the forward primer of the RdRP_SARSr set. New sets were designed for the five affected assays, restricted to the 28,825 positions (96.4% of the genome) conserved across all six sequences, showing complete complementarity and adequate thermodynamic parameters. Specificity screening against the six reference human coronaviruses indicated no expected reactivity with MERS-CoV or with the seasonal coronaviruses, although the sets targeting ORF1b and the E gene retain recognition of SARS-CoV, a property inherited from the original pan-Sarbecovirus design. Global genome conservation does not ensure the integrity of diagnostic sites, and monitoring these regions should be integrated into routine genomic surveillance.

papers.title: Personalized HLA-aware TCR measure predicts the risk of symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection following booster vaccination
papers.abstract: HLA-driven heterogeneity and limitations of live T cell functional assays routinely thwart assessment of cell-mediated immunity in vaccination trials. To address this, we developed a T-cell receptor (TCR)-based measure of immunogen recognition and evaluated it in COV-BOOST, a third-dose COVID-19 vaccine trial, during the Delta and Omicron waves (2021-2022, United Kingdom). We estimated HLA-aware Spike-reactive T cell (HA-TS) breadth from participant HLA genotypes, TCR{beta} repertoires, and a novel SARS-CoV-2 S HLA-linked reference catalog. Higher post-boost HA-TS breadth was associated with lower symptomatic infection risk (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.39-0.86). This association persisted after adjustment for neutralizing antibody titers and IFN-{gamma} responses. Examination of HA-TS across prior studies showed that it reflects participant genotype, exposure intensity, and time from exposure to sampling. These findings highlight the possibility that estimates of antigen-specific T cell repertoire breadth could serve as a correlate of protection to accelerate vaccine development.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address the challenges of assessing cell-mediated immunity in vaccination trials by developing a T-cell receptor (TCR)-based measure of immunogen recognition. The research evaluated this measure in COV-BOOST, a third-dose COVID-19 vaccine trial, during the Delta and Omicron waves in the United Kingdom. The authors estimated HLA-aware Spike-reactive T cell (HA-TS) breadth using participant HLA genotypes, TCR{beta} repertoires, and a novel SARS-CoV-2 S HLA-linked reference catalog. Higher post-boost HA-TS breadth was associated with lower symptomatic infection risk (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.39-0.86). The association remained significant even after adjusting for neutralizing antibody titers and IFN-{gamma} responses. These results suggest that HA-TS breadth could serve as a correlate of protection, offering potential for accelerating vaccine development. However, the study acknowledges limitations posed by HLA-driven heterogeneity and the challenges of live T cell functional assays.

papers.title: Correlation Study between Civilian SARS-CoV-2 Wastewater Concentration and COVID-19 Cases among U.S. Military Health System Beneficiaries
papers.abstract: Wastewater-based epidemiology has emerged as a new near real-time tool for population-wide COVID-19 surveillance. This study examined the statistical correlation between county-level civilian SARS-CoV-2 wastewater concentration and COVID-19 cases among beneficiaries of the U.S. Military Health System (MHS) from April 2024 to April 2025 in the continental United States. The analysis revealed an overall high correlation for both MHS beneficiaries ( rs = 0.797; 95% CI: 0.626–0.893) and active-duty service members ( rs = 0.800; 95% CI: 0.633–0.892). Further, an assessment of external factors suggested that correlations were stronger in regions with higher MHS populations. Our findings indicated that civilian SARS-CoV-2 wastewater served as a robust early indicator for COVID-19 trends among MHS beneficiaries and that integrating civilian wastewater data may enhance near real-time Department of War health surveillance monitoring of COVID-19.
papers.journal: The American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene

papers.title: Structure-based and AI-guided redesign of Sotrovimab for enhanced recognition of SARS-CoV-2 BA.2 and the E340G escape mutant
papers.abstract: Introduction The rapid evolution of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants has substantially compromised the efficacy of several monoclonal antibody therapies, including Sotrovimab, through mutations that disrupt antibody–antigen recognition. Developing antibodies with improved recognition of emerging variants and resistance-associated mutations is therefore essential for maintaining therapeutic effectiveness. Methods Here, we employed an integrated computational framework combining structure-guided antibody engineering, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted sequence design, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and binding free-energy analyses to redesign Sotrovimab against the Omicron BA.2 receptor-binding domain (RBD) and the clinically relevant E340G escape mutant. Residue-level energetic profiling was used to identify destabilizing interface residues, followed by mutational redesign and ProteinMPNN-guided sequence optimization. The resulting candidates were evaluated through 500 ns all-atom MD simulations, complemented by conformational analyses, MM/PBSA binding free-energy calculations, residue-level energy decomposition, and dynamic cross-correlation analyses. Results and Discussion The top-ranked redesigned Sotrovimab candidates retained the characteristic immunoglobulin fold while exhibiting improved structural stability, compactness, and reduced conformational fluctuations. Principal component analysis and free-energy landscape calculations further revealed more confined and energetically favorable conformational states, suggesting enhanced dynamic compatibility with the target RBD. MM/PBSA calculations indicated substantially more favorable binding free energies for both redesigned candidates against the BA.2 RBD and E340G mutant. Residue-level energy decomposition and dynamic cross-correlation analyses further demonstrated improved energetic complementarity and intermolecular communication across the antibody–antigen interface. These improvements were accompanied by enhanced hydrogen-bonding, hydrophobic, and van der Waals interactions, together with increased engagement of the conserved N343-linked glycan, potentially providing additional stabilization to the antibody -antigen complex. Among the redesigned candidates, Sotrovimab-design-2 consistently exhibited the most favorable structural and energetic characteristics. Conclusion Collectively, these findings demonstrate the potential of integrating AI-guided sequence optimization with structure-based antibody engineering to improve antibody recognition of SARS-CoV-2 variants and resistance-associated mutations. This framework provides a computational foundation for developing mutation-resilient therapeutic antibodies against evolving viral pathogens.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address the challenge of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants compromising the efficacy of monoclonal antibody therapies like Sotrovimab. The researchers developed a computational framework integrating structure-guided antibody engineering, AI-assisted sequence design, molecular dynamics simulations, and binding free-energy analyses to redesign Sotrovimab for improved recognition of the BA.2 variant and the E340G escape mutant. The top-ranked redesigned candidates showed enhanced structural stability, compactness, and reduced conformational fluctuations. Principal component analysis and free-energy landscape calculations indicated more confined and energetically favorable conformational states, suggesting better dynamic compatibility with the target RBD. MM/PBSA calculations revealed more favorable binding free energies for the redesigned candidates against the BA.2 RBD and E340G mutant. Residue-level energy decomposition and dynamic cross-correlation analyses demonstrated improved energetic complementarity and intermolecular communication across the antibody-antigen interface. These findings highlight the potential of combining AI-guided sequence optimization with structure-based antibody engineering to enhance therapeutic effectiveness against evolving SARS-CoV-2 variants. The study's results are based on computational methods and simulations, which provide insights into the structural and energetic improvements of the redesigned antibodies.

papers.title_zh: 基于结构和人工智能引导的Sotrovimab改造,以增强对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 BA.2变体及E340G逃逸突变体的识别能力
papers.source_body_en: Introduction The rapid evolution of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants has substantially compromised the efficacy of several monoclonal antibody therapies, including Sotrovimab, through mutations that disrupt antibody–antigen recognition. Developing antibodies with improved recognition of emerging variants and resistance-associated mutations is therefore essential for maintaining therapeutic effectiveness. Methods Here, we employed an integrated computational framework combining structure-guided antibody engineering, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted sequence design, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and binding free-energy analyses to redesign Sotrovimab against the Omicron BA.2 receptor-binding domain (RBD) and the clinically relevant E340G escape mutant. Residue-level energetic profiling was used to identify destabilizing interface residues, followed by mutational redesign and ProteinMPNN-guided sequence optimization. The resulting candidates were evaluated through 500 ns all-atom MD simulations, complemented by conformational analyses, MM/PBSA binding free-energy calculations, residue-level energy decomposition, and dynamic cross-correlation analyses. Results and Discussion The top-ranked redesigned Sotrovimab candidates retained the characteristic immunoglobulin fold while exhibiting improved structural stability, compactness, and reduced conformational fluctuations. Principal component analysis and free-energy landscape calculations further revealed more confined and energetically favorable conformational states, suggesting enhanced dynamic compatibility with the target RBD. MM/PBSA calculations indicated substantially more favorable binding free energies for both redesigned candidates against the BA.2 RBD and E340G mutant. Residue-level energy decomposition and dynamic cross-correlation analyses further demonstrated improved energetic complementarity and intermolecular communication across the antibody–antigen interface. These improvements were accompanied by enhanced hydrogen-bonding, hydrophobic, and van der Waals interactions, together with increased engagement of the conserved N343-linked glycan, potentially providing additional stabilization to the antibody -antigen complex. Among the redesigned candidates, Sotrovimab-design-2 consistently exhibited the most favorable structural and energetic characteristics. Conclusion Collectively, these findings demonstrate the potential of integrating AI-guided sequence optimization with structure-based antibody engineering to improve antibody recognition of SARS-CoV-2 variants and resistance-associated mutations. This framework provides a computational foundation for developing mutation-resilient therapeutic antibodies against evolving viral pathogens.
papers.abstract_zh: 引言 新冠病毒Omicron变体的快速进化显著削弱了包括Sotrovimab在内的多种单克隆抗体疗法的有效性,这些变化通过干扰抗体-抗原识别机制实现。因此,开发能够更好地识别新兴变体并具有抗逃逸突变能力的抗体对于维持治疗效果至关重要。方法 在本研究中,我们采用了一种整合的计算框架,结合结构引导的抗体工程、人工智能(AI)辅助的序列设计、分子动力学(MD)模拟和结合自由能分析,对Sotrovimab进行改造,以针对Omicron BA.2受体结合域(RBD)和具有临床意义的E340G逃逸突变体。通过残差级能量谱分析确定了不稳定界面残基,随后进行突变设计和由ProteinMPNN引导的序列优化。所得候选抗体通过500纳秒全原子MD模拟进行评估,并辅以构象分析、MM/PBSA结合自由能计算、残差级能量分解和动态交叉相关分析。结果与讨论 排名最高的Sotrovimab改造候选抗体保留了特征性的免疫球蛋白折叠结构,同时表现出增强的结构稳定性、紧凑性和减少的构象波动。主成分分析和自由能景观计算进一步揭示了更为受限且能量更有利的构象状态,表明其与目标RBD的动态兼容性得到了增强。MM/PBSA计算显示,这两个改造候选抗体对BA.2 RBD和E340G突变体的结合自由能显著更有利。残差级能量分解和动态交叉相关分析进一步证明了抗体-抗原界面处更优的能量互补性和分子间通信。这些改进伴随着增强的氢键、疏水和范德华相互作用,以及保守的N343连接糖蛋白的更高参与度,可能为抗体-抗原复合物提供额外的稳定性。在所有改造候选抗体中,Sotrovimab-design-2始终表现出最有利的结构和能量特性。结论 这些发现表明,将人工智能引导的序列优化与基于结构的抗体工程相结合,能够有效提升抗体对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2变体及抗逃逸突变能力的识别。该框架为开发针对不断演变的病毒病原体的抗逃逸突变治疗性抗体提供了计算基础。

papers.title: Immunogenicity and safety of inactivated SARS-CoV-2 vaccine (CoronaVac) using a two-dose primary protocol in children and adolescents (Immunita-002, Brazil): a phase IV one-year follow-up
papers.abstract: Long-term evidence on the durability and quality of immune responses induced by the inactivated whole-virus CoronaVac vaccine in children and adolescents remains limited. We evaluated humoral and cellular immunity and safety over 12 months after completion of the primary vaccination schedule. In this phase IV longitudinal study, 640 children and adolescents aged 3–17 years who received two doses of CoronaVac were followed for 12 months. Humoral immunity was assessed by anti-Spike (anti-S) and anti-Nucleocapsid (anti-N) IgG ELISAs and neutralizing antibody assays against the ancestral SARS-CoV-2 B.1 lineage and Omicron BA.1 and BA.5 subvariants. Cellular immunity was evaluated through antigen-specific stimulation of peripheral blood mononuclear cells, multiplex quantification of soluble immune mediators, and immune network analysis. Safety and suspected COVID-19 cases were monitored throughout follow-up. Anti-S and anti-N IgG seropositivity remained high throughout follow-up (90-96% and 93-98%, respectively). Neutralizing antibodies against the ancestral B.1 lineage remained high in both age groups, although seropositivity decreased to 80% at 12 months among children aged 3–11 years. In contrast, cross-neutralization against Omicron BA.5 increased over time, reaching 100% seropositivity in both age groups at 12 months. Vaccination was associated with changes in chemokines, inflammatory and regulatory cytokines, and growth factors, alongside dynamic immune network remodeling. Antigen-specific PBMC stimulation demonstrated cytokine and chemokine responses one year after vaccination, with distinct profiles following ancestral and Omicron Spike stimulation. No additional adverse events were reported during the final six months. Previously reported serious adverse events resolved without vaccine-related sequelae, and no clinically reported COVID-19 cases occurred during the final six months of surveillance. CoronaVac induced persistent humoral responses and was associated with longitudinal changes in antigen-stimulated immune activity over 12 months. Integrated immunological analyses provide insights into the durability and coordination of immune responses following primary vaccination in children and adolescents, while the mechanisms underlying immune memory and the relationship between immune responses and clinical protection remain to be elucidated.
authors: Jordana Grazziela Alves Coelho dos Reis

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the immunogenicity and safety of the inactivated SARS-CoV-2 vaccine CoronaVac in children and adolescents over a one-year follow-up period. The research aimed to assess humoral and cellular immunity and safety, with 640 participants aged 3–17 years receiving two doses of the vaccine. Humoral immunity was measured using IgG ELISAs and neutralizing antibody assays against the ancestral B.1 lineage and Omicron subvariants, while cellular immunity was analyzed through PBMC stimulation and immune network profiling. Results showed persistent anti-S and anti-N IgG responses, with neutralizing antibodies against B.1 remaining high but decreasing in younger children. Cross-neutralization against Omicron BA.5 increased, reaching 100% seropositivity in both age groups. Safety monitoring indicated no additional adverse events in the final six months, and previously reported serious events resolved without sequelae. The study suggests CoronaVac induces durable immune responses and immune network changes, though the relationship between these responses and clinical protection remains unclear. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and lack of control groups.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 目前关于灭活全病毒CoronaVac 疫苗在儿童和青少年中诱导的免疫应答的持久性和质量的长期证据仍然有限。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们评估了在完成基础疫苗接种接种计划后12个月内的体液免疫、细胞免疫和安全性。在本项第四期纵向研究中,640名3至17岁接受两剂CoronaVac的儿童和青少年被随访了12个月。
elements_zh.methods: Humoral immunity was assessed by anti-Spike (anti-S) and anti-Nucleocapsid (anti-N) IgG ELISAs and neutralizing antibody assays against the ancestral SARS-CoV-2 B.1 lineage and Omicron BA.1 and BA.5 subvariants. Cellular immunity was evaluated through antigen-specific stimulation of peripheral blood mononuclear cells, multiplex quantification of soluble immune mediators, and immune network analysis. Safety and suspected COVID-19 cases were monitored throughout follow-up.
elements_zh.main_results: 抗S和抗N IgG血清阳性率在整个随访期间保持较高水平(分别为90-96%和93-98%)。针对原始B.1谱系的中和抗体在两个年龄段均保持较高水平,但3至11岁儿童在12个月时血清阳性率降至80%。相比之下,针对奥密克戎BA.5的交叉中和能力随时间增加,12个月时两个年龄段均达到100%血清阳性率。疫苗接种与趋化因子、炎症和调节性细胞因子以及生长因子的变化相关,并伴随动态免疫网络重塑。在最后六个月中未报告额外的不良事件。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: CoronaVac诱导了持续的体液免疫反应,并与12个月内抗原刺激引起的免疫活动的纵向变化相关。综合免疫学分析为儿童和青少年在完成基础疫苗接种接种后免疫应答的持久性和协调性提供了见解,而免疫记忆的机制以及免疫应答与临床保护之间的关系仍有待阐明。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为CoronaVac 疫苗接种在儿童和青少年中诱导的免疫应答的持久性以及免疫网络重塑的潜力提供了谨慎的见解,这可能有助于未来疫苗的研发和长期监测策略的制定。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其依赖于自我报告的安全性数据,并且在六个月内缺乏长期临床结果。证据强度中等,因为其基于一项单一的观察性研究,且没有对照组。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 目前关于灭活全病毒CoronaVac 疫苗在儿童和青少年中诱导的免疫应答的持久性和质量的长期证据仍然有限。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们评估了在完成基础疫苗接种接种计划后12个月内的体液免疫、细胞免疫和安全性。在本项第四期纵向研究中,640名3至17岁接受两剂CoronaVac的儿童和青少年被随访了12个月。
analysis_zh.main_results: 抗S和抗N IgG血清阳性率在整个随访期间保持较高水平(分别为90-96%和93-98%)。针对原始B.1谱系的中和抗体在两个年龄段均保持较高水平,但3至11岁儿童在12个月时血清阳性率降至80%。相比之下,针对奥密克戎BA.5的交叉中和能力随时间增加,12个月时两个年龄段均达到100%血清阳性率。疫苗接种与趋化因子、炎症和调节性细胞因子以及生长因子的变化相关,并伴随动态免疫网络重塑。在最后六个月中未报告额外的不良事件。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: CoronaVac诱导了持续的体液免疫反应,并与12个月内抗原刺激引起的免疫活动的纵向变化相关。综合免疫学分析为儿童和青少年在完成基础疫苗接种接种后免疫应答的持久性和协调性提供了见解,而免疫记忆的机制以及免疫应答与临床保护之间的关系仍有待阐明。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为CoronaVac 疫苗接种在儿童和青少年中诱导的免疫应答的持久性以及免疫网络重塑的潜力提供了谨慎的见解,这可能有助于未来疫苗的研发和长期监测策略的制定。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其依赖于自我报告的安全性数据,并且在六个月内缺乏长期临床结果。证据强度中等,因为其基于一项单一的观察性研究,且没有对照组。

papers.title: Schistosoma mansoni Infection Alters Antibody Subclass Profiles but Preserves SARS-CoV-2 mRNA Vaccine-Induced Neutralizing Activity in a Murine Model
papers.abstract: Abstract Objectives Helminth infections can modulate host immune responses and potentially influence immunogenicity of vaccines against unrelated pathogens. This study investigated the effects of Schistosoma mansoni infection on immune responses to COVID-19 mRNA vaccine (BNT162b2) on in a murine model. Methods Two experiments were conducted using C57BL/6J mice assigned to three groups: uninfected and unvaccinated controls, S. mansoni -infected vaccinated mice, and uninfected vaccinated mice. The experiments differed in parasite inoculum and BNT162b2 vaccine dose. IgG, IgG1, and IgG2a antibodies against the spike-protein S1 were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing activity was assessed using an in vitro virus neutralization assay. For Experiment 1 (Exp 1), bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) of spleen tissues and measurement of cytokine production by peptide-stimulated splenocytes were also performed. Results Vaccination induced robust spike-specific antibody responses in both infected and uninfected mice. In Exp 1, infected mice exhibited significantly higher total IgG and IgG2a titres than uninfected vaccinated mice following the booster dose. In Experiment 2 (Exp 2), antibody titres were comparable between vaccinated groups. The IgG2a/IgG1 ratio was consistently higher in uninfected vaccinated mice, suggesting that S. mansoni infection altered vaccination-induced antibody subclass profiles. In Exp 1, liver egg burden was inversely correlated with IgG2a titres (Spearman’s ρ = −0.87, p = 0.0054), but this association was not observed in Exp 2. Peptide-stimulated splenocytes from infected mice showed significantly lower levels of the Th1-associated cytokines in infected mice. Despite these immunological changes, neutralizing activity did not differ significantly between infected and uninfected vaccinated mice in either experiment. Neutralizing titres were positively correlated with total spike-specific IgG and IgG2a titres in both experiments. mansoni infection modified Th1-associated immune response to BNT162b2 vaccination, particularly antibody subclass distribution, without consistently reducing spike-specific antibody titres or SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing activity. These findings suggest that helminth-associated immune modulation can alter vaccine-induced immune responses without necessarily compromising the generation of functional antiviral antibodies. Further studies involving direct viral challenge and longer-term immune assessments are needed to determine whether these responses confer equivalent protection in infected and uninfected hosts.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated how Schistosoma mansoni infection affects immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccines in a murine model. Two experiments were conducted with varying parasite inoculum and vaccine dose, comparing infected and uninfected vaccinated mice. The results showed that while S. mansoni infection altered antibody subclass profiles, it preserved SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing activity. The findings suggest that helminth-associated immune modulation may influence vaccine-induced responses without reducing functional antiviral antibodies. These results could inform vaccine strategies in helminth-endemic areas. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨曼氏血吸虫感染如何影响免疫应答到严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2 mRNA 疫苗,基于对寄生虫感染可以调节宿主免疫并可能影响疫苗对无关病原体的免疫原性的理解。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用C57BL/6J小鼠进行了两项实验,分为三组:未感染且未接种疫苗的对照组、感染曼氏血吸虫并接种疫苗的小鼠组以及未感染但接种疫苗的小鼠组。实验在寄生虫接种量和疫苗剂量方面有所不同。
elements_zh.methods: 通过酶联免疫吸附测定(ELISA)测量了针对刺突蛋白S1的IgG、IgG1和IgG2a抗体。通过体外病毒中和试验评估了严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的中和活性。此外,在实验1中还进行了脾脏组织的批量RNA测序以及肽刺激脾细胞的细胞因子产生检测。
elements_zh.main_results: 疫苗接种在感染和未感染小鼠中均诱导了针对刺突蛋白的强特异性抗体反应。在实验1中,感染小鼠在加强剂量后总IgG和IgG2a滴度显著高于未感染接种疫苗的小鼠。未感染接种疫苗的小鼠中IgG2a/IgG1比值始终较高。感染小鼠的肽刺激脾细胞显示出显著较低的Th1相关细胞因子水平。在两个实验中,感染和未感染接种疫苗的小鼠之间的中和活性均无显著差异。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,寄生虫相关的免疫调节可能改变疫苗诱导的免疫应答,而不一定损害功能性抗病毒药物抗体的产生。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了关于寄生虫感染如何影响疫苗对严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2的反应的见解,这可能有助于在寄生虫流行地区制定疫苗的开发和接种策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于小鼠模型,结果可能无法直接应用于人类免疫应答。证据强度中等,因为这些发现基于体外和体内实验,而没有直接的病毒感染或长期免疫评估。

supplementary_news.content_title: National flu and COVID-19 surveillance report: 12 November 2026 (week 46)
supplementary_news.content: This publication is licensed under the terms of the Open Government Licence v3.0 except where otherwise stated. To view this licence, visit nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3 or write to the Information Policy Team, The National Archives, Kew, London TW9 4DU, or email: psi@nationalarchives.gov.uk . Where we have identified any third party copyright information you will need to obtain permission from the copyright holders concerned. This publication is available at https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/national-flu-and-covid-19-surveillance-reports-2026-to-2027-season/national-flu-and-covid-19-surveillance-report-12-november-2026-week-46 This report summarises the information from the surveillance systems which are used to monitor COVID-19 (caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2)), influenza, respiratory syncytial virus ( RSV ) and diseases caused by other seasonal respiratory viruses in England. The report is based on data up to week 45 of 2026 (2 November to 8 November 2026). The main messages of this report are: Annual reports for the 2025 to 2026 season: Influenza in the UK, annual epidemiological report: winter 2025 to 2026 (published 28 May 2026) Epidemiology of COVID-19 in England (published 25 June 2026) Seasonal influenza vaccine uptake in all GP patients: annual report 2025 to 2026 (published 28 May 2026) Seasonal influenza vaccine uptake in school-aged children: annual report 2025 to 2026 (published 28 May 2026) Seasonal influenza vaccine uptake in frontline healthcare workers: annual report 2025 to 2026 (published 28 May 2026) Influenza activity increased and is circulating at low levels. Emergency department ( ED ) attendances for influenza-like-illness ( ILI ) increased and were above seasonally expected levels. The number of influenza-confirmed acute respiratory infection ( ARI ) incidents increased compared with the previous week. A briefing note has been issued to inform the NHS that influenza activity is now above baseline levels. Compared with the equivalent week last season (week 45 data, 2025 to 2026), vaccine uptake is lower among patients aged 65 years and over (63.1% versus 65.1%), patients aged 6 months to under 65 years in clinical risk groups (30.4% versus 31.4%), those aged 2 years (35.8% versus 36.6%), and those aged 3 years (35.6% versus 36.8%). In contrast, vaccine uptake is higher among pregnant women (32.7% versus 31.4%). Influenza vaccination data was unavailable or incomplete at the time of analysis in weeks 41 and 42 and led to several cohorts not being published in week 42. This has been corrected since week 43, and all cohorts are included. This will be corrected retrospectively in the report for week 42. There remains an issue that affects the attribution of vaccinations by provider setting. This is not expected to affect overall vaccination uptake estimates, which are considered to remain an accurate reflection of the influenza vaccination programme. COVID-19 activity was stable and is circulating at low levels. ED attendances for COVID-19-like illness decreased. The number of COVID-19 confirmed acute respiratory infections ( ARI ) incidents increased compared with the previous week. By the end of week 45 2026, 51.8% of all people aged 75 years and over in England had been vaccinated with an autumn 2026 dose. Similarly, 22.1% of all people aged under 75 years with a weakened immune system in England had been vaccinated with an autumn 2026 dose since 1 October 2026. RSV hospital activity increased to low levels with other indicators within baseline levels. ED attendances for acute bronchiolitis increased and were below seasonally expected levels. Note 1: these indicators use the moving epidemic method ( MEM ) and the mean standard deviation method ( MSD ) to define thresholds to determine their respective levels of activity. Further information on these methods can be found in Influenza surveillance in Europe: establishing epidemic thresholds by the Moving Epidemic Method and Setting thresholds to determine COVID-19 activity levels using the mean standard deviation ( MSD ) method, England, 2022 to 2024 . The MEM approach is well-established for some influenza surveillance indicators, however, for other indicators both the MEM and MSD are experimental and may be subject to future revision. Influenza laboratory surveillance and GP swabbing positivity have transitioned from using MEM to using MSD . These approaches will be considered alongside expert opinion and triangulation of other data sources. The Second Generation Surveillance System ( SGSS ) captures test result information for notifiable infectious diseases, including COVID-19 and influenza, from laboratories in England. The unified sample dataset ( USD ) stores all SARS-CoV-2 test results reported to SGSS , Respiratory DataMart and UKHSA laboratories, and is used to calculate the percentage of tests positive for SARS-CoV-2 among all SARS-CoV-2 tests conducted. As of 10 November 2026, there were a total of 1,587 COVID-19 cases identified in hospital settings in week 45, decreasing from 1,914 cases in the previous week. SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) PCR positivity in hospital settings remained stable in week 45, with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 7.2% up to Sunday 8 November 2026 compared with 7.4% for the same period on the previous Sunday. Positivity rates were highest among those aged 85 years and over with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 10.7% up to Sunday 8 November 2026. This has remained stable compared to 10.7% in the same age group on the previous Sunday. Note 2: data from previous seasons is aligned by day. Note 3: testing policy and practice may change over time which can impact positivity rates, therefore comparisons over time should be interpreted with caution. Notable changes in testing policy occurred during 2022 to 2023, which are outlined in the data quality report . Note 4: the highlighted line corresponds to the age group in the subplot title, grey lines correspond to all other age groups. Influenza positivity remained stable in week 45, with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 8.1% up to Sunday 8 November 2026. This is compared with 7.8% on the previous Sunday. By type, influenza A positivity remained stable in week 45, with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 7.2% up to Sunday 8 November 2026. Influenza B positivity remained stable in the same week, with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 0.3% up to Sunday 8 November 2026. Influenza A positivity rates were highest among those aged between 5 and 11 years, with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 12.8% up to Sunday 8 November 2026. This has increased from 10.7% in the same age group on the previous Sunday. Influenza B positivity rates for the same period were highest among those aged between 12 and 17 years, with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 1.6%. This has increased from 1.0% in the same age group on the previous Sunday. RSV swab-positivity based PCR test results reported through SGSS have been included as a pilot indicator from week 49 2025 onwards. RSV positivity increased in week 45, with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 3.2% up to Sunday 8 November 2026, compared with 2.5% up to the previous Sunday. RSV positivity rates were highest in those aged between 0 and 4 years with a rolling 7-day positivity rate of 19.6% up to Sunday 8 November 2026 in week 45. This has increased from 15.6% in the same age group on the previous Sunday. Respiratory DataMart is a sentinel laboratory-based surveillance system where participating laboratories report positive and negative test results for a number of respiratory viruses from samples primarily taken in hospital. A small proportion of primary care samples are also included in this reporting. In week 45, data is based on reporting from 9 out of the 14 sentinel laboratories. In week 45, 4,231 respiratory specimens reported through the Respiratory DataMart System were tested for influenza. There were 328 positive samples for influenza: 216 influenza A (not subtyped), 10 influenza A (H3N2), 88 influenza A (H1N1)pdm09, and 18 influenza B. Overall, influenza positivity remained stable at 7.8% in week 45 compared with 7.5% in the previous week. In week 45, 4,588 respiratory specimens reported through the Respiratory DataMart System were tested for SARS-CoV-2. There were 271 positive samples for SARS-CoV-2. SARS-CoV-2 positivity decreased slightly to 5.9% compared with 7.2% in the previous week, with the highest positivity in those aged 80 years and over at 9.4%. RSV positivity increased slightly to 3.2%, with the highest positivity in those aged under 5 years at 17.5%. Adenovirus positivity remained stable at 1.8%, with the highest positivity in those aged between 5 and 14 years at 5.6%. Human metapneumovirus ( hMPV ) positivity decreased to 0.1%, with the highest positivity in those aged between 65 and 79 years at 0.3%. Parainfluenza positivity remained stable at 3.6%, with the highest positivity in those aged under 5 years at 11.7%. Rhinovirus positivity decreased slightly to 14.1%, with the highest positivity in those aged under 5 years at 28.4%. DataMart data is provisional and subject to retrospective updates. Note 5: shading represents 95% confidence intervals. This section is updated fortnightly. Data below was last updated in the week 45 report. UKHSA conducts genomic surveillance of SARS-CoV-2 lineages. This section provides an overview of circulating lineages in England, derived from data on sequenced PCR -positive SARS-CoV-2 samples in SGSS . The prevalence of UKHSA -designated lineages among sequenced cases is presented in Figure 13. To account for reporting delays, we report the proportion of lineages within COVID-19 cases that have had a sequenced positive sample between 28 September 2026 and 11 October 2026. Note that low sequencing numbers, especially within the latest reporting period, will impact the accuracy of the prevalence estimates. These most recent figures should therefore be interpreted with caution. Note that lineages will be grouped independently from their parent lineage once they reach sufficient prevalence, and may be re-grouped into their parent lineage if their prevalence subsequently falls. The data quality report contains more information on lineage groupings. Analysis of viruses from primary and secondary care shows that circulating A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses show low genetic diversity and all belong to clade D.3.1.1. Observations published from the WHO influenza vaccine composition meeting (VCM) in September 2026 suggest low reactivity of some viruses within the D.3.1.1 subclade with post-infection ferret antisera raised against A/Missouri/11/2025 (H1N1)pdm09-like virus – the A(H1N1)pdm09 component in 2026 Southern and 2026 to 2027 Northern Hemisphere cell- and egg-based influenza vaccines - and human sera post-vaccination with the Southern Hemisphere vaccine 2026. It is not yet clear how vaccine effectiveness against clinical disease may be affected by these observations. Vaccines typically still provide protection against severe clinical disease when drifted strains are seen with only a modest reduction in effectiveness. The characterisation of circulating A(H3N2) viruses shows that A(H3N2) viruses are currently showing low genetic diversity. All sequenced viruses to date belong to genetic subclade K. To date, only a small number of influenza B viruses have been detected, which show some genetic diversity. Between week 35 2026 (week ending 30 August 2026) and week 45 2026 (week ending 8 November 2026), the UKHSA respiratory virus unit ( RVU ) has genetically characterised 397 seasonal influenza viruses, and identified 267 influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses, 96 influenza A(H3N2) viruses, and 34 influenza B viruses. Details of the characterised viruses by subtype are shown in Tables 1, 2 and 3. The RVU has confirmed by genome sequencing the detection of live attenuated influenza vaccine ( LAIV ) viruses in 16 influenza A/B positive samples, collected from children aged between 2 and 16 years. UKHSA RVU performs antigenic characterisation of influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, influenza A(H3N2) and influenza B viruses using haemagglutination inhibition ( HI ) assays. Data from these assays are used to compare how similar the currently circulating influenza viruses are to the strains included in seasonal influenza vaccines, and to monitor for changes in circulating influenza viruses. Similarity of currently circulating influenza strains to vaccine strains is defined as having an antibody titre within 4-fold when compared with reference viruses representative of the vaccine strain. Antigenic characterisation of viruses in the current reporting period is underway. A(H1N1)pdm09: 13 A(H1N1)pdm09 viruses have been antigenically characterised and 11 were similar to reference viruses representative of the A/Missouri/11/2025 (H1N1)pdm09-like Northern Hemisphere 2026 to 2027 (H1N1)pdm09 vaccine strains. A(H3N2): 6 A(H3N2) viruses have been antigenically characterised and 6 were similar to reference viruses representative of the A/Darwin/1454/2025 (H3N2)-like and A/Darwin/1415/2025 (H3N2)-like Northern Hemisphere 2026 to 2027 (H3N2) vaccine strains. Influenza positive samples are screened for mutations in the virus neuraminidase ( NA ) and the cap-dependent endonuclease of the polymerase acidic protein (PA) genes known to confer neuraminidase inhibitor (oseltamivir and zanamivir) or baloxavir resistance, respectively. Results from this surveillance are given in table 4. There have been seven detections with mutations related to reduced susceptibility/resistance to oseltamivir and/or reduced susceptibility to baloxavir. Data is presented on viral ARI incidents in different settings that are reported to UKHSA health protection teams ( HPTs ). Please note that reporting practices are known to vary between seasons and between regions. Any interpretation of temporal and regional trends should consider the likelihood of differences in reporting of ARI incidents over time and between regions. There were 124 new ARI incidents reported in week 45 in England. These included: 114 incidents from care homes, of which 25 were due to SARS-CoV-2, 23 were due to influenza A, 12 were due to influenza (no type information available), 5 were due to multiple pathogens, 4 were due to other pathogens and 1 was due to RSV . No pathogen was reported in 44 incidents 2 incidents from hospitals, of which 2 were due to SARS-CoV-2 7 incidents from educational settings, of which 3 were due to RSV and 1 was due to influenza (no type information available). No pathogen was reported in 3 incidents 1 incident from other settings, of which 1 was due to SARS-CoV-2 FluSurvey is an internet-based participatory surveillance system based on the InfluenzaNet platform. It monitors trends of influenza-like illness ( ILI ) in the community using self-reported respiratory symptoms from registered participants. As a participatory surveillance system, new signups can occur throughout the season and participation can vary in each week. The European Centre for Disease Control ( ECDC ) ILI case definition of sudden onset of symptoms with at least one of fever (chills), malaise, headache, muscle pain and at least one of cough, sore throat, shortness of breath is used for reporting. Please note that ILI is a broad definition and can include other respiratory illnesses such as COVID-19. Healthcare use is presented as self-reported use of health services among participants meeting the ILI ECDC case definition. Where a person reports use of more than one healthcare service, secondary care will be indicated over primary care use and physical attendance to primary care will be indicated over use of remote services (for example, online NHS services, telephoning their GP or 111). During week commencing 2 November 2026: there were 2,484 participants who completed the weekly symptoms questionnaire 361 (14.5%) reported fever or cough and 126 (5.1%) met the ILI case definition, in the past week 14.3% of participants meeting the ILI case definition reported contact with healthcare services as a result of self-reported symptoms; the most frequently reported contact was a visit to the pharmacy the proportion of participants meeting the ILI case definition slightly decreased compared with the previous week (5.1% compared with 5.3% in week 44) data submitted in the current week (commencing 9 November) is available on the UKHSA data dashboard to support more timely insights. For further details see the data quality report Syndromic surveillance collects data from various healthcare sources where presentations are classified by patterns of symptoms compatible with specific infections. In some settings, the syndromic diagnosis can be supplemented by (rapid) testing. In this report, ED attendances are displayed. Further details and data from other syndromic surveillance systems can be found in the syndromic surveillance weekly summaries . During the week ending on 8 November 2026, ED attendances for acute respiratory infections increased slightly and were similar to the seasonally expected level. ED attendances for COVID-19-like illness decreased. ED attendance for influenza-like illness increased slightly and was above seasonally expected levels. ED attendances for acute bronchiolitis (a syndrome related to RSV infection) increased and were below seasonally expected levels. NHS 111 online assessments for acute respiratory infections increased and remained similar to expected levels, while NHS 111 triaged calls for acute respiratory infections remained stable and below expected levels. GP in-hours consultation rates for lower respiratory tract infections and bronchiolitis increased in children aged 0 to 4 years. Careers Internships & Fellowships Apprenticeships & Workforce Development Work at DOE Funding Opportunities Breadcrumb Biological and Environmental Research Redesigned Hepatitis C Drug Becomes a Powerful New Treatment for COVID-19 Redesigned Hepatitis C Drug Becomes a Powerful New Treatment for COVID-19 Scientists transformed an old drug into a potent COVID-19 treatment effective against drug-resistant variants. Biological and Environmental Research February 19, 2026 Estimated Read Time 3 min The final version of the redesigned drug binds tightly to the main COVID-19 protease, an enzyme the virus needs to multiply. The drug’s structure is effective even against mutated forms that resist other treatments. Image courtesy of Stanford University The Science Researchers have redesigned the hepatitis C drug boceprevir to create a more effective treatment for COVID-19. Some virus variants no longer respond well to current therapies, like Paxlovid, due to mutations in the main COVID-19 virus protease (Mpro). This is a key enzyme the virus uses to replicate. Mpro is essential to the virus and remains intact from variant to variant. As such, it is an ideal target for treatments to focus on. Using X-ray crystal structures, scientists refined boceprevir atom by atom. They worked to improve how the drug binds within key pockets of the enzyme. The researchers used the Stanford Synchrotron Radiation Lightsource (a DOE Office of Science User Facility) to analyze the crystal structure when the drug was attached to Mpro. The Impact This research produced a drug that is effective against COVID-19 strains that are resistant to existing treatments. The resulting compound, ML2006a4, binds more tightly and durably than earlier drugs. It also shows superior protection in preclinical animal studies. By redesigning an older hepatitis C drug, scientists made it more effective against mutated forms of the virus’s protease. This could help doctors treat patients who no longer respond to existing therapies. Summary Boceprevir is a protease inhibitor originally developed to treat hepatitis C. Scientists adapted this drug to target the main protease (Mpro) of SARS-CoV-2. This is a critical enzyme the virus uses to process its polyproteins and replicate. Because Mpro is conserved across variants and has no close human equivalent, it remains a prime target for antiviral drug development. However, some SARS-CoV-2 variants contain mutations in Mpro that reduce the effectiveness of existing treatments. Using X-ray crystallography data collected at the Macromolecular Crystallography Beamlines at the Stanford Synchrotron Radiation Lightsource (SSRL), researchers determined high-resolution structures of Mpro bound to various boceprevir analogs. These structural insights guided a stepwise redesign of the molecule to improve its fit within the enzyme’s active site and sub-pockets. The team optimized interactions and reduced internal strains within the drug’s structure to improve binding, potency, and resistance profile. The final compound, ML2006a4, binds covalently to Mpro and retains strong activity even against variants harboring resistance-associated mutations. This structure-guided approach demonstrates how iterative design can yield next-generation antivirals with broad-spectrum activity. It also underscores the vital role of DOE- and NIH-supported synchrotron-based methods in accelerating drug discovery against emerging viral threats. Contact Michael Lin Stanford University mzlin@stanford.edu Funding Funding for this research included: Sarafan ChEM-H and the Innovative Medicines Accelerator, Harrington Scholar-Innovator Award, Emergent Ventures at the Mercatus Center at George Mason University, Stanford-Coulter Translational Research Grant, National Institute of Health(NIH)/National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) Antiviral Drug Discovery (AViDD) Center, the Denver Foundation, the Novo Nordisk Foundation, the Stanford Bio-X Program and a Bio-X Interdisciplinary Graduate Student Fellowship, E&M Foundation Postdoctoral Fellowship, Postdoctoral Fellowship in Translational Medicine from the PhRMA Foundation and an anonymous donation to establish the Stanford BSL3 facility. The research used resources at SSRL, a DOE Office of Science user facility, and of the SSRL Structural Molecular Biology Program supported by the DOE Office of Biological and Environmental Research and by NIH National Institute of General Medical Sciences. Publications Westberg, M., et al. “An orally bioavailable SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibitor exhibits improved affinity and reduced sensitivity to mutations”, Sci. Transl. Med. 16, eadi0979 (2024). Coronavirus (COVID-19) cases, %%COUNTRY%% data Source: World Health Organization Loading... Loading... Loading... What is the definition of 'confirmed' and 'reported' in COVID-19 data? All data represents the date of reporting as opposed to date of symptom onset. All data is subject to continuous verification and may change based on retrospective updates to accurately reflect trends, changes in country case definitions and/or reporting practices.
