COVID-19)大流行过去多年之后,世界仍持续面临重大的健康、社会与经济挑战,而新发与再发传染病依然是日益严峻的全球公共卫生关切。这一趋势凸显了相互关联卫生系统的重要性,并揭示了全球公 义翘神州以4RISE服务能力,为全球AI蛋白设计团队提供高效、深入、连续的验证服务,了解更多>> 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Review Open access 在2019冠状病毒病(Coronavirus Disease 2019, COVID-19)大流行过去多年之后,世界仍持续面临重大的健康、社会与经济挑战,而新发与再发传染病依然是日益严峻的全球公共卫生关切。这一趋势凸显了相互关联卫生系统的重要性,并揭示了全球公共卫生准备与应对的优势与劣势。在此背景下,研究人员对COVID-19大流行与近期安第斯病毒(Andes virus, ANDV)疫情进行比较分析,聚焦其流行病学与病毒学特征,并讨论COVID-19公共卫生应对的有效性。研究人员同时探讨了可应用于快速变化生态系统中未来人畜共患威胁的关键经验教训。研究结果显示,COVID-19与汉坦病毒(Hantavirus)感染共享若干分子与临床特征,但传播模式存在差异。COVID-19可在人际间高效传播并引发全球大流行,而汉坦病毒感染主要由啮齿动物传播至人类,尽管病例死亡率(case fatality rate, CFR)更高,但仍呈地域性局限。虽然COVID-19已有疫苗,但汉坦病毒病(Hantavirus disease)目前尚无疫苗。研究还强调,人工智能(artificial intelligence, AI)、疫情情报(epidemic intelligence)与“同一健康”(One Health)方法在改善疫情预测、检测与监测方面的价值。 1 Introduction 欢迎下载【综合性CAR-NK细胞疗法开发解决方案】从早期靶点发现到临床前研发每个阶段全方位需求解析,全面支持CAR-NK细胞研究。领 取 人畜共患疾病被定义为可在动物与人类之间通过直接或间接接触传播的感染性疾病,病原体涵盖细菌、病毒、寄生虫、真菌、立克次体、衣原体、支原体等多种类型。部分人畜共患病原体拥有多个动物储主,通过维持病原体存在、扩增及向人类溢出而促进传播。据估计,人畜共患疾病每年约导致270万死亡,对全球健康影响显著。环境改变,包括森林砍伐、栖息地破碎化、农业扩张、灌溉、城市化及气候变化,破坏生态系统并增加人类与野生动物接触,从而促成疟疾、莱姆病等疾病并促进病原体溢出。宿主数量与分布的变化可显著影响人畜共患疾病的发生与传播。例如,1991至1992年及1997至1998年发生在美国西南部的厄尔尼诺事件通过增加降水与植被生长为啮齿动物提供更多食物,导致啮齿动物数量显著增加,进而促进汉坦病毒在啮齿动物间传播并导致人类汉坦病毒感染病例上升。气候变化与栖息地破坏亦与近期病例增加相关,如阿根廷气候变化与栖息地破坏通过有利于啮齿动物储主而直接或间接地促进病例增加。人口增长与对食物需求的增加提高了人类接触食源性人畜共患病原体的机会。环境破坏已使汉坦病毒感染、Mpox、埃博拉病毒病及COVID-19等具备严重暴发与广泛公共卫生影响的潜力。COVID-19由严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2, SARS-CoV-2)引起,提供了人畜共患疾病全球健康后果的重大案例。SARS-CoV-2于2019年末在中国武汉被首次识别,早期调查提示最初病例与海鲜及活体动物市场存在流行病学关联。蝙蝠被认为是相关冠状病毒的可能自然储主,而包括穿山甲在内的其他动物的潜在中间宿主作用仍不确定且持续被研究。COVID-19大流行将人畜共患疾病推至全球关注前沿,展示了人类-动物-环境界面的破坏如何产生深远健康、社会与经济后果。近期,世界经历了与邮轮MV Hondius相关的新安第斯病毒(ANDV)疫情。该疫情的重要性不在于其提示大流行级传播力,而在于其结合了严重的自然感染与延迟且非特异性早期症状、高度流动的国际接触者、船上有限的医疗能力、复杂的多司法管辖区监督,以及COVID-19大流行后公众增加的传染病暴发敏感性。这引出了一个重要问题:COVID-19公共卫生应对的有效性如何,以及哪些经验教训可应用于2026年ANDV疫情作为快速变化生态系统中当代案例的研究。为回答此问题,本研究采用比较分析方法,从综合多学科与环境视角审视两种疾病的流行病学、病毒学、生态学与公共卫生维度。 2 Epidemiology 2019年,新发严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒(severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus, SARS-CoV)SARS-CoV-2出现并迅速全球蔓延。世界卫生组织(World Health Organization, WHO)于2020年3月11日宣布COVID-19构成大流行。截至2024年4月13日,全球报告病例超7.04亿,死亡约701万。欧洲2020年超额死亡率介于14.9%至54.3%,美洲死亡率约1%,非洲与亚洲病例死亡率(case fatality rate, CFR)因地区而异,范围从0.346%至2.548%不等。SARS-CoV-2并非首个被识别的冠状病毒(coronavirus, CoV),在SARS-CoV-2之前已有六种人类冠状病毒被认知,其中两种——严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒(SARS-CoV)与中东呼吸综合征冠状病毒(Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus, MERS-CoV)——与严重及有时致命的疾病相关。关于近期ANDV疫情,WHO于2026年5月2日报告船上乘客出现严重呼吸道疾病集群。船上载有147名乘客与船员。至5月4日,已确定7例汉坦病毒相关病例,包括2例实验室确诊与5例疑似。在这些病例中,3例死亡,1例病情危重,3例表现为轻度症状。截至2026年7月2日,共报告13例病例,含3例死亡,对应23%的病例死亡率(CFR)。其中12例经实验室确诊ANDV感染,1例分类为可能病例。汉坦病毒并非新发病原体,而是早已被认知的重要人畜共患病毒。据估计每年全球发生1万至超过10万例汉坦病毒感染,亚洲与欧洲负担最高。肾综合征出血热(hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, HFRS)主要在亚洲与欧洲导致数千病例,病例死亡率低于1%至15%;汉坦病毒心肺综合征(hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, HCPS)主要发生于美洲,与更高死亡率相关,美洲CFR高达50%。具体而言,在智利,近70%的HCPS患者报告有职业或家庭啮齿动物暴露史,20至35%在高风险区域 recreational activities 中暴露。2025年,美洲区域报告229例病例与59例死亡,CFR为25.7%。在法国大陆,汉坦病毒感染相对罕见,2005年以来每年报告14至320例经确诊的HFRS病例,但德国与芬兰发病率更高。2025年,美国报告890例汉坦病毒病例。 3 Virology SARS-CoV-2属于冠状病毒科(Coronaviridae),巢病毒目(Nidovirales),是一种包膜、单股正链RNA病毒,由包膜(envelope, E)、膜(membrane, M)、核衣壳(nucleocapsid, N)及刺突(spike, S)四种主要结构蛋白组成。其通过S蛋白与血管紧张素转换酶2(angiotensin-converting enzyme 2, ACE2)受体结合进入宿主细胞,S蛋白被宿主蛋白酶切割为S1与S2亚基。人-人间传播主要通过密切接触经呼吸道飞沫与气溶胶发生,特别是在拥挤或通风不良的室内环境,也可间接通过接触污染物传播。潜伏期通常为2至7天。值得注意的是,SARS-CoV-2亦 capable of 反向人畜共患传播(reverse zoonotic transmission),人类可将病毒传给动物,特别是鼬科物种、老虎、狮子、土狼、鹿及仓鼠。汉坦病毒属于汉坦病毒科(Hantaviridae),布尼亚病毒目(Bunyavirales),为包膜球形RNA病毒,基因组分节包括小(small, S)、中(medium, M)、大(large, L)节段,分别编码核蛋白(nucleoprotein, N)、包膜糖蛋白(glycoproteins, Gn与Gc)及RNA依赖性RNA聚合酶(RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, L protein)。汉坦病毒主要从啮齿动物传播给人类,但大多数不在人际间传播。ANDV是已知具有人际传播能力的主要汉坦病毒,尤其与感染的长时间密切接触相关。汉坦病毒感染潜伏期通常较COVID-19更长,一般为1至6周;ANDV潜伏期为7至39天,中位数约18天。 4 Viral strains RNA病毒具有高度遗传变异与适应能力。冠状病毒尤其以频繁遗传重组为特征,可加速病毒进化。WHO将部分SARS-CoV-2变异株列为关注变异株(variant of concern, VOC)或感兴趣变异株(variant of interest, VOI),包括Alpha、Beta、Gamma、Delta、Omicron等,这些变异株显著影响病毒传播力、毒力、临床结局及感染控制策略。2020年至2021年2月, ancestral SARS-CoV-2 strain remain predominant。2021年3月至7月,Alpha、Beta与Gamma变异株出现并逐渐流行。2021年8月至11月,Delta成为优势株,与传播及疾病负担大幅增加相关。2022年初,Omicron出现导致报告感染数急剧上升。在非洲,大流行呈现三波:第一波以原始株为主,第二波以Delta为主,第三波与Omicron出现相关。欧洲则经历了四波主要流行。不同变异株CFR各异,Beta(4.19%)与Gamma(3.60%)较高,Omicron(0.70%)较低。Delta变异株亦与动物园内传播相关。关于汉坦病毒多样性,截至2020年已识别38种汉坦病毒株,目前近140个分类单元被认可。汉坦病毒传统上分为旧世界(Old World)与新世界(New World)两类。风险组2包括PUUV与TULV;风险组3包括HTNV、DOBV、SEOV、SNV、ANDV及Bayou。每种汉坦病毒通常与特定储主相关。 5 Immunopathogenesis and host-pathogen interactions SARS-CoV-2通过其S蛋白与ACE2受体结合进入宿主细胞。感染后先天免疫激活,触发免疫细胞募集及细胞因子如白介素-6(interleukin-6, IL-6)、干扰素-γ(interferon-γ, IFN-γ)、干扰素-γ诱导蛋白-10(interferon-γ-inducible protein-10, IP-10)及单核细胞趋化蛋白-1(monocyte chemoattractant protein-1, MCP-1)释放。过度或失调的免疫激活导致组织损伤与多器官并发症。内皮损伤是重症COVID-19与汉坦病毒感染的关键病理特征,两者均涉及内皮激活与功能障碍,增加血管通透性、放大炎症、破坏凝血并促进多器官损伤。在汉坦病毒感染中,Gn与Gc糖蛋白与内皮细胞上的β-整合素受体相互作用,尽管感染的内皮细胞通常不被破坏,但其功能障碍导致血管渗漏,构成HFRS与HCPS的特征性表现。欧洲与亚洲汉坦病毒倾向靶向肾脏与肝脏,美洲汉坦病毒倾向靶向肺部。严重疾病似乎源于感染内皮细胞、血小板、补体、先天细胞因子、淋巴细胞及局部组织环境的复杂相互作用,而非直接病毒细胞致病效应。宿主遗传因素可影响易感性,如免疫相关基因(包括TLR2)罕见变异与重症COVID-19相关;性别差异亦影响结局。人类白细胞抗原(human leukocyte antigen, HLA)多态性与汉坦病毒感染易感性或保护相关。研究已鉴定出COVID-19与肾综合征出血热(HFRS)间32个共享基因,其中6个枢纽基因(RAD51、ALDH1A1、UBA52、CUL3、GADD45B、CDKN1A)被强调为可能参与共同病理生理机制的关键调控因子。 6 Clinical manifestations COVID-19与汉坦病毒感染初期均可表现为非特异性流感样症状,但在传播模式、临床病程及主要受累器官系统方面存在显著差异。COVID-19呼吸系统表现包括干咳或咳痰、呼吸困难、肺炎及急性呼吸窘迫综合征(acute respiratory distress syndrome, ARDS)。全身症状包括发热、乏力、虚弱、肌痛、嗅觉丧失、寒战以及味觉和/或嗅觉丧失。非呼吸系统表现涉及多个器官系统,包括胃肠、肝、胰、皮肤、肾、心脏、神经及眼部受累。约80%患者表现为轻至中度症状,约20%发展至重至危症。在危症中,急性肾损伤在入住重症监护病房(intensive care unit, ICU)的患者中更为常见。汉坦病毒感染早期症状常为非特异性,与流感、COVID-19、病毒性肺炎、钩端螺旋体病、登革热及脓毒症重叠,包括乏力、发热及肌肉酸痛。HFRS主要表现为肾脏损害与出血表现,从瘀点到严重内脏出血;HCPS主要表现为肺炎与心血管功能障碍。HFRS死亡率约12%,HCPS接近40%。近期ANDV疫情中,患者于2026年4月6日至28日发病,表现为发热、胃肠道症状,并快速进展至肺炎、ARDS与休克。研究表明,合并SARS-CoV-2感染的HFRS患者可能面临更严重疾病风险。 7 Diagnosis 确诊COVID-19的实验室方法包括核酸扩增检测(nucleic acid amplification tests, NAATs)、等温扩增技术、快速抗原检测及血清学检测。实时逆转录聚合酶链反应(real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, rRT-PCR)仍是SARS-CoV-2检测的“金标准”,因其具有高敏感性与特异性。基于抗原的快速诊断检测,如侧向流动免疫分析(lateral flow immunoassays, LFIs),被广泛用于快速筛查。汉坦病毒感染的实验室确诊主要依赖检测汉坦病毒特异性IgM抗体或证明IgG抗体滴度升高的血清学方法。分子技术如rRT-PCR亦用于病程急性期,尤其ANDV检测首选全血。两种感染的实验室诊断均存在局限性,分子方法需要专门设备、训练有素人员及适当样本采集处理。MV Hondius疫情应对进一步说明了对罕见人畜共患疾病建立灵活且可快速部署诊断网络的价值。汉坦病毒感染因非特异性症状使早期诊断尤为困难,因此详细的患者病史至关重要,需特别注意啮齿动物暴露、职业与环境危险因素、旅行史及与确诊病例接触史。已提出若干潜在预后标志物,包括血小板减少、血液浓缩、白细胞增多、乳酸升高、肾功能障碍、白介素-6(IL-6)、血管生成素信号改变及多种体液中病毒RNA检测,但大多数候选预测指标需在大规模多样化患者队列中验证。 8 Socio-economic impact COVID-19大流行对农业、石油工业、制造业、金融、旅游、交通运输、贸易、医疗保健及教育等多个部门产生负面影响。学校停课扰乱数百万学生的学习,行动限制与经济活动减少降低了对许多商品与制造产品的需求,而医疗设备、防护物资与医疗服务需求大幅增加。食品部门亦出现临时短缺与供应链中断。汉坦病毒感染缺乏全面经济负担估算,但重症病例常需重症监护病房(ICU)护理、高级呼吸支持,部分病例需体外膜氧合(extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, ECMO)。在偏远农村地区,急诊转运与转院进一步增加成本。MV Hondius疫情表明,即使罕见的人畜共患感染也可通过影响旅行信心与公众安全感知而产生国际社会经济后果。 9 Public health response 9.1 Epidemic intelligence 传统疫情监测主要依赖对结构化数据的手工分析,尤其通过官方公共卫生系统报告的信息,这些常规方法可受限于报告延迟、数据不完整及覆盖不足。人工智能(artificial intelligence, AI)驱动的监测系统能够整合分析多元、异质、多语言数据流,以支持更早检测与更及时公共卫生应对。WHO疫情枢纽旨在加强全球监测。学术机构是关键合作伙伴,在新冠疫情期间显著推进了分析与建模能力。SARS-CoV-2基因组的测序与比较分析揭示了病毒谱系的出现、循环与重组。然而,非洲大片区域代表性不足,主要归因于财务投资不足、训练人员短缺、实验室能力有限及数字基础设施与工具 inadequate。汉坦病毒疾病监测始于1993年美国Four Corners地区,HCPS于1995年成为全国法定报告疾病,此后通过国家法定报告疾病监测系统报告。在中国与韩国等高负担国家,常规监测系统地收集病例数据并监测啮齿动物种群。 9.2 Rapid communication strategy COVID-19大流行证明,识别并有效沟通公共卫生威胁是实施适当解决方案的首要关键步骤,但在科学证据有限或仍在涌现时,难以说服决策者。早期阶段,各国在建立一致连贯叙述以解释疾病流行病学、相关风险及预防措施方面面临重大挑战。有效的沟通对于培养公众对依赖广泛采用才能产生影响的卫生干预措施的信任与接受至关重要,COVID-19疫苗的推出因公众关于安全性与有效性的重大关切、错误信息快速传播而面临额外阻力。汉坦病毒疾病方面,WHO建立了三级协调机制。MV Hondius疫情中,WHO与佛得角、荷兰、南非、西班牙及英国的National IHR Focal Points保持持续协调。阿根廷National IHR Focal Point根据国籍分享乘客与船员名单,促进国际接触者追踪。 9.3 One health approach One Health框架认识到人类、动物、植物与环境健康之间的相互关联,旨在可持续地促进所有相互关联系统的福祉。四方组织制定了《One Health Joint Plan of Action (2022-2026)》。尽管ANDV疫情通过协调国际应对管理,包括流行病学调查、病例隔离与临床管理、医疗后送程序及广泛实验室分析,由卫生当局评估,疫情已于2026年7月2日得到控制,且WHO疾病暴发新闻DON611中无持续或大规模社区传播证据,但由于汉坦病毒感染潜伏期相对较长,担忧未来数周可能出现额外病例。啮齿动物控制是汉坦病毒预防的关键组成部分,措施包括环境改造、改善卫生、捕杀及针对性啮齿动物数量减少。 9.4 Ecosystem restoration 生态系统修复可被视为公共卫生干预。恢复生态系统可减少空气污染、改善绿色与蓝色空间获取可及性,并可能降低汉坦病毒风险。例如,将巴西大西洋森林恢复至法定要求水平可通过降低主要啮齿动物储主数量将汉坦病毒风险降低约45%。 9.5 Artificial Intelligence AI可增强疫情检测、疾病监测及诊断、药物与疫苗开发。AlphaFold等近期进展加速生物医学发现。AI驱动的疫情情报系统通过识别早期预警信号补充传统监测方法。机器学习模型已用于预测疾病传播与建模疫情。对于汉坦病毒,提出的HRP-AI框架采用多源预警模型,整合啮齿动物与环境监测数据、症候群监测、实验室结果、旅行与流动性指标、数字弱信号及商业脆弱性指标,旨在实现更早的疫情检测、风险分层与透明的风险沟通。AI在基因组分析、突变追踪、疫苗开发及大流行准备中亦发挥重要作用。 9.6 Therapeutics COVID-19疫情期间,若干既往获批用于其他适应症的制药药物被研究并重新用于SARS-CoV-2感染治疗,包括抗疟药、抗原虫药及一系列免疫调节疗法。小分子抗病毒药物如remdesivir、nirmatrelvir/ritonavir及molnupiravir已被使用。单克隆抗体在COVID-19治疗反应中发挥重要作用。目前尚无FDA批准的专门用于治疗汉坦病毒感染的药物,临床管理主要支持性治疗。HFRS治疗通常关注仔细的液体与电解质管理及肾脏替代治疗,包括必要时的透析。严重HCPS病例可能需要重症监护支持、机械通气及选择性ECMO。广谱核苷类似物ribavirin在体外与动物模型中显示抗ANDV活性,但临床证据有限。新兴免疫治疗策略代表有前景的途径,特别是针对Gn与Gc糖蛋白的中和单克隆抗体(monoclonal antibodies, mAbs)。然而,由于疾病进展理解不足、资金与商业兴趣有限及Gn/Gc糖蛋白复合物重组生产困难,汉坦病毒对策开发受到阻碍。 9.7 Vaccines 首批COVID-19疫苗产品于2020年年中引入,2020年7月22日开始紧急使用授权。截至2023年12月31日,全球已接种超136亿剂COVID-19疫苗,约67%全球人口完成初级接种。目前尚无广泛获批的专门用于治疗汉坦病毒疾病的疫苗。针对HTNV与SEOV的灭活疫苗于1980年代末在中国与韩国使用,例如Hantavax。这些疫苗诱导强烈初始免疫反应,但中和抗体在加强免疫一年后的检出率仅约50%。新兴的mRNA-脂质纳米粒(lipid nanoparticle, LNP)疫苗与病毒样颗粒(virus-like particle, VLP)疫苗代表有前景的新策略,可诱导高中和抗体反应并在动物攻击模型中提供完全保护。 9.8 Prevention COVID-19的预防包括正确佩戴口罩、定期洗手、遮挡咳嗽、避免触摸面部、保持身体距离及确保室内通风等。汉坦病毒疾病预防主要基于减少人类与啮齿动物储主之间的接触,包括保持家居与 workplace 清洁、封堵洞口、安全储存食物、受污染区域湿式清洁及手卫生。 10 Conclusion supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 16, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Review Identifies COVID-19 Insights to Strengthen Global Hantavirus Outbreak Preparedness by November 14, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 7 mins read 0 Review Identifies COVID-19 Insights to Strengthen Global Hantavirus Outbreak Preparedness Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A comprehensive comparative analysis published in Discover Public Health demonstrates that emerging hantavirus outbreaks and the global Coronavirus Disease 2019 pandemic share critical molecular, clinical, and immunopathological hallmarks despite exhibiting fundamentally divergent transmission dynamics and case fatality trajectories. Conducted by researchers Salma Madihi, Warda Baha, and Abdelouaheb Benani, the systematic investigation synthesizes evidence from major biomedical databases including PubMed and Google Scholar, alongside technical evaluations from the World Health Organization and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The review establishes that while both pathogens initiate profound systemic disease driven by microvascular damage and excessive immune activation, their public health footprints diverge significantly due to contrasting environmental reservoirs and modes of contagion. Zoonotic infections account for an estimated 2.7 million human deaths annually, highlighting an urgent need to translate the hard-won operational, diagnostic, and surveillance lessons acquired during the pandemic response into proactive countermeasures against neglected zoonoses that maintain persistent reservoirs in wildlife populations. The critical impetus for examining public health readiness arose following a maritime outbreak of Andes virus aboard the expedition cruise vessel MV Hondius, which departed Ushuaia, Argentina, on April 1, 2026, carrying 147 passengers and crew members across a South Atlantic itinerary. By May 4, 2026, health authorities had identified seven related cases, including two laboratory-confirmed infections, five suspected cases, and three early fatalities, presenting severe respiratory distress that required international coordination after Cabo Verde denied the ship docking permissions. Disembarkation was subsequently coordinated by the World Health Organization and Spanish authorities on the island of Tenerife in the Canary Islands, illustrating the intricate legal and jurisdictional barriers governing maritime quarantine protocols. By July 2, 2026, the cluster had expanded to thirteen total cases comprising twelve laboratory-confirmed infections and one probable case across Dutch, British, Spanish, German, Swiss, French, and Canadian nationals. Yielding an alarming case fatality rate of 23 percent, the incident demonstrated how modern international travel circuits can rapidly distribute rare pathogens carrying extended incubation periods across multijurisdictional boundaries. Virological comparisons reveal structural and genetic contrasts that govern how these enveloped RNA viruses interact with human hosts and adapt across ecological niches. Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 is classified within the family Coronaviridae and order Nidovirales as a single-stranded, positive-sense RNA virus possessing a genome that encodes four major structural proteins: envelope, membrane, nucleocapsid, and the surface spike glycoprotein. Host entry requires the spike protein to bind cellular angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 receptors before cleavage by host proteases, specifically TMPRSS2 and ADAM17, to facilitate cellular membrane fusion. In contrast, hantaviruses belong to the family Hantaviridae within the order Bunyavirales, maintaining a negative-sense, single-stranded RNA genome divided into three distinct segments: small, medium, and large. These viral segments encode the structural nucleoprotein, the surface envelope glycoproteins Gn and Gc, and the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. While coronaviruses evolve through rapid point mutations and frequent genetic recombination, hantaviruses maintain evolutionary diversity through genetic mutation, reassortment, and long-term co-divergence with specific small mammal reservoirs. Discover more COVID-19 Get Rapid Tests Read Med Journals Read Health News Check Symptoms Contrasting transmission biology heavily dictates the distinct public health containment strategies required for each infectious agent. Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 transmits efficiently between human hosts through respiratory droplets and microscopic aerosols expelled during breathing, speaking, singing, coughing, or sneezing, resulting in widespread airborne spread within crowded or poorly ventilated indoor spaces. Its brief incubation window, typically lasting between two and seven days, facilitated exponential community transmission that produced over 704 million confirmed cases and more than seven million deaths worldwide by April 2024. Conversely, hantaviruses are predominantly contracted through the inhalation of aerosolized excreta, saliva, or dust contaminated by infected rodents, generally lacking the capacity for sustained human-to-human transmission. Andes virus represents the notable exception, possessing documented capacity for secondary human transmission during intimate, prolonged contact within households or early prodromal periods, as observed during historical outbreaks in Argentina and Chile. Compounding contact tracing challenges, hantavirus incubation periods range from one to six weeks, with Andes virus displaying an incubation span of 7 to 39 days and a median of 18 days. At the cellular level, the investigation highlights that severe illness in both viral syndromes is anchored in extensive endothelial injury and dysregulated inflammatory cascades rather than unconstrained direct cellular cytopathicity. Pathogenic hantaviruses utilize surface glycoproteins Gn and Gc to attach to beta-integrin receptors on human endothelial cells without necessarily destroying the infected cellular architecture, yet their presence disrupts endothelial barrier integrity to induce profound vascular hyperpermeability. Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 produces comparable systemic microvascular damage, triggering glycocalyx shedding, coagulation abnormalities, and unrestrained cytokine release characterized by elevated interleukin-6, interferon-gamma, interferon-gamma-inducible protein-10, and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1. Bioinformatic evaluations identified 32 shared genes between Coronavirus Disease 2019 and hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, highlighting six central regulatory hub genes: RAD51, ALDH1A1, UBA52, CUL3, GADD45B, and CDKN1A. Concomitant clinical studies indicate that patients suffering from hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome who experience concurrent coronavirus infection face compounded clinical risks, demonstrating lengthened hospitalizations, more pronounced organ damage, and elevated overall mortality rates compared to patients experiencing monoinfection. Geographic and clinical expressions across global populations reflect the ecological diversity of their underlying animal reservoirs. Coronaviruses maintain broad natural reservoirs among bats, with ongoing investigations examining potential intermediate hosts, while demonstrating capacity for reverse zoonotic transmission into captive tigers, lions, hyenas, farmed mink, and wild deer. Hantaviruses, by contrast, exhibit tight evolutionary specialization alongside specific rodent hosts, dividing epidemiologically into Old World and New World lineages that generate between 10,000 and 100,000 human infections annually. Old World species, such as Hantaan virus carried by the striped field mouse Apodemus agrarius and Puumala virus hosted by the bank vole Myodes glareolus, cause hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome across Europe and Asia with case fatality rates ranging from under 1 percent to 15 percent. New World strains cause hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome across the Americas, where Sin Nombre virus, Bayou virus carried by the marsh rice rat Oryzomys palustris, Maripa virus, and Andes virus hosted by Oligoryzomys longicaudatus generate severe cardiopulmonary failure and shock, producing mortality rates reaching up to 50 percent. Diagnostic workflows illustrate another critical operational vulnerability where hantavirus management lags far behind the massive testing infrastructure deployed during the coronavirus pandemic. Coronavirus diagnostic services rely upon real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction assays as a gold standard within Biosafety Level 2 containment, supported by loop-mediated isothermal amplification platforms and widely distributed rapid antigen lateral flow immunoassays using nasopharyngeal swabs. Laboratory verification of hantavirus infection, however, remains predominantly dependent upon serological detection of specific immunoglobulin M antibodies or documented rises in immunoglobulin G titers, because acute-phase viremia is frequently fleeting. When molecular testing is conducted for Andes virus, whole blood or buffy coat specimens serve as optimal sample matrices due to distinct viral tropism for circulating mononuclear cells. Routine patient testing requires Biosafety Level 2 facilities, whereas viral culture, propagation, and handling of infectious animal tissues mandate strict Biosafety Level 3 precautions. Managing the MV Hondius cluster required the World Health Organization to coordinate rapid shipment of diagnostic kits from Argentina to five countries, with testing conducted at specialized reference facilities in South Africa and Senegal. The comparative review delineates sharp disparities regarding clinical therapeutics and licensed countermeasure pipelines across both diseases. The pandemic response stimulated rapid repurposing and clinical licensing of small-molecule antivirals, including remdesivir, molnupiravir, and nirmatrelvir boosted with ritonavir, alongside convalescent plasma and recombinant monoclonal antibodies targeting the viral spike protein. In contrast, no antiviral agents have received Food and Drug Administration approval specifically indicated for hantavirus infections, leaving clinical management almost entirely supportive. Patients suffering from severe hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome require precise fluid and electrolyte monitoring combined with renal replacement therapy or dialysis, whereas severe hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome demands intensive mechanical ventilation and early extracorporeal membrane oxygenation rescue. The broad-spectrum nucleoside analogue ribavirin demonstrates in vitro and Syrian hamster model efficacy against Andes virus and offers partial clinical benefits in renal syndrome, yet human trials show no therapeutic benefit in cardiopulmonary disease. Preclinical investigations evaluating favipiravir and neutralizing monoclonal antibodies targeting Gn and Gc glycoproteins, including JL16 and SAB-163, show experimental promise but face structural instability hurdles during recombinant protein production. Disparities in preventative immunization further accentuate global vulnerability to emerging rodent-borne pathogens. The coronavirus pandemic catalyzed the development and global administration of over 13.6 billion vaccine doses by December 2023, utilizing mRNA-lipid nanoparticle formulations, adenoviral vectors, protein subunits, and inactivated platforms to achieve complete primary series coverage across approximately 67 percent of the human population. Conversely, no globally standardized or widely authorized vaccine exists for hantavirus prevention. Formalin-inactivated vaccines derived from suckling mouse brain tissue, notably Hantavax targeting Hantaan and Seoul viruses, have been deployed in South Korea and China since the late 1980s, achieving 97 percent seroconversion one month after booster administration; however, neutralizing antibody titers decline to approximately 50 percent after one year without demonstrating statistically significant reductions in clinical disease severity. Advanced preclinical research is currently evaluating next-generation nucleic acid platforms, including mRNA-lipid nanoparticles encoding Andes virus glycoproteins and virus-like particles displaying intact Gn and Gc proteins, which have induced complete protection and high neutralizing antibody responses in rodent challenge models, demonstrating that modern platform technologies can be adapted for neglected viral threats. Mitigating future zoonotic spillovers requires transitioning from reactive outbreak containment to predictive epidemic intelligence embedded within a comprehensive One Health framework. Environmental disturbances, including deforestation, agricultural expansion, and climate anomalies like historic El Niño events in the southwestern United States, repeatedly drive dramatic fluctuations in rodent reservoir densities that precede human infection spikes. Ecological restoration provides a direct public health defense; for example, reforesting Brazil’s Atlantic Forest to statutory mandates could reduce hantavirus spillover risk by approximately 45 percent by reducing densities of generalist reservoir species such as Oligoryzomys nigripes and Necromys lasiurus. Concurrently, epidemic surveillance must incorporate artificial intelligence architectures, such as the proposed Hantavirus Risk Prediction Artificial Intelligence framework, which merges syndromic tracking, climate metrics, rodent population surveys, and cross-border mobility data to identify subtle pre-outbreak signals. Coupled with international genomic monitoring networks pioneered during the pandemic, proactive One Health coordination offers the essential architecture to detect, characterize, and contain virulent zoonotic pathogens before localized transmissions expand across vulnerable global populations. (2026). Learning from COVID-19 to strengthen hantavirus preparedness and public health response. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 16, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Intramuscular Sotrovimab Matches Intravenous Viral Clearance in Early COVID-19 Trial by November 14, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 7 mins read 0 Intramuscular Sotrovimab Matches Intravenous Viral Clearance in Early COVID-19 Trial Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A multicenter randomized clinical trial has established that intramuscular administration of the monoclonal antibody sotrovimab achieves virologic equivalence to intravenous infusion in reducing respiratory severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 viral load among adults with early, mild-to-moderate coronavirus disease 2019. Investigating alternative administration pathways for neutralizing antibodies during epidemic surges, the COMET-PEAK study evaluated whether injecting sotrovimab directly into skeletal muscle tissue could replicate the virologic performance of standard intravenous infusions without compromising patient tolerability. The trial confirmed that both a 500-milligram and an exploratory 250-milligram intramuscular dose met rigorous statistical equivalence thresholds when compared directly against the established 500-milligram intravenous delivery route, as measured by nasopharyngeal viral exposure across the first eight days of therapy. Intramuscular delivery was accompanied by a low incidence of mild, transient local injection-site symptoms and showed no emergence of treatment-related serious adverse events. However, because prior phase three investigations demonstrated that the lower 250-milligram intramuscular dose failed to match intravenous clinical efficacy in preventing disease progression, these virologic findings provide critical empirical evidence that upper respiratory viral clearance does not reliably predict clinical protection against hospitalization. Sotrovimab is an engineered human immunoglobulin G1 kappa monoclonal antibody derived from the parental antibody S309, designed to bind a highly conserved epitope within the receptor-binding domain of the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 spike protein. The therapeutic antibody demonstrated significant clinical benefit in the pivotal phase three COMET-ICE trial, where a 500-milligram intravenous infusion produced a statistically significant 79 percent relative risk reduction compared with placebo against hospitalization lasting longer than 24 hours or death from any cause. This initial evidence supported intravenous authorization across international regulatory bodies, including marketing authorization from the European Medicines Agency in December 2021 and Emergency Use Authorization from the United States Food and Drug Administration in May 2021 for non-hospitalized individuals at elevated risk of progression. Although the United States authorization was suspended in April 2022 and subsequently revoked in December 2024 following the widespread emergence of the Omicron BA.2 variant, the logistical challenges of administering intravenous infusions during community transmission surges highlighted an urgent clinical need to evaluate intramuscular delivery options. In the parallel COMET-TAIL non-inferiority study, 500 milligrams delivered intramuscularly proved non-inferior to intravenous infusion for preventing disease progression, whereas a reduced 250-milligram intramuscular arm was terminated early due to excess hospitalizations. The COMET-PEAK investigation was executed across 37 investigative centers situated in the United States, Spain, Canada, and South Korea as a randomized, parallel-group, three-part trial registered under clinical identifier NCT04779879. The initial segment, Part A, utilized a double-blind design to compare two distinct manufacturing iterations of sotrovimab administered intravenously, contrasting the generation one material derived from stably transfected non-clonal cell pools with the commercially intended generation two product manufactured from a clonally derived cell bank. Parts B and C functioned as open-label, active-comparator phases dedicated to evaluating the generation two antibody delivered through divergent administration routes and dosing tiers. Part B centrally randomized non-hospitalized adult participants in a one-to-one ratio to receive either a single 500-milligram intravenous infusion or a single 500-milligram intramuscular injection split evenly across two separate four-milliliter injections into opposing dorsogluteal muscles. Part C subsequently randomized participants in an equivalent one-to-one ratio to receive either the standard 500-milligram intravenous infusion or a lower 250-milligram intramuscular dose administered as either a single four-milliliter gluteal injection or two two-milliliter injections partitioned across bilateral deltoid muscles, incorporating prospective stratification based on prior receipt of authorized or approved vaccines. Discover more Compare Clinics Save on Rx Track Biotech Get Rapid Tests COVID-19 Enrollment across the trial captured non-hospitalized individuals aged 18 to 69 years in Part B, 18 to 71 years in Part C, and 18 to 65 years in Part A, with a minimum age threshold of 19 years enforced at South Korean clinical sites. Prospective participants met eligibility criteria by documenting symptomatic illness within seven days of symptom onset, possessing an oxygen saturation of at least 94 percent while breathing room ambient air, and verifying infection through a positive validated molecular diagnostic test. Protocol exclusions barred individuals requiring immediate hospitalization, presenting severe respiratory distress or resting dyspnea, exhibiting advanced immunocompromising conditions, or presenting bleeding disorders and thrombocytopenia that contraindicated deep intramuscular injections. While Parts A and B strictly excluded individuals who had received an authorized or approved vaccine against coronavirus disease 2019, Part C accommodated vaccinated volunteers to reflect changing vaccination coverage during the pandemic. Among the randomized safety population, which totaled 166 individuals in Part B and 157 in Part C, median participant ages ranged between 42 and 47 years across cohorts. Approximately 50 percent of all enrolled subjects presented at least one documented baseline medical comorbidity associated with severe disease progression, predominantly obesity defined by a body mass index exceeding 30 kilograms per square meter and age of 55 years or older. The designated primary objective across Parts B and C focused on establishing virologic equivalence between intramuscular and intravenous sotrovimab, quantifying the area under the viral load curve from day one through day eight using serial nasopharyngeal swab specimens analyzed via quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction at a centralized laboratory. Prespecified statistical criteria established that therapeutic equivalence was achieved if the 90 percent confidence interval for the geometric mean ratio of viral load area under the curve remained entirely within the pharmacologic equivalence boundary of 0.5 to 2.0. Analysis of covariance adjusted for baseline viral load and prior vaccination status confirmed that Part B yielded an adjusted geometric mean ratio of 1.04 for 500 milligrams intramuscular versus intravenous administration, with a tight 90 percent confidence interval spanning from 0.98 to 1.09. Similarly, Part C demonstrated an adjusted geometric mean ratio of 1.02 for the reduced 250-milligram intramuscular dose compared against 500 milligrams intravenous infusion, generating a 90 percent confidence interval spanning from 0.94 to 1.11. Both experimental intramuscular regimens therefore successfully satisfied the primary equivalence hypothesis, while concurrently remaining within far stricter bounds of 0.85 to 1.20. Analysis of secondary virologic endpoints reinforced the primary geometric mean comparisons across extended temporal windows of infection. Prespecified secondary assessments examining the mean log-transformed area under the curve from day one through day five and from day one through day eleven demonstrated parallel reductions in respiratory viral burden between the intramuscular and intravenous cohorts across both trial parts. Serial quantification of log10 copies per milliliter documented steady viral clearance from baseline through the entire 29-day follow-up duration across all randomized treatment arms. Mean viral load trajectories overlapped closely between the 500-milligram intravenous infusion and the 500-milligram intramuscular injection groups throughout Part B, and identical parallel clearance kinetics characterized the comparison between the 500-milligram intravenous and 250-milligram intramuscular cohorts in Part C. By day 29, the vast majority of treated individuals in all study arms exhibited respiratory viral levels that declined beneath established lower limits of laboratory detection. Furthermore, intrasubject variability in viral shedding, assessed through the coefficient of variation surrounding geometric mean area under the curve metrics, exhibited comparable stability across the different routes of administration and dosage levels throughout the acute follow-up period. Pharmacokinetic evaluations demonstrated expected physiological distinctions in systemic drug bioavailability, absorption timing, and overall systemic exposure between direct vascular infusion and extravascular intramuscular injection. Total systemic drug exposure across the initial 29 days, calculated as the area under the serum concentration-time curve, reached a mean of 1407.6 day micrograms per milliliter following a single 500-milligram intravenous infusion. In contrast, the identical 500-milligram dose delivered via intramuscular gluteal injection generated an exposure of 671.3 day micrograms per milliliter, demonstrating approximately half the systemic bioavailability of the intravenous infusion over the same monthly interval. The exploratory 250-milligram intramuscular dose delivered a proportionally reduced mean exposure of 380.8 day micrograms per milliliter, representing roughly half the drug exposure achieved by the 500-milligram intramuscular injection. Peak circulating drug concentrations diverged substantially by delivery route, as intravenous delivery produced immediate mean maximum concentrations of approximately 140 micrograms per milliliter at the conclusion of the 15-minute infusion. Intramuscular absorption was considerably prolonged, producing a mean maximum serum concentration of 28.2 micrograms per milliliter reached at a median time of 6.9 days for the 500-milligram dose, and 11.4 micrograms per milliliter at a median time of 14 days for the 250-milligram dose. Comprehensive safety monitoring demonstrated that intramuscular sotrovimab was well tolerated without the appearance of novel or unexpected safety signals. The most frequent adverse events linked to intramuscular delivery were localized injection-site reactions, all classified as mild Grade 1 events that resolved rapidly without therapeutic intervention. In the 500-milligram intramuscular cohort of Part B, ten participants experienced mild local reactions, with eight individuals developing localized symptoms within one hour post-injection that resolved fully by the two-hour clinical assessment, while two participants experienced reactions on day one. In Part C, four individuals receiving 250 milligrams intramuscularly developed Grade 1 injection-site reactions, equally divided between gluteal and deltoid administration sites. Overall rates of treatment-related adverse events remained low across the trial, documented in 13 percent of the 500-milligram intramuscular cohort, two percent of the Part B intravenous cohort, five percent of the 250-milligram intramuscular cohort, and zero percent of the Part C intravenous cohort, consisting mostly of transient injection-site pain, local nodules, discomfort, and mild urticaria. Severe adverse events related to coronavirus disease 2019 occurred in seven participants overall across follow-up, culminating in one death from viral pneumonia in the 250-milligram intramuscular arm, though investigators concluded none of the serious events were related to sotrovimab administration. Genomic resistance surveillance conducted via deep next-generation sequencing of the viral spike gene evaluated the selective pressure exerted by sotrovimab across study arms. Among 222 treated participants with paired baseline and post-baseline sequencing data available, 152 individuals exhibited treatment-emergent amino acid substitutions within the spike protein, with 27 participants carrying substitutions located directly within the sotrovimab epitope. Epitope substitution frequencies did not reflect increased selection pressure under intramuscular delivery, occurring in seven percent of participants receiving 500 milligrams intramuscularly compared to 15 percent receiving 500 milligrams intravenously in Part B, and 15 percent receiving 250 milligrams intramuscularly compared to 12 percent receiving 500 milligrams intravenously in Part C. The most prevalent treatment-emergent substitution was E340K, identified in 15 subjects, while substitutions documented in cell culture to confer reduced in-vitro neutralization susceptibility—specifically P337L, E340A, E340K, and E340V—appeared in 20 participants. Importantly, none of the seven hospitalized trial participants possessed treatment-emergent epitope substitutions, and individuals harboring resistance mutations cleared respiratory virus successfully, illustrating the unclear clinical impact of localized in-vitro resistance mutations during resolving acute disease. The study authors highlighted several methodological limitations that temper the clinical interpretation of the COMET-PEAK findings, notably the absence of an untreated control group to distinguish antibody-mediated viral clearance from the natural clearance kinetics of acute infection. Furthermore, trial enrollment coincided with major shifts in circulating viral variants of concern, progressing from predominant Alpha transmission during Parts A and B to Delta dominance throughout Part C. Crucially, the finding that 250 milligrams of intramuscular sotrovimab achieved complete virologic equivalence to 500 milligrams of intravenous infusion despite the lower dose producing excess clinical hospitalizations in COMET-TAIL indicates that upper respiratory viral load reduction is an inadequate surrogate biomarker for preventing severe clinical progression. This observation aligns directly with regulatory guidance from the United States Food and Drug Administration indicating that virologic biomarkers are unsuited as primary registrational endpoints for phase three clinical efficacy trials. While the COMET-PEAK data confirm that concentrated intramuscular antibody delivery into gluteal or deltoid musculature is feasible, pharmacokinetically predictable, and clinically well tolerated, future therapeutic programs cannot rely solely on respiratory viral dynamics to establish optimal clinical dosing regimens. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 16, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Biology Circulating Cholesterol Fuels SARS-CoV-2 Replication Through Viral ORF3a Receptor Stabilization by November 14, 2026 in Biology Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Circulating Cholesterol Fuels SARS-CoV-2 Replication Through Viral ORF3a Receptor Stabilization Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram SARS-CoV-2 exploits extracellular low-density lipoprotein to accelerate viral ribonucleic acid replication within infected host tissues, operating through the viral accessory protein ORF3a. In cell culture systems, human airway organoid models, and small animal infection studies, researchers established that circulating cholesterol directly stimulates viral genome synthesis rather than viral attachment, entry, or structural assembly. The investigation demonstrated that elevated levels of low-density lipoprotein, commonly referred to as bad cholesterol, provide essential lipids that the pathogen repurposes to construct specialized intracellular replication organelles. While previous epidemiological observations noted that individuals with pre-existing metabolic conditions suffered significantly worse disease trajectories, the molecular mechanisms connecting circulating lipoproteins to viral replication efficiency had remained largely unexplained. By tracing the cellular uptake of labeled cholesterol particles and tracking viral double-stranded ribonucleic acid accumulation, the investigators showed that extracellular cholesterol availability directly dictates the speed and magnitude of coronaviral genomic replication across human airway cells. Metabolic comorbidities such as advanced age, obesity, and type 2 diabetes have consistently correlated with severe COVID-19 manifestations and increased patient mortality throughout the global pandemic. Prior clinical reports documented that patients receiving statin therapy to lower circulating low-density lipoprotein exhibited milder disease progressions, whereas individuals possessing the apolipoprotein E4 genetic variant, which elevates circulating low-density lipoprotein concentrations, suffered heightened morbidity. Additionally, clinical evaluations of fenofibrate, a therapeutic agent that stimulates lipoprotein lipase activity, reported reduced intracellular lipid accumulation and improved survival among infected individuals. Animal experiments utilizing diet-induced obesity in rodents similarly corroborated the pathological contribution of circulating lipids to coronavirus pathogenesis. However, whether extracellular lipoproteins actively participated in biochemical events within infected cells remained an unresolved question. Because respiratory tissues rely on circulating lipoprotein complexes to supply approximately eighty percent of their cellular cholesterol requirements, researchers hypothesized that host cholesterol scavenging pathways might directly nourish the replicative cycle of SARS-CoV-2. To evaluate how specific extracellular lipids influence infection dynamics, the research team exposed cultured human lung cells and organoids to purified lipid fractions prior to viral inoculation. Experiments utilizing A549 lung carcinoma cells overexpressing the human ACE2 receptor and primary human airway organoids revealed that low-density lipoprotein supplementation significantly elevated viral ribonucleic acid synthesis. Quantifying viral nucleocapsid and envelope genes via reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction confirmed elevated intracellular viral transcripts. Furthermore, low-density lipoprotein and very low-density lipoprotein treatments expanded the proportion of infected cells displaying double-stranded viral ribonucleic acid, whereas high-density lipoprotein or oleic acid supplementation produced no measurable enhancement. Because oleic acid stimulated triglyceride synthesis without driving infection, and high-density lipoprotein operates primarily in cholesterol efflux rather than massive import, the authors deduced that targeted cholesterol internalization was specifically required. Pharmacological inhibition of PCSK9 using the small molecule (R)-IMPP increased low-density lipoprotein receptor abundance, which subsequently amplified viral infection rates in treated cellular cultures. Discover more Cholesterol cholesterol Lower Cholesterol Meet Dietitians Get Rapid Tests To pinpoint the exact phase of the viral lifecycle supported by cholesterol, the scientists deployed several specialized subgenomic model systems. First, pseudotyped lentiviral particles displaying the SARS-CoV-2 spike glycoprotein and carrying luciferase reporter genes were used to isolate viral entry mechanisms. Adding low-density lipoprotein failed to alter luciferase signal in target cells expressing ACE2 alone or cells co-expressing ACE2 and the transmembrane serine protease TMPRSS2, indicating that cholesterol does not directly facilitate receptor-mediated viral entry. Next, virus-like particles containing all viral structural proteins were utilized to assess viral assembly and egress; low-density lipoprotein treatment again produced no measurable change in particle generation or luciferase transfer. In sharp contrast, single-round replicon systems lacking the envelope gene and harboring a secreted nanoluciferase reporter demonstrated substantial luminescence increases following low-density lipoprotein administration. These replicon findings established that the primary benefit of extracellular cholesterol occurs downstream of entry during intracellular genomic replication. Microscopic examinations confirmed that extracellular cholesterol actively fuels the physical assembly of intracellular replication complexes. Staining experiments demonstrated that replicon-bearing cells treated with low-density lipoprotein developed significantly larger double-stranded ribonucleic acid foci and higher overall viral transcript levels. When investigators exposed lung cells to infectious virus for one hour, washed away unattached virions, and then introduced low-density lipoprotein, viral replication surged three-fold for the ancestral WA1 strain and four-fold for the Beta variant over seventy-two hours. Correlative light and electron microscopy of infected Vero cells further illuminated dramatic ultrastructural reorganizations occurring within host cytoplasm. Cells cultured in the presence of low-density lipoprotein displayed an elevated abundance and packing density of double-membrane vesicles, which serve as protective membrane hubs for viral replication, alongside numerous open double-membrane spherules. To identify which viral component orchestrates this lipid scavenging program, the researchers systematically screened individual viral proteins expressed within human lung cells. Using fluorescent DiI-labeled low-density lipoprotein to quantify particle uptake, they found that authentic viral infection increased cellular low-density lipoprotein uptake by approximately twenty percent. Strikingly, expressing the accessory protein ORF3a alone increased particle internalization by more than thirty percent relative to empty vector controls. Other viral proteins, including non-structural proteins NSP1, NSP2, NSP6, and NSP12, significantly suppressed lipoprotein uptake, highlighting that ORF3a exerts a dominant activating role during authentic infection. Lipid profiling via thin-layer chromatography corroborated that infected cells accumulated substantial stores of cholesterol esters, the principal intracellular storage format for imported cholesterol. Quantitative polymerase chain reaction further verified that infection upregulated critical host uptake factors, including the low-density lipoprotein receptor and NPC1, illustrating that the virus systematically drives cellular machinery to replenish intracellular cholesterol reserves. Mechanistic investigations revealed that ORF3a directly interacts with and stabilizes the host low-density lipoprotein receptor within intracellular endosomes. Confocal microscopy demonstrated that FLAG-tagged ORF3a co-localized extensively with green fluorescent protein-tagged low-density lipoprotein receptors in cultured cells, while co-immunoprecipitation confirmed their physical association. Notably, ORF3a expression led to the preferential enrichment of higher molecular weight bands representing mature receptors rather than newly synthesized precursors located in the endoplasmic reticulum. By binding to mature receptors within endosomes, ORF3a hindered the association between the receptor and PCSK9, a regulatory chaperone that normally triggers receptor breakdown within lysosomes. Cycloheximide chase experiments confirmed that ORF3a expression prolonged receptor half-life in host cells. Flow cytometry showed that surface receptor presentation and recycling via CCC and WASH protein complexes remained intact. CRISPR-Cas9 knockouts targeting the low-density lipoprotein receptor, NPC1, or NPC2 severely impaired viral infection, proving that intact host cholesterol uptake machinery is vital for the viral cycle. To validate whether ORF3a drives cholesterol-dependent pathogenesis in living organisms, the researchers conducted in vivo infection experiments using Golden Syrian hamsters. Male hamsters were preconditioned for two weeks on either a standard laboratory rodent chow or a high-cholesterol diet formulated with fifteen percent lard and zero-point-five percent cholesterol. Animals were then intranasally inoculated with ancestral WA1 virus or an engineered mutant possessing a premature stop codon at the initial amino acid position of ORF3a, designated ORF3a-STOP. In hamsters infected with the ancestral strain, consuming a high-cholesterol diet produced a statistically significant increase in infectious virion titers and elevated nucleocapsid antigen staining across lung tissues. In marked contrast, hamsters infected with the ORF3a-STOP mutant displayed no increase in viral titers or lung tissue pathology when fed the high-cholesterol diet. The investigation further unraveled an evolutionary divergence between viral lineages, explaining why the Beta variant responded with the strongest replication enhancement upon low-density lipoprotein exposure. The Beta genome carries two specific point mutations in ORF3a: Q57H and S171L. While ancestral ORF3a binds host VPS39, a component of the HOPS tethering complex, affinity purification mass spectrometry and co-immunoprecipitation demonstrated that the S171L mutation markedly abrogates this interaction. Ancestral ORF3a deacidifies endosomes through its VPS39 interaction, inadvertently impairing acid-dependent cholesterol ester hydrolysis from internalized particles. Conversely, Beta ORF3a maintains endosomal acidification, as demonstrated by elevated fluorescence in LDL-pHrodo Red live imaging assays. By preserving luminal acidification while continuing to stabilize the low-density lipoprotein receptor, Beta ORF3a optimizes both particle endocytosis and subsequent enzymatic cholesterol liberation. Stable expression of Beta ORF3a or the single S171L mutant in Calu-3 cells rescued replication of the ORF3a-STOP virus to a substantially greater extent than ancestral ORF3a. In contrast to the Beta lineage, the Omicron variant exhibited diminished sensitivity to extracellular low-density lipoprotein, aligning with its altered clinical profile. Genomic sequencing shows that Omicron BA.1 carries ancestral-like ORF3a sequences lacking the Beta mutations, while earlier studies documented that Omicron expresses lower overall levels of ORF3a messenger RNA and protein. Although these findings explain why hypercholesterolemic hosts faced heightened disease severity during ancestral and Beta variant waves, several mechanistic questions remain open. The authors emphasized that several viral proteins, including NSP3, NSP9, NSP11, NSP16, and ORF7a, have not yet been evaluated for their individual effects on host lipid uptake. Furthermore, while the study establishes a direct biochemical link between circulating cholesterol, receptor stabilization, and double-membrane vesicle formation, translating these cell and animal findings into human antiviral therapies requires targeted clinical investigation before specific cholesterol-modulating protocols can be validated. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 16, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health COVID-19 Antibodies Did Not Affect Denosumab Biosimilar Immunogenicity in Clinical Trial by November 14, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 5 mins read 0 COVID-19 Antibodies Did Not Affect Denosumab Biosimilar Immunogenicity in Clinical Trial Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram During the COVID-19 pandemic, drug developers and regulatory authorities faced widespread uncertainty regarding whether adaptive immune responses provoked by natural severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection or newly introduced vaccines might interfere with clinical trial endpoints, particularly the immunogenicity profiles of therapeutic biologics. In an exploratory evaluation conducted within a clinical trial supporting the approval of GP2411—a biosimilar candidate to reference denosumab—investigators implemented a dedicated serology testing framework to monitor anti-SARS-CoV-2 immunoglobulin G (IgG) responses among healthy volunteers. The research demonstrated that the development of anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG antibodies, whether acquired through natural viral exposure or vaccination, exerted no clinically meaningful impact on the incidence, persistence, or magnitude of anti-drug antibodies directed against the denosumab biosimilar. The underlying clinical trial was conducted in Germany between 2020 and 2022 and enrolled healthy male participants aged 28 to 65 years who received a single dose of denosumab administered as GP2411 or reference Xgeva. Denosumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody engineered to bind receptor activator of nuclear factor-kappa B ligand (RANKL), thereby preventing activation of its receptor RANK on the surface of osteoclasts and suppressing osteoclastic bone resorption. Because therapeutic proteins carry an inherent potential to stimulate an unwanted immune response in recipients, assessing anti-drug antibodies (ADAs) served as a primary secondary endpoint in the trial. To resolve potential confounding factors arising from widespread pandemic exposure, the research team instituted an exploratory serological testing program to evaluate whether immune activation against SARS-CoV-2 could heighten immunogenic sensitivity or cross-react with the biotherapeutic. To evaluate participant serology systematically, the researchers selected and partially validated a commercially available qualitative enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) test kit, the SCoV-2 Detect SARS-CoV-2 IgG ELISA developed by InBios International, which held Emergency Use Authorization from the US Food and Drug Administration. This indirect ELISA incorporates the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein as an immobilized capture antigen to detect human IgG antibodies targeting viral epitopes. Initial pre-validation experiments conducted in-house verified the assay’s operational characteristics across a panel of diverse human serum specimens. The kit correctly identified all negative control sera obtained from healthy donors prior to the 2019 outbreak, achieving a confirmed baseline specificity of 100 percent across six unexposed samples, including hemolytic and lipemic controls. Discover more Track Biotech Save on Rx Study Biology Find Treatments In sensitivity testing across different cohorts, the assay detected anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG in 92 percent of hospitalized symptomatic donors evaluated at least 14 days after confirmation by polymerase chain reaction. These hospitalized patients exhibited robust antibody reactivity, yielding immunological status ratio (ISR) values that ranged predominantly between 12.3 and 16.6. When applied to vaccinated individuals, the assay demonstrated 100 percent sensitivity across six serum samples, displaying ISR values between 1.8 and 8.4. Conversely, in non-hospitalized donors with confirmed asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infections, the assay identified anti-spike IgG in 57 percent of individuals; retrospective records confirmed that the three non-reactive donors were negative for IgG while testing positive for anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgM responses, reflecting earlier-stage humoral adaptation. A pivotal bioanalytical innovation within the study was the formal validation of singlicate sample analysis alongside traditional duplicate testing. Historically, ligand binding assays have relied on duplicate measurements to compensate for potential analytical variance, yet processing clinical samples as singlicates presents opportunities to conserve biological matrix and accelerate high-throughput screening while maintaining compliance with bioanalytical standards. Using freshly prepared validation samples diluted from a verified SARS-CoV-2-positive human serum pool into unexposed healthy volunteer serum, the investigators assessed assay selectivity, precision, and tolerance. Under predefined acceptance criteria requiring a coefficient of variation of 20 percent or lower, singlicate analysis achieved intra-assay precision values ranging from 5 to 11 percent, compared to 3 to 4 percent for duplicates, while inter-assay precision ranged from 8 to 16 percent for singlicates and 8 to 14 percent for duplicates. Discover more Find Vaccines Donate to Research Read Med Journals The validation protocol also examined whether the presence of circulating denosumab or anti-drug antibodies could interfere with the qualitative detection of anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG antibodies, causing false-positive or false-negative readings. The assay established identical drug tolerance and ADA tolerance thresholds under both singlicate and duplicate evaluation formats, verifying that therapeutic drug concentrations and host antibodies against the monoclonal therapy did not impede accurate serological assessment. To safeguard against borderline ambiguity in routine singlicate execution, a re-analysis algorithm was implemented: any singlicate specimen producing an ISR value between 0.9 and 1.1 was automatically re-tested in duplicate to establish a definitive result. In the subsequent analysis of 1970 clinical study samples, only 24 samples (approximately 1 percent) fell within this equivocal re-analysis window. Serological monitoring across the trial cohort tracked 499 healthy male volunteers over four sequential sampling visits spanning baseline, day 85, day 169, and the formal conclusion of the study. Overall, anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG antibodies were detected in 1165 serum samples, establishing an overall study seroprevalence of 82 percent among the trial population. The assay identified viral antibodies in all 55 participants who reported a confirmed COVID-19 infection during the trial. Furthermore, among 325 participants who received an authorized COVID-19 vaccine at least 14 days before sampling, 321 individuals (99 percent) exhibited detectable anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG responses in at least one post-vaccination specimen, aligning with established rates of vaccine seroconversion. At the individual specimen level, 863 serum samples were obtained from participants who either had a verified COVID-19 infection, had completed vaccination at least two weeks prior, or experienced both events. The validated ELISA detected anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG in 835 of these 863 samples, achieving a clinical detection rate of 97 percent. Among the 28 samples lacking detectable IgG, most had been collected shortly after the initial vaccine dose. For the 835 reactive samples, ISR measurements ranged from 1.1 to 7.4, demonstrating comparable overall antibody levels between vaccinated individuals and those with confirmed clinical infection; median ISR values were recorded at 5.8 for vaccinated participants and 6.3 for those with confirmed natural infection. Concurrently, the trial rigorously evaluated the secondary immunogenicity endpoint of the denosumab biosimilar using a drug-tolerant electrochemiluminescence bridging assay sensitive down to 6 nanograms per milliliter in neat serum. Across 6408 clinical serum samples drawn from the 499 dosed participants, 319 individuals (64 percent) tested positive for anti-drug antibodies at some point during follow-up. Crucially, all confirmed ADA-positive samples exhibited very low antibody concentrations, remaining below the formal titer reporting threshold of 20 nanograms per milliliter. Furthermore, anti-drug antibody reactivity proved transient across virtually all participants, with persistent ADAs observed in only three subjects whose seroconversion timing showed no consistent relationship with viral antibody exposure. Neutralizing anti-drug antibodies capable of inhibiting the therapeutic activity of denosumab were extraordinarily rare throughout the trial, appearing in only four serum samples collected from three participants. When cross-referenced against concurrent COVID-19 serology results, neutralizing anti-drug antibody findings displayed no link to SARS-CoV-2 immunity: two neutralizing samples coincided with negative anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG readings, while one matched a positive viral serology result. These findings collectively demonstrated that systemic immune activation provoked by COVID-19 infection or spike-directed vaccination did not augment anti-denosumab antibody titers, alter ADA persistence, or elevate the incidence of neutralizing antibodies, validating the biosimilar’s predictable immunogenicity profile during global pandemic conditions. The study authors highlighted several methodological boundaries, noting that because the authorized ELISA relied exclusively on the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, the assay could not distinguish between vaccination-induced antibodies and responses elicited by natural viral infection. In addition, acute infections during the trial were captured via self-reported outside diagnostic testing rather than scheduled in-trial diagnostic swabs, precluding a formal calculation of in-study diagnostic specificity. Nevertheless, the successful deployment of singlicate bioanalytical screening proved robust, demonstrating that efficient, low-volume serology strategies can effectively isolate confounding pandemic variables and support regulatory compliance in clinical trials of biotherapeutic candidates. (2025). Evaluation of Anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG Responses in a Clinical Study of a Biosimilar Candidate to Denosumab Using Singlicate Analysis. supplementary_news.content: web statistics Sections Malaysia Business World Opinion Sports & Fitness Culture & Lifestyle Podcast Education Videos Gallery About The Team Contact Us Advertising Privacy Policy Terms of Use About Us Get the app Follow us on Health WHO urges testing as new COVID-19 variant PJ.2.1 mimics flu, common cold symptoms Emerging variant detected across several continents, with reports of severe sore throat and prolonged fatigue raising health concerns Updated 5 days ago · Published on 10 Nov 2026 2:43PM Shares The warning comes as the SARS-CoV-2 lineage, first identified in Ontario, Canada, in May 2026, has been detected across parts of Asia - November 10, 2026 THE World Health Organisation (WHO) has urged continued diagnostic testing as a newly emerging COVID-19 variant, PJ.2.1, spreads internationally with symptoms that can be mistaken for influenza or the common cold. The warning comes as the SARS-CoV-2 lineage, first identified in Ontario, Canada, in May 2026, has been detected across North America, Europe, Australia, New Zealand and parts of Asia. WHO said symptoms alone were insufficient to reliably distinguish PJ.2.1 infections from other respiratory illnesses, stressing that diagnostic testing remained the most accurate way to identify the virus. This is particularly important when confirmation of an infection could affect treatment decisions or public health measures. The organisation said it was closely monitoring the variant amid concerns over its growing geographical spread. Preliminary research published in the Journal of Infection suggests PJ.2.1 may have a growth advantage through increased binding to the ACE2 receptor, which enables the coronavirus to enter human cells, rather than through a substantial ability to evade vaccine-induced antibodies. The variant carries multiple mutations in its spike protein, the structure responsible for facilitating infection. Meanwhile, Russian infectious disease specialist and virologist Elena Malinnikova said infections involving PJ.2.1 could cause severe sore throat and prolonged fatigue during recovery compared with some other variants. However, further research is needed to establish whether the variant causes more severe disease, spreads more easily or significantly reduces protection from existing immunity. - November 10, 2026 Popular Trending Spotlight Malaysia Loke urges PM to focus on reforms, not early election pressure Malaysia Melaka declares special holiday tomorrow, in recognition of the people's mandate Malaysia Ab Rauf retains Melaka leadership Malaysia Mahathir makes first major party appearance since Hasmah's death at Pejuang AGM Malaysia Perak Sultan warns against shielding rulers from people's grievances Malaysia Retiree loses RM80k after WhatsApp investment scam demands RM50k to release profits Health Selangor health clinics prioritise emergency cases regardless of patients’ nationality Malaysia Some 243,501 undocumented migrants sent home under Malaysia's repatriation programme Malaysia Police hunt 38-year-old man over fatal stabbing in Kota Kinabalu You may be interested Health Selangor health clinics prioritise emergency cases regardless of patients’ nationality Off beat Penang moves to strengthen position as green manufacturing hub By Ian McIntyre Events Annie Tan looks to keep traditional Asian flavours relevant through modern dining By Alfian Z.M. supplementary_news.content: Logo Go Ad-Free Home India World Politics Sports Business Quick Take Columns Entertainment Art & Culture Lifestyle Books Technology Open Avenues Archives Movies Cover Stories Features Health Digital Stories Logo Home India World Politics Entertainment Sports Search NewsWrap HomeLifestyleNew COVID-19 variant PJ.2.1 spreads across countries: Symptoms, risks and what the research says New COVID-19 variant PJ.2.1 spreads across countries: Symptoms, risks and what the research says Open Bureau Last Updated:November 10, 2026, 17:09 IST Summarise Share Share ADVERTISEMENT First detected in Canada in May 2026, the COVID-19 variant PJ.2.1 has since been identified in North America, Europe and parts of Asia. Early laboratory research suggests it may enter human cells more efficiently, but there is currently no evidence that it causes more severe illness or significantly escapes vaccine-induced immunity. Covid-19 Virus FAQsSummarise COVID-19 may no longer dominate daily headlines, but the virus has not stopped evolving. A newly identified lineage, PJ.2.1, is attracting attention after appearing in several countries and displaying genetic changes that researchers are examining closely. Does this mean another major wave is approaching? Are existing vaccines still useful? And should people in India be concerned? COVID-19 testing kits Here is what current research and public health surveillance tell us about the variant. ADVERTISEMENT Sign up for Open Magazine's ad-free experience Enjoy uninterrupted access to premium content and insights. Go Ad-Free What is the new COVID-19 variant PJ.2.1? PJ.2.1 is a lineage of SARS-CoV-2, the virus responsible for COVID-19. Researchers describe it as a saltation variant, meaning it emerged with a relatively large number of genetic changes rather than accumulating mutations gradually. COVID-19 testing kits A study published in the Journal of Infection on October 24, 2026, by researchers including Markus Hoffmann and colleagues, traced its origins to MC.10.1.7, a descendant of the JN.1 lineage. Its first documented sample was collected in Ontario, Canada, on May 2, 2026. Open Magazine Latest Edition is Out Now! The Wealth Issue 2026 06 Nov 2026 - Vol 05 | Issue 45 Portraits of Dreamers and Doers under 35 Read Now Where has PJ.2.1 been detected? Is it spreading globally? After its initial detection in Canada, PJ.2.1 was identified in several US states and countries including Spain, France, Israel, Singapore, Australia and New Zealand. Public Health Ontario's genomic surveillance data showed that PJ.2.1 accounted for 25.2% of sequenced SARS-CoV-2 samples between September 20 and October 17, up from 16.9% in the preceding four-week period. Get Rapid Tests Hong Kong's Centre for Health Protection also reported PJ.2.1 within its JN.1 lineage surveillance data in its November 5 update. However, that figure represents the broader JN.1 group, not PJ.2.1 alone. Recommended Stories Quick Take | What Is Brain Stacking? Seven Things to Know About the Trend That Wants You Off Your Phone The Music between Us: Poetry, memory and kinship that endure beyond borders The Double Danger The Last Word on Salon: Why Literary Media Is Worth Saving The Diabetes Epidemic Hiding Inside India’s ‘Healthy’ Bodies Why is the PJ.2.1 variant attracting scientific attention? The key question is how effectively the variant can enter human cells. SARS-CoV-2 uses its spike protein to attach to a receptor called ACE2, which is present on human cells. The Journal of Infection study found that PJ.2.1 appeared to bind more efficiently to ACE2 in laboratory experiments. This characteristic could help explain its growth, although laboratory findings alone cannot establish how easily it spreads between people. Infection control products Researchers also examined its ability to evade antibodies. They found no substantial additional immune escape compared with most of the other variants tested. ADVERTISEMENT What are the symptoms of the PJ.2.1 COVID-19 variant? There is currently no confirmed symptom pattern unique to PJ.2.1. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), common COVID-19 symptoms include: Fever and chills, sore throat, persistent cough, runny or blocked nose, headache and body aches, fatigue and weakness, shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting or diarrhoea. Some people may also experience changes in their sense of taste or smell. The WHO cautions that COVID-19 symptoms can overlap with those of influenza and other respiratory infections. Symptoms alone cannot reliably establish which virus has caused an illness; testing may be necessary. More from the author Open Bureau Quick Take | What Is Brain Stacking? Seven Things to Know About the Trend That Wants You Off Your Phone India Beat New Zealand by 22 Runs to Seal ODI Series as Pacers Lead the Way Kate Middleton Joins Prince William in Mumbai for Their First Overseas Tour Together Since 2022 ‘Because of Your Dk?’ Australian PM caught in embarrassing hot mic gaffe With Chris Bowen Is PJ.2.1 more dangerous than previous COVID-19 variants? There is not enough clinical evidence to conclude that PJ.2.1 causes more severe disease, hospitalisations or deaths. The research published in the Journal of Infection primarily examined the variant's genetic characteristics, cell entry and antibody sensitivity. It did not establish that people infected with PJ.2.1 are more likely to develop serious complications. Older adults, people with weakened immune systems and those with underlying conditions such as diabetes, heart disease and chronic respiratory illnesses remain at greater risk of severe COVID-19. ADVERTISEMENT Do existing COVID-19 vaccines protect against PJ.2.1? The laboratory findings offer some reassurance. Researchers found that antibodies from people who had received an LP.8.1-adapted COVID-19 vaccine could neutralise PJ.2.1. Its sensitivity to neutralisation was 1.8 times lower than that of the LP.8.1 reference variant. This suggests that the variant has not demonstrated a dramatic ability to escape vaccine-induced antibodies. However, laboratory neutralisation results do not establish how well a vaccine prevents infection in everyday conditions. The WHO continues to recommend COVID-19 vaccination for people at highest risk of severe disease, including older adults and individuals with certain underlying conditions. Has PJ.2.1 been detected in India? Should people be worried? There is currently no verified public confirmation that PJ.2.1 has been detected in India. The Indian SARS-CoV-2 Genomics Consortium (INSACOG) monitors changes in circulating coronavirus strains through a network of sequencing laboratories, but its publicly available dashboard does not identify PJ.2.1 as a confirmed Indian detection. There is also an important distinction in the WHO's classification. Its latest published variant-tracking information lists JN.1 as a variant of interest and XFG, NB.1.8.1, PQ.16.1.1 and BA.3.2 as variants under monitoring. PJ.2.1 is not separately listed in those categories. For now, the emergence of PJ.2.1 calls for continued surveillance rather than alarm. Maintaining vaccination among vulnerable groups, practising good respiratory hygiene and seeking medical advice when symptoms become concerning remain sensible precautions. The research is still developing, and whether this lineage will have a significant impact on global COVID-19 trends remains to be seen. (With inputs from ANI) Frequently Asked Questions What is the new COVID-19 variant PJ.2.1? - PJ.2.1 is a SARS-CoV-2 lineage described as a saltation variant, emerging with many genetic changes. Its first sample was collected in Ontario, Canada, on May 2, 2026. Where has the PJ.2.1 variant been detected globally? + PJ.2.1 was detected in Canada, several US states, Spain, France, Israel, Singapore, Australia, and New Zealand. Public Health Ontario reported it accounted for 25.2% of sequenced samples by October 17. Why is the PJ.2.1 variant attracting scientific attention? + Scientists are examining PJ.2.1 because laboratory experiments suggest it binds more efficiently to the ACE2 receptor on human cells, potentially explaining its growth. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 16, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health AZD7442 Antibody and Bivalent COVID-19 Vaccine Are Well Tolerated in Immunocompromised Adults by November 13, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 AZD7442 Antibody and Bivalent COVID-19 Vaccine Are Well Tolerated in Immunocompromised Adults Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Co-administering the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 followed by a bivalent Ancestral/BA.1 mRNA/LNP SARS-CoV-2 vaccine was well tolerated with no serious adverse events in immunocompromised adults, according to findings from the multicentre, open-label, phase II randomised controlled RAPID-PROTECTION trial. The clinical trial evaluated the safety, pharmacokinetics, and immunogenicity of the combination regimen in 139 immunocompromised adult participants who remain highly vulnerable to severe COVID-19 infection. Under the study protocol, participants received the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 followed 28 days later by the bivalent vaccine. Pharmacokinetic monitoring showed that serum concentrations of AZD7442 peaked at day 28 following administration. Circulating concentrations of the monoclonal antibody remained detectable across different disease cohorts through day 180 of follow-up. Discover more Study Biology vaccines Vaccine vaccine Find Vaccines Humoral immune evaluations revealed that anti-Spike antibody responses increased following AZD7442 administration and reached their highest measured levels after subsequent vaccination. However, while binding antibodies against Omicron variants increased post-vaccination, functional neutralisation of Omicron remained limited after both AZD7442 and vaccination. Detailed epitope mapping showed that vaccination preferentially boosted antibodies directed against the S2 subunit, the S1 N-terminal domain, and receptor-binding domain epitopes distinct from those bound by AZD7442. Vaccination was also observed to increase S2-specific memory B cells among participants. In addition to humoral responses, vaccine-induced T-cell responses demonstrated cross-reactivity between ancestral SARS-CoV-2 and Omicron variants. The trial investigators concluded that these findings support the consideration of combined antibody and vaccine strategies in future therapeutic antibody development, with the study registered under ISRCTN53507177. The multicentre RAPID-PROTECTION clinical trial evaluated this intervention using an open-label, phase II randomised controlled trial design focused on immunocompromised adults who remain at high risk of severe COVID-19. Study participants received the long-acting monoclonal antibody AZD7442 and were subsequently administered the bivalent Ancestral/BA.1 mRNA/LNP SARS-CoV-2 vaccine twenty-eight days later. Across the cohort of 139 adult patients, clinical monitoring confirmed that the long-acting monoclonal antibody was well tolerated, with investigators documenting no serious adverse events throughout the trial protocol. The study was officially registered with the International Standard Randomised Controlled Trial Number registry under identifier ISRCTN53507177.
