Serum concentrations of AZD7442 reached their peak at day 28 following administration, coinciding with the timing of subsequent vaccination. Longitudinal follow-up further established that serum AZD7442 remained detectable across different disease cohorts through day 180. Alongside these pharmacokinetic measurements, assessments of humoral immunogenicity demonstrated that anti-Spike antibody responses rose following the initial AZD7442 administration and reached their highest measured levels after participants received the bivalent mRNA/LNP vaccination. Detailed analysis of antibody targets revealed distinct patterns of humoral immune activation following the sequential regimen. Vaccination preferentially boosted antibodies targeting the S2 subunit, the S1 N-terminal domain, and receptor-binding domain epitopes that were not bound by AZD7442 itself. In addition to expanding circulating antibody breadth, the bivalent vaccination increased the presence of S2-specific memory B cells in the immunosuppressed participants. However, the trial identified notable boundaries in humoral protection against circulating viral variants. Although binding antibodies directed against Omicron variants increased after vaccination, functional neutralisation of Omicron remained limited following both the initial AZD7442 administration and the subsequent vaccine dose. While neutralising antibody activity against Omicron was constrained, evaluations of cellular immunity showed broader activity across SARS-CoV-2 strains. Vaccine-induced T-cell responses proved cross-reactive between ancestral SARS-CoV-2 and Omicron variants, demonstrating that cellular responses remained capable of recognising divergent viral lineages. Because immunocompromised individuals continue to face serious risks from SARS-CoV-2 infection, these combined immunological and pharmacokinetic findings provide direct empirical support for future therapeutic development. The investigators concluded that the documented safety, cellular cross-reactivity, and pharmacokinetic stability support the consideration of combined monoclonal antibody and vaccination strategies in future therapeutic antibody development programs. supplementary_news.content_title: Could a common diabetes drug help prevent long COVID?
supplementary_news.content: A nationwide study suggests that prescribing the widely used diabetes drug metformin soon after COVID-19 infection may substantially reduce the risk of long COVID or death, reinforcing earlier clinical trial findings. Study: Metformin at the Time of COVID-19 Infection and Risk of Long COVID: A Target Trial Emulation Study. Image credit: TBamphoto/Shutterstock.com Prescription of metformin within six days of documented severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 ( SARS-CoV-2 ) infection is associated with a 53% lower risk of developing long COVID or death over six months, according to a new study published in the Journal of Medical Virology . Metformin emerges as a potential long COVID preventive SARS-CoV-2, the causative pathogen of the coronavirus disease 2019 ( COVID-19 ) pandemic, continues to cause new infections across countries. Long COVID refers to symptoms that persist or develop following SARS-CoV-2 infection, typically lasting at least three months, and has become a major public health concern worldwide. Long COVID is also associated with a significant economic burden, highlighting the need for identifying medications that can reduce the risk of developing long COVID. Metformin, a widely used medication for type 2 diabetes, has shown the ability to inhibit SARS-CoV-2 in in vitro studies. In a randomized clinical trial, patients receiving metformin were found to have lower nasal viral load and a reduced risk of developing long COVID. However, the trial restricted enrollment by age and body mass index, and only 22% were enrolled during the Omicron era. These factors might have restricted the generalizability of its findings to patients with diverse sociodemographic and health conditions. The current study aimed to investigate the association between newly prescribed metformin at the time of SARS-CoV-2 infection and the risk of developing long COVID in a broader sample, using electronic health records. Nationwide health records help assess metformin and long COVID The study analyzed electronic health record data from a nationwide database containing over 21 million individuals with documented SARS-CoV-2 infection from every state in the United States to identify new metformin users who were prescribed the drug within six days of documented SARS-CoV-2 infection. New metformin users were compared with those prescribed comparator medications, including fluvoxamine, fluticasone, ivermectin, or montelukast, for the risk of long COVID or death within 180 days of the metformin or comparator medication prescription. The researchers excluded patients with documented indications for chronic metformin use, including diabetes and prediabetes, as well as those prescribed metformin or comparator medications in the preceding 12 months. Eligible patients were also required to have attended outpatient visits during both the 0–6-month and 6–12-month periods before infection. Early metformin prescriptions linked to lower long COVID risk The study included 248 patients in the metformin group and a comparator group with a weighted size equivalent to approximately 248 patients. In most cases, medications were prescribed within two days of SARS-CoV-2 infection, suggesting successful identification of patients who were seeking metformin or control medications for their infection. The analysis of primary outcomes showed that, after weighting, about 4% of patients in the metformin group and 8.5% of patients in the control group had long COVID or died, representing an absolute difference of approximately 4.5 percentage points. Download the latest edition The adjusted risk ratio analysis indicated that patients who received a metformin prescription within a week of documented SARS-CoV-2 infection had a 53% lower risk of long COVID or death over a 6-month period, compared with those who received a prescription for comparator medications. Further analysis suggested that having a metformin prescription within one day of infection was associated with a 61% lower risk of long COVID or death, whereas having the same prescription within 14 days of infection was associated with a 25% lower risk. Real-world findings reinforce earlier metformin clinical trial results The study provides further evidence of an association between newly prescribed metformin during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection and a lower risk of long COVID or death over a period of six months. The association appeared stronger in patients who received metformin earlier in infection. These findings are consistent with previous studies demonstrating that early initiation of antiviral treatment against SARS-CoV-2 infection is more effective in reducing viral replication than late-stage treatment. Previous in vitro studies have also indicated that metformin reduces SARS-CoV-2 RNA while increasing cell viability. Similarly, previous randomized clinical trials have shown reduced viral load in patients using metformin. In the subgroup excluding those with a nirmatrelvir–ritonavir prescription, the study found a slightly higher risk ratio. This finding raises the hypothesis that patients receiving a nirmatrelvir–ritonavir prescription in addition to a new metformin prescription may have a lower risk ratio than the entire study population. Because of the observational design, the study analyses may be limited by missing data and misclassification of exposures, outcomes, and confounders. Since nirmatrelvir–ritonavir could be obtained directly from pharmacies without a physician visit, there remains a possibility that the use of these medications may not be fully captured in electronic health records. Another potential limitation is missing vaccination data. Patients with or without COVID-19 vaccination may experience differential outcomes following SARS-CoV-2 infection, independent of metformin use. Furthermore, the analyzed electronic health records may not include the exact number and date of SARS-CoV-2 infections because of home testing, and the elevated levels of glycated hemoglobin in the metformin group suggest that this group may have included patients with undiagnosed diabetes or prediabetes. There may be several other factors that might have influenced the observed outcomes, such as vague symptoms, access to healthcare, and pre-existing health conditions. However, these are challenges inherent in identifying and diagnosing long COVID. Future clinical trials and further research are needed to clarify the potential benefits of metformin for preventing long COVID and help inform treatment guidelines

Goldberg, Michael D. Kupperman, and Ruian Ke. The modern enormous scale of viral genomic data, as exemplified during the COVID-19 pandemic by SARS-CoV-2, presents unique opportunities for epidemic inference and real-time monitoring. A key operational challenge in viral surveillance is wading through an extremely large stream of sequence data in order to identify small subsets of sequences that may represent rapid population growth of newly emerged lineages. To address this challenge, the authors formulated a novel methodology that represents the distances between small subsets of viral sequences as graph Laplacians. By leveraging these mathematical representations, the team was able to identify specific structural features directly tied to rapid population growth. From early SARS-CoV-2 sequence data collected in the United States and the United Kingdom between 2021 and mid-2022, the investigators identified two primary features—genetic diversity and graph connectivity—that allow the model to reliably estimate the growth rates of newly emerged lineages. Discover more machine learning Learn AI Tools Machine Learning Get Rapid Tests Find Lung Care To test the validity and generalizability of their model, the researchers applied it to viral genomic data collected from mid-2022 to the end of 2024. For data collected in 2023, when sequencing efforts were relatively high with thousands of sequences generated per day in both the United States and the United Kingdom, the model correctly identified the most rapidly expanding lineages when they were still at low frequencies. Overall, the researchers concluded that their work provides a scalable and adaptable tool to estimate the growth rate of newly emerged SARS-CoV-2 lineages. supplementary_news.content_title: Could a common diabetes drug help prevent long COVID?
supplementary_news.content: A nationwide study suggests that prescribing the widely used diabetes drug metformin soon after COVID-19 infection may substantially reduce the risk of long COVID or death, reinforcing earlier clinical trial findings. Study: Metformin at the Time of COVID-19 Infection and Risk of Long COVID: A Target Trial Emulation Study. Image credit: TBamphoto/Shutterstock.com Prescription of metformin within six days of documented severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection is associated with a 53% lower risk of developing long COVID or death over six months, according to a new study published in the Journal of Medical Virology. Metformin emerges as a potential long COVID preventive SARS-CoV-2, the causative pathogen of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, continues to cause new infections across countries. Long COVID refers to symptoms that persist or develop following SARS-CoV-2 infection, typically lasting at least three months, and has become a major public health concern worldwide. Long COVID is also associated with a significant economic burden, highlighting the need for identifying medications that can reduce the risk of developing long COVID. Metformin, a widely used medication for type 2 diabetes, has shown the ability to inhibit SARS-CoV-2 in in vitro studies. In a randomized clinical trial, patients receiving metformin were found to have lower nasal viral load and a reduced risk of developing long COVID. However, the trial restricted enrollment by age and body mass index, and only 22% were enrolled during the Omicron era. These factors might have restricted the generalizability of its findings to patients with diverse sociodemographic and health conditions. The current study aimed to investigate the association between newly prescribed metformin at the time of SARS-CoV-2 infection and the risk of developing long COVID in a broader sample, using electronic health records. Nationwide health records help assess metformin and long COVID The study analyzed electronic health record data from a nationwide database containing over 21 million individuals with documented SARS-CoV-2 infection from every state in the United States to identify new metformin users who were prescribed the drug within six days of documented SARS-CoV-2 infection. New metformin users were compared with those prescribed comparator medications, including fluvoxamine, fluticasone, ivermectin, or montelukast, for the risk of long COVID or death within 180 days of the metformin or comparator medication prescription. The researchers excluded patients with documented indications for chronic metformin use, including diabetes and prediabetes, as well as those prescribed metformin or comparator medications in the preceding 12 months. Eligible patients were also required to have attended outpatient visits during both the 0–6-month and 6–12-month periods before infection. Early metformin prescriptions linked to lower long COVID risk The study included 248 patients in the metformin group and a comparator group with a weighted size equivalent to approximately 248 patients. In most cases, medications were prescribed within two days of SARS-CoV-2 infection, suggesting successful identification of patients who were seeking metformin or control medications for their infection. The analysis of primary outcomes showed that, after weighting, about 4% of patients in the metformin group and 8.5% of patients in the control group had long COVID or died, representing an absolute difference of approximately 4.5 percentage points. The adjusted risk ratio analysis indicated that patients who received a metformin prescription within a week of documented SARS-CoV-2 infection had a 53% lower risk of long COVID or death over a 6-month period, compared with those who received a prescription for comparator medications. Further analysis suggested that having a metformin prescription within one day of infection was associated with a 61% lower risk of long COVID or death, whereas having the same prescription within 14 days of infection was associated with a 25% lower risk. Real-world findings reinforce earlier metformin clinical trial results The study provides further evidence of an association between newly prescribed metformin during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection and a lower risk of long COVID or death over a period of six months. The association appeared stronger in patients who received metformin earlier in infection. These findings are consistent with previous studies demonstrating that early initiation of antiviral treatment against SARS-CoV-2 infection is more effective in reducing viral replication than late-stage treatment. Previous in vitro studies have also indicated that metformin reduces SARS-CoV-2 RNA while increasing cell viability. Similarly, previous randomized clinical trials have shown reduced viral load in patients using metformin. In the subgroup excluding those with a nirmatrelvir–ritonavir prescription, the study found a slightly higher risk ratio. This finding raises the hypothesis that patients receiving a nirmatrelvir–ritonavir prescription in addition to a new metformin prescription may have a lower risk ratio than the entire study population. Because of the observational design, the study analyses may be limited by missing data and misclassification of exposures, outcomes, and confounders. Since nirmatrelvir–ritonavir could be obtained directly from pharmacies without a physician visit, there remains a possibility that the use of these medications may not be fully captured in electronic health records. Another potential limitation is missing vaccination data. Patients with or without COVID-19 vaccination may experience differential outcomes following SARS-CoV-2 infection, independent of metformin use. Furthermore, the analyzed electronic health records may not include the exact number and date of SARS-CoV-2 infections because of home testing, and the elevated levels of glycated hemoglobin in the metformin group suggest that this group may have included patients with undiagnosed diabetes or prediabetes. There may be several other factors that might have influenced the observed outcomes, such as vague symptoms, access to healthcare, and pre-existing health conditions. However, these are challenges inherent in identifying and diagnosing long COVID. Future clinical trials and further research are needed to clarify the potential benefits of metformin for preventing long COVID and help inform treatment guidelines. - Bramante CT. (2026). Metformin at the Time of COVID-19 Infection and Risk of Long COVID: A Target Trial Emulation Study. Journal of Medical Virology. Introduction 结构生物学为严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(SARS-CoV-2)病毒功能和干预研究提供了分子参考点。该病毒编码四种结构蛋白——刺突(S)、膜(M)、包膜(E)和核衣壳(N)——以及十六个非结构蛋白(nsps 1–16)和多种附属蛋白。本综述探讨结构观察何时能够支持生物学解释,以及何种额外证据可将其与干预结局相连接。比较沿三个独立维度展开:结构覆盖、实验背景和功能支持。评估标准包括:功能是否在表达该蛋白的内源系统中测量、结构-功能关联是否通过突变得以验证、观察是否在独立系统或独立小组中重现、以及感染期间是否产生该蛋白。 2. Structural Proteins 2.1. Spike (S) Glycoprotein S糖蛋白是同源三聚体I类融合蛋白,也是主要抗原靶点。预融合S胞外域结构采用2P稳定设计,显示一个受体结合域(RBD)向上构象。每个S原聚体含22个潜在N-连接糖基化位点。RBD与血管紧张素转化酶2(ACE2)结合的晶体结构定义了受体结合界面,分子动力学(MD)模拟显示SARS-CoV-2 RBD-ACE2复合物动态降低且静电吸引力增强。跨膜蛋白酶丝氨酸2(TMPRSS2)和内体组织蛋白酶参与蛋白切割。跨膜结构域(TMD)通过核磁共振(NMR)和冷冻电镜解析,显示平行三聚体组装,胞质侧半胱氨酸被棕榈酰化。冷冻电子断层扫描(cryo-ET)显示完整病毒颗粒上S蛋白的铰链样运动和构象多样性,内部核糖核蛋白(RNP)组装呈堆叠排列。RBD内的脂肪酸结合位点可稳定锁定构象。可溶性胞外域不报告膜锚施加的约束。 2.2. Membrane (M) Protein M蛋白是病毒包膜中最丰富的蛋白,含222个氨基酸和三个跨膜螺旋。两种构象的M二聚体已解析,脂质纳米盘中的结构描述了确定膜环境中的二聚体。M与JNJ-9676结合的冷冻电镜结构支持其作为潜在抗病毒靶点。直接脂质相互作用与M构象行为相关。 2.3. Envelope (E) Protein E蛋白是75个氨基酸的小膜蛋白,体外电生理记录显示离子通道活性。固态核磁共振(NMR)解析了其跨膜结构域的五聚体螺旋束。C末端区域与宿主蛋白识别相关,E C末端肽与PALS1片段结合的冷冻电镜结构定义了特异性宿主结合界面。 2.4. Nucleocapsid (N) Protein N蛋白含N端结构域(NTD,参与RNA结合)和C端结构域(CTD,介导二聚化和RNA结合),由内在无序区域连接。NTD晶体结构、NTD-RNA复合物模型及CTD二聚体结构已解析。体外N-RNA混合物可形成凝聚体。cryo-ET揭示了病毒颗粒内RNP组装的空间组织。 3. Nonstructural Proteins and Replication Machinery 3.1. Overview of Nonstructural Proteins and the Replication–Transcription Complex (RTC) 复制转录复合体(RTC)与双膜囊泡(DMV)相关。核心聚合酶复合物由nsp12(RNA依赖的RNA聚合酶,RdRp)、nsp7和nsp8组成。其他酶包括nsp13解旋酶、nsp14(具有3'-5'外切核糖核酸酶(ExoN)和N7-甲基转移酶活性)、nsp15内切核糖核酸酶和nsp16 2'-O-甲基转移酶。扩展RTC结构显示核心聚合酶与nsp9、nsp13、nsp10和nsp14等关联,但不同研究解析的组件不同。nsp3、nsp4和nsp6参与内质网(ER)膜重塑。nsp11是13个氨基酸的肽。 3.2. Nsp1 Nsp1参与调节宿主蛋白合成。分离Nsp1 N端结构域的晶体结构提供了其折叠核心。冷冻电镜和功能分析表征了核糖体相关Nsp1,并将其与细胞蛋白合成抑制关联。 3.3. Nsp2 交联质谱为nsp2架构提供了整合模型。全长模型结合冷冻电镜数据和计算预测,但实验支持因区域而异。保守锌结合基序提示可能的核酸相互作用。 3.4. Main Protease (Mpro/Nsp5) Mpro(又称3C样蛋白酶(3CLpro)或nsp5)是半胱氨酸蛋白酶,在pp1ab的11个典型位点切割复制酶多聚蛋白。成熟酶作为同源二聚体,每个原聚体含两个β桶结构域和C端α螺旋结构域,催化位点含半胱氨酸-组氨酸二元组。早期N3结合结构为基础抑制剂发现提供基础。Mpro与萘瑞特韦(nirmatrelvir)的复合物显示其与催化半胱氨酸(Cys145)形成共价加合物。 3.5. Papain-Like Protease (PLpro/Nsp3 Domain) PLpro参与多聚蛋白加工,并去除宿主蛋白的泛素和干扰素刺激基因15(ISG15)修饰。PLpro含N端泛素样(Ubl)结构域和蛋白酶区(拇指、手掌和手指亚结构域)。PLpro与ISG15 C末端探针共价结合的结构已解析。GRL0617结合结构显示非共ovalent抑制剂占据靠近但独立催化半胱氨酸(Cys111)的位点。 3.6. RNA-Dependent RNA Polymerase (RdRp/Nsp12) RdRp(nsp12)与辅助因子nsp7和nsp8一起发挥作用。其聚合酶结构域采用经典右手折叠,含手指、手掌和拇指亚结构域,N端NiRAN域通过界面域连接。RNA-free和RNA-bound聚合酶结构已解析。NiRAN域和nsp9参与非经典RNA加帽途径。瑞德西韦(remdesivir)阻断RNA转位的结构和生化分析支持延迟抑制RNA延伸。 3.7. Helicase (Nsp13) Nsp13是核苷三磷酸依赖的解旋酶,含N端锌结合域和两个具有重组酶A(RecA)样折叠的结构域。代表性晶体结构已解析。片段筛选识别了与早期抑制剂研究相关的结合片段。 3.8. Exoribonuclease (Nsp14 ExoN) and Mismatch Recognition Nsp14是双功能蛋白,含N端ExoN域和C端N7-甲基转移酶域。Nsp10刺激ExoN活性,结构比较将其结合与nsp14盖亚结构域重折叠关联。nsp10-nsp14 ExoN域复合物及RNA-bound冷冻电镜结构为携带3'-末端错配的RNA底物的识别提供分子基础。 3.9. Endoribonuclease (Nsp15 NendoU) Nsp15是类尼多病毒尿苷酸特异性内切核糖核酸酶(NendoU),形成六聚体。在感染期间,该活性拮抗双链RNA(dsRNA)诱导的抗病毒信号。 3.10. 2′-O-Methyltransferase (Nsp16 with Nsp10) Nsp16是298个氨基酸的2'-O-甲基转移酶,与nsp10合作在病毒mRNA加帽中发挥作用。nsp16-nsp10复合物与S-腺苷甲硫氨酸(SAM)和帽相关配体的晶体结构已解析。异四聚体组装包含两个nsp16-nsp10异二聚体。 4. Accessory Proteins 4.1. ORF3a Protein ORF3a是275个氨基酸的膜蛋白。脂质纳米盘中的冷冻电镜结构显示二聚体构象,每个原聚体有三个跨膜螺旋。关于ORF3a是否导电存在争议:一项研究记录通道样活性,另一项研究未发现可归因于ORF3a的可重复电流。ORF3a还阻断HOPS复合物介导的自噬体-溶酶体融合。研究人员不将通道活性视为这些细胞表型的默认解释。 4.2. ORF3c Protein ORF3c由与ORF3a重叠的替代阅读框编码。比较基因组分析支持其蛋白质编码状态,且已证实感染期间的表达。其通过靶向线粒体抗病毒信号蛋白(MAVS)抑制先天感知。 4.3. ORF6 Protein ORF6通过与RNA输出1(Rae1)和核孔蛋白98(Nup98)相互作用破坏核质运输,阻断信号转导子和转录激活子(STAT)蛋白的核输入。NMR研究在重构膜环境中表征了其构象并鉴定了N端膜锚。ORF6 C末端肽与Rae1/Nup98片段结合的晶体结构定义了宿主蛋白结合界面。 4.4. ORF7a and ORF7b Proteins ORF7a具有免疫球蛋白样胞外域,其晶体结构已确定。重组胞外域影响HLA-DR/DP/DQ表面表达。ORF7b是小疏水膜蛋白,固态NMR显示在重构膜环境中主要形成α螺旋构象。 4.5. ORF8 Protein ORF8具有免疫球蛋白样折叠,晶体结构显示同源二聚体。功能研究对IL-17受体参与结论不一。研究人员将ORF8相关炎症反应视为在某些实验系统中得到支持。 4.6. ORF9b and the Putative ORF9c Product ORF9b由N基因内的替代阅读框编码。分离的同源二聚体及与TOM70结合的晶体结构已解析。ORF9c是推定的编码区,但感染期间的蛋白质表达尚未确立。 4.7. ORF10 and ORF3b ORF10是推定的短编码区。ORF10-Cullin-2-ZYG11B复合物在细胞培养条件下不是感染所需的。ORF3b是推定的重叠编码区,比较基因组分析不支持其作为保守蛋白质编码基因。 5. Cross-Protein Assemblies and In Situ Structural Insights cryo-ET揭示了病毒颗粒内S蛋白的构象变化和内部RNP组装。nsp3-nsp4跨膜孔复合体在DMV双膜界面处的结构已被解析。超分辨率成像区分了DMV相关dsRNA和dsRNA颗粒,支持蛋白酶依赖性成熟模型。 6. Effects of Variants on Structure and Function 早期变异株的S蛋白结构显示相似的总体架构但RBD构象群体不同。Omicron研究结合S结构和RBD-抗体复合结构,显示尽管架构广泛保留,但中和活性降低。后续Omicron谱系引入了多个替代,其中一些位于1类抗体表位内。Mpro变异评估显示对特定抑制剂的敏感性取决于化合物和蛋白变体。 7. Structure-Guided Intervention Research: Antivirals, Antibodies, and Vaccines 7.1. Small-Molecule Antivirals 瑞德西韦(remdesivir)的冷冻电镜结构显示其活性形式在聚合酶催化位点,RNA合成在额外核苷酸掺入后停滞。萘瑞特韦(nirmatrelvir)与Mpro的复合物显示其与催化半胱氨酸形成可逆共价键。恩司特韦(ensitrelvir)是非共价Mpro抑制剂。计算筛选提出Mpro抑制剂候选物。 7.2. Therapeutic Antibodies Barnes等的四类方案根据RBD抗体与ACE2位点的关系及其在不同S蛋白构象中的可及性对其进行分组。组合抗体如REGN-COV2和AZD7442结合非重叠表位。完整IgG抗体在病毒颗粒上的cryo-ET显示双价结合。美国FDA撤销了REGEN-COV、sotrovimab、Evusheld和bebtelovimab的紧急使用授权。 7.3. Vaccine Design and Structural Insights 预融合稳定方法 informed SARS-CoV-2抗原设计。HexaPro扩展了2P设计。人研究显示疫苗受者比康复个体具有更高的RBD结合IgG效价,但中和效价与RBD结合IgG效价的比例更低。变异株适应疫苗研究提供了针对更新抗原的血清中和活性。 8. Methodological Challenges and Advances 8.1. Experimental Methods and Sample Context 单颗粒冷冻电镜解析了早期预融合S和聚合酶复合物。缓冲成分(如CHAPS或DDM)可将重构的S蛋白群体移向关闭状态。cryo-ET存在缺失楔问题。X射线晶体学和NMR提供互补信息。蛋白质组的结构覆盖不均一。 8.2. Computational Simulations and Integrative Modeling MD模拟探索构象动力学。结合自由能估计提供了模型依赖描述。虚拟筛选可提名候选物,但需要独立实验评估。AlphaFold预测扩展了结构范围,但预测完整性不意味着均匀实验支持。 9. Outlook 本综述支持特定的分子特征,但从结构到生物功能和临床益处的某些联系仍未解决。主要未解决问题涉及天然组装体中分子组件的组织和功能关系。理解动态需要将结构状态与随时间过程的测量更紧密地联系。S蛋白的跨膜锚定部分是一个特定差距。 10. Conclusions 结构生物学建立了对SARS-CoV-2受体识别、多聚蛋白加工、RNA合成和处理的分子描述。当独立的生化和结构测量在可比的实验条件下解决相同的分子主张时,这些观察最强烈地支持生物学解释。该综述将结构发现与其所支持的主张联系起来,并识别了将分子观察与细胞功能和干预结局联系所需的证据。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 2000+篇,学术前沿动态全时追踪! 从2000到2026,27载全因有您;您的每一分支持,都给予我们无穷的动力! 公测期:打赏8元解锁30天免费阅读! 下载安捷伦电子书《通过细胞代谢揭示新的药物靶点》探索如何通过代谢分析促进您的药物发现研究 10x Genomics新品Visium HD 开启单细胞分辨率的全转录组空间分析! 欢迎下载Twist《不断变化的CRISPR筛选格局》电子书 下载《细胞内蛋白质互作分析方法电子书》 引领行业 | 聚焦麦特绘谱代谢组学整体解决方案>> 「大小鼠繁育与健康管理」指导海报,点击即可免费领取电子版或实体海报>> 揭秘单细胞测序-深入了解这项正在改变我们开展科学研究的技术>> 18,000+ 成品模型现货随取,点击下载模式生物选型指南>> 相关新闻 生物通微信公众号 生物通新浪微博 微信 新浪微博 我要投稿 搜索 国际 国内 人物 产业 热点 科普 热搜:SARS-CoV-2蛋白质组|结构覆盖|功能解释|实验背景|干预研究|多维证据评估 热点排行 今日动态 | 人才市场 | 新技术专栏 | 中国科学人 | 云展台 | BioHot | 云讲堂直播 | 会展中心 | 特价专栏 | 技术快讯 | 免费试用 版权所有 生物通 Copyright© eBiotrade.com, All Rights Reserved 联系信箱: 粤ICP备09063491号

supplementary_news.content: Skip to main content FactCheck.org® A Project of The Annenberg Public Policy Center FactCheck.org® Home Articles FactCheck Posts SciCheck En Español Players Guide 2026 Project 2025 series Debunking Viral Claims Ask a Question Ask FactCheck Ask SciCheck Donate Topics 2026 election President Trump immigration inflation crime healthcare vaccination View All About Us Our Mission Our Process Our Funding Our Staff Undergraduate Fellows Awards Request a Correction Contact Us Search More Newsletter Viral Claims Instagram Threads YouTube TikTok Facebook X FactCheck On the Air FactCheck Posts › SciCheck Florida’s Surgeon General Spins State COVID-19 Vaccine Comparison Study By Jessica McDonald Posted on November 12, 2026 A new analysis of data from Florida found a higher risk of mortality in those receiving the Pfizer versus the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine in the year after a first dose. It does not establish that the Pfizer vaccine was dangerous or caused deaths, contrary to suggestions by the state’s surgeon general or statements by online purveyors of vaccine misinformation. The study did not compare outcomes to unvaccinated people, so it cannot say whether vaccination with either shot was associated with higher or lower mortality overall. The paper acknowledged that one possible reason for Pfizer’s higher relative mortality risk is that the Moderna vaccine was more effective against COVID-19 than the Pfizer shot. The study was published on Nov. 4 in the journal Global Epidemiology and was mostly conducted by members of the Florida Department of Health using state data. It found that compared with a Moderna dose, adult Pfizer recipients had a 40% higher risk of dying from any cause within one year of a first dose. Relative to Moderna, the Pfizer vaccine was also associated with a 91% higher risk of dying from COVID-19, a 57% higher risk of dying from cardiovascular disease and a 37% higher risk of dying from something other than COVID-19, as recorded on a death certificate. Previous research has not found that either vaccine increases mortality. Both vaccines have saved many lives by preventing COVID-19 deaths. Experts told us the study itself, which was upfront about its limitations, is not especially problematic. But some interpretations of it — including by some of the paper’s own authors — are. “As I said in January 2024, no one should be taking mRNA COVID-19 vaccines because of their terrible safety profile,” Dr. Joseph Ladapo, a co-author and Florida’s surgeon general, wrote on X the day after publication. “But for those who had to take one, Florida’s public health data strongly implies that thousands of Floridians died as a result of receiving Pfizer instead of Moderna. The number of lives lost in the U.S. and internationally is staggering, based on this analysis.” Jeffrey S. Morris, the director of biostatistics at the University of Pennsylvania who wrote a detailed critique on X of what the paper can and cannot say, told us that Ladapo’s comment goes beyond the evidence. “That is like orders of magnitude beyond what his own paper showed,” he said. Ladapo, who has a history of promoting flawed studies that argue the mRNA vaccines are dangerous, including one from the Florida Department of Health that claimed to identify a higher risk of cardiac death after vaccination in young men, cited unsubstantiated concerns when calling for a halt in the use of all mRNA COVID-19 vaccines in January 2024. That fall, the Florida Department of Health began advising all people — even older people at high risk of severe COVID-19 — to not get vaccinated with an mRNA vaccine. At the time, and still today, there is only one non-mRNA COVID-19 vaccine available in the U.S., the protein-based Novavax vaccine. No other state recommends against mRNA COVID-19 vaccination. Speaking to Children’s Health Defense, the nonprofit opposed to vaccines that Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. previously led, Ladapo framed the results as indicative of a safety concern, saying the new study helps show that “our system for evaluating vaccine safety is broken.” “The findings of this study should not be interpreted as establishing the overall safety of the Moderna vaccine,” he said, citing prior research that he claimed also raised safety concerns about the Moderna vaccine (we’ve written about that study, too). “We reiterate our recommendation that, based on what is currently known about the safety of mRNA COVID-19 vaccines, no one should receive them,” he added. The Florida Department of Health did not respond to our inquiries asking about his interpretation of the study and whether the department shared his views. Online, others made even more explicit claims about the new paper. “This is an extremely important paper. It shows that the Pfizer vaccine was not safe. It killed people. There is no other way to interpret this data,” Steve Kirsch, a former tech entrepreneur who has long spread inaccurate information about the vaccines, said on X on Nov. 5. “An official government study just confirmed that COVID shots resulted in a CATASTROPHIC loss of life,” Nicolas Hulscher, another prominent spreader of vaccine misinformation, wrote on X, sharing a video in which he further claimed that extrapolating the Florida findings to the U.S. would mean “you get a minimum of 330,000 American deaths from Pfizer alone.” These claims are false. Natalie Dean, an associate professor of biostatistics and bioinformatics at Emory University, told us the study isn’t evidence that either of the vaccines is killing people. “I don’t see how this is an indictment of the safety of these vaccines since it’s just a comparison of two different vaccines,” she said. “The way the paper is getting talked about does not align with the actual evidence in the paper,” Morris, who is also a distinguished research fellow with our parent organization, the Annenberg Public Policy Center, said. “The study legitimately demonstrates an association between vaccine brand and subsequent mortality in a selected matched Florida cohort,” he said in an X post. “It does not establish that these differences are causal, much less that they reflect vaccine-related harm.” When asked for comment, a Pfizer spokesperson told us that medical experts and regulatory authorities around the globe have reviewed and approved or recommended the vaccine, and that it continues to be monitored for safety. “With billions of doses of the vaccine administered around the world, the safety profile for the vaccine for all authorized groups continues to be favorable,” the spokesperson said. Study Limitations In the Global Epidemiology paper, the authors attempted to identify similar individuals in the state who received a Pfizer versus a Moderna vaccine in the first eight months of the vaccine rollout. They then looked at death outcomes within a year of the first vaccine dose to estimate relative mortality risk. To try to control for factors other than vaccine brand, the authors matched about 1 million individuals who received a Pfizer vaccine with 1 million who received a Moderna dose on seven different variables. These were age group; sex; race; ethnicity; calendar month of vaccination; type of vaccination site, such as private pharmacy or hospital; and census tract. The authors also did other checks to try to show that this matching was largely successful, finding no statistical difference, for example, when the same pairings were assessed for cancer deaths or suicide or homicide. The problem is that since this is an observational study, there is still concern that the mortality differences observed between the vaccines were not due to the vaccines themselves, but to other factors. Photo by guteksk7 / stock.adobe.com. A key issue Morris and Dean raised is that the vaccine recipients were not matched for medical frailty or underlying health status. If the Pfizer recipients were in poorer overall health or had more risk factors for COVID-19 or other diseases, that could explain a large part of why the Moderna recipients appear to have lower mortality, rather than suggesting anything about the vaccine itself. Then, even if the mortality difference is due to the vaccines, Morris explained in an article on X, it does not necessarily mean that the Pfizer vaccine is causing harm. It may simply be that the Moderna vaccine is better at preventing harm, making the Pfizer vaccine look bad in comparison. “You can see the better effectiveness of the Moderna vaccine in there,” Dean said of the study’s findings. Several studies have found that the Moderna vaccine was slightly more effective at preventing severe COVID-19 outcomes than Pfizer’s. Although quite similar, the original Moderna vaccine contained significantly more mRNA per dose than the Pfizer shot and the second dose was given an extra week apart. Higher protection against COVID-19 could also spill over into the other mortality categories as well, particularly during Florida’s delta variant wave in 2021, Morris said. “Any deaths that were in fact due to COVID, but they didn’t formally get tested would not have been documented as COVID, so they would be in the non-COVID deaths,” he told us. Studies have found that severe COVID-19 infections raise the risk of cardiovascular events and death well after the infection. In the paper, the authors were careful to note many of these caveats, and to say that the findings could be explained by a more protective Moderna vaccine, other factors the researchers were not able to control for, or what they term “non-specific effects” of the vaccines (or some combination thereof). It is nevertheless clear that in public, some of the authors preferred to promote the latter idea, which could include the notion that the Pfizer vaccine has some kind of harmful effect. In a post on X, Retsef Levi, the corresponding author, wrote, “This study adds to a growing evidence that the mRNA COVID vaccines of Moderna and Pfizer may have different non-specific effects.” Levi is a professor at Massachusetts Institute of Technology’s business school who has long said that mRNA COVID-19 vaccines should not be used. He was one of Kennedy’s appointees to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s vaccine advisory committee in June 2025 before a judge paused the appointments and temporarily blocked the group’s decisions in March. In his X post, Levi also pointed to a recent nanoscience study that he said “showed significant differences in systemic persistence of nano-lipids and spike mRNA between Moderna and Pfizer mRNA COVID vaccines!” The senior author of the nanoscience paper, immunologist Stephen Kent of the University of Melbourne, told us in an email that it is “inappropriate to refer to our paper supporting death from Pfizer” and that “it would not be scientifically appropriate to use our findings to draw conclusions about vaccine safety or mortality risks.” He, too, said the observed outcome in the Florida analysis could be related to Moderna protecting against COVID-19 better than Pfizer. Putting the Study in Fuller Context Another argument against jumping to the conclusion that the Pfizer vaccine is actively harming people through an unspecified mechanism is the larger body of research conducted on the COVID-19 vaccines. In particular, there is a Veterans Affairs study published in December 2021 in the New England Journal of Medicine that also compared the Pfizer and Moderna vaccines to one another using a matching approach similar to the one in the Florida analysis. (This study also did not match for health status or comorbidities, but unlike the Florida analysis, it did provide a table showing that the matched pairs did not substantially differ on those parameters.) The study was smaller and over a shorter time period, but it found that the Moderna vaccine recipients had a lower risk of a variety of adverse COVID-19 outcomes. Although not statistically significant, Pfizer recipients were 11% more likely to die from COVID-19 than Moderna recipients. The study did not, however, find any other mortality differences between the vaccines. As a check on their main findings, the authors looked at non-COVID-19 deaths, finding virtually identical patterns of death in matched recipients of both vaccines (see figure S3). “They found absolutely no difference in non-COVID deaths, like not even a trend,” Morris said. A few other studies have identified a slightly higher all-cause mortality after vaccination with various Pfizer shots compared with Moderna, but nothing approaching 40% — and some results have favored the Pfizer vaccine instead. If the Florida study results “were really true and really driven by vaccine harm, we would expect them to be replicated elsewhere, but it doesn’t seem to be,” Morris said. Notably, the studies that have looked at all-cause mortality among vaccinated and unvaccinated people have consistently found much lower rates of death in vaccinated people. A 2025 French study, for example, compared mortality over four years, finding about a 25% lower risk of death in vaccinated versus unvaccinated individuals (with a lower risk for Pfizer than Moderna). Scientists don’t think the vaccines actually lowered death risk by that much because of something called the healthy vaccinee effect. People who choose to get vaccinated are generally healthier than those who don’t — especially closer to the vaccination date, since people near the end of their lives aren’t getting vaccinated. While studies try to adjust for this issue, and longer-running ones are less affected by it, it remains a concern when interpreting the results. Still, these findings do not support the notion that the vaccines are increasing the risk of death. The authors of the French study concluded that “a causal link between mRNA vaccination and excess long-term mortality appears highly unlikely.” For both vaccines to have some kind of toxic effect, as some claim — and for the Pfizer vaccine to have a nearly 40% higher risk of death than Moderna, but not be detected in these sorts of studies — the healthy vaccinee effect would have to be “really enormous,” Morris said. Dean noted that even if the Moderna vaccine is better at protecting against COVID-19, it was still important to have both vaccines as options. When the shots were first rolled out, not only was it not yet known how the two vaccines compare, but there weren’t enough shots of any single brand for all Americans. Some data suggest the Moderna vaccine caused more intense expected side effects, such as a fever, than the Pfizer shot. “For some people, Pfizer has been a better option” because of the milder side effects, she said. “I just don’t understand indicting things backwards.” It’s worth noting that the original versions of the Florida analysis, which were posted to preprint servers, made more sweeping statements more akin to how some authors have presented the paper online, with one preprint concluding that the results are “suggestive of differential non-specific effects” of the two vaccines “and potential concerning adverse effects on all-cause and cardiovascular mortality.” The published version lacks these statements. Individuals can now point to a published document “that is going to be hard for people to understand because it’s very complex and there’s a lot of tables,” Dean said, and it can be used to “make more extreme claims.” Editor’s note: FactCheck.org does not accept advertising. supplementary_news.content_title: Severe COVID-19 Hospitalization Multiplies Post-Acute Asthma Flare Risks
supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 16, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Severe COVID-19 Hospitalization Multiplies Post-Acute Asthma Flare Risks Without Lasting Control Loss by November 10, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Severe COVID-19 Hospitalization Multiplies Post-Acute Asthma Flare Risks Without Lasting Control Loss Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Hospitalization for severe COVID-19 significantly elevates the subsequent risk of asthma exacerbations during the post-acute phase, yet overall asthma control does not suffer sustained long-term deterioration across evaluated patient populations. This primary conclusion emerges from a rigorous systematic review synthesizing data from eleven observational studies that evaluated both pediatric and adult asthma cohorts. Across large population-based datasets, individuals who required inpatient hospital admission for acute severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 infection exhibited an approximate two- to five-fold surge in post-acute asthma exacerbations relative to uninfected comparators. Conversely, patients who recovered from mild or non-hospitalized coronavirus infections experienced substantially lower, more variable, and frequently null increases in flare-up rates. Furthermore, while measurable declines in asthma control scores occurred within the initial months following infection, extended observation revealed that symptom stability and recovery remained the prevailing outcome across monitored patient groups. The newly compiled evidence addresses a persistent knowledge gap surrounding the enduring respiratory consequences of viral illness in vulnerable airway cohorts. Because viral respiratory pathogens serve as primary precipitants of acute attacks and loss of clinical control, the emergence of the global pandemic prompted urgent inquiries regarding post-infection trajectories. Initial scientific investigations centered almost entirely on whether baseline asthma heightened vulnerability to contracting coronavirus disease 2019 or exacerbated acute hospitalizations, intensive care unit admissions, and fatal events. Once accumulating epidemiological evidence confirmed that well-managed asthma did not systematically elevate acute mortality, scientific focus transitioned toward investigating lingering respiratory sequelae and post-acute functional status. Post-acute coronavirus sequelae, frequently categorized under post-acute COVID-19 syndrome or long COVID, encompass an expansive spectrum of persistent systemic complications and organ-specific symptoms that endure for weeks or months past the resolution of primary illness. Among afflicted individuals, respiratory complaints remain especially prominent, with ongoing cough, persistent dyspnea, and compromised physical exercise capacity presenting frequently in clinical settings. In patients carrying established asthma diagnoses, these lingering respiratory disturbances created pressing clinical questions regarding whether viral exposure causes persistent loss of disease control, triggers recurrent clinical exacerbations, alters underlying airway inflammation, or necessitates treatment escalation. However, prior investigations predominantly examined asthma merely as a demographic comorbidity rather than tracking its unique post-viral trajectory, or evaluated short-term peri-infectious complications without applying validated asthma-specific measurement tools or appropriate non-infected control cohorts, leaving clinical guidance uncertain. To establish reliable clinical conclusions, the review team executed a systematic evaluation adhering strictly to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 standards and an a priori registered PROSPERO protocol bearing reference CRD420261290371. The investigators systematically interrogated five major electronic databases, comprising PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature, covering all records published between 1 January 2020 and 21 January 2026. The search combined standardized medical subject headings with free-text terms tailored to identify asthma outcomes following confirmed viral infection. Eligible investigations were required to feature observational designs involving human participants with established asthma and evaluate disease-specific control or exacerbation endpoints measured at least four weeks subsequent to laboratory-confirmed or clinically documented infection, comparing outcomes against uninfected asthma cohorts or within-individual pre-infection baselines. The rigorous literature selection procedure commenced with the retrieval of 4,494 potentially pertinent citations across the searched databases. Following computerized de-duplication, independent reviewers screened 2,655 unique title and abstract records, subsequently setting aside 2,574 citations as clearly ineligible. The researchers then obtained and appraised the complete texts of 81 candidate articles, excluding 70 reports that failed to satisfy the predefined protocol criteria. The predominant grounds for exclusion comprised the absence of asthma-specific post-acute outcomes assessed beyond the initial four-week window, the evaluation of asthma solely as a baseline risk factor for COVID-19 severity, lack of appropriate comparator cohorts or longitudinal pre-post designs, inclusion of non-asthma populations without stratified reporting, and reliance on unadjusted pandemic-era ecological comparisons. Ultimately, eleven observational investigations met all predefined criteria and were admitted into the qualitative narrative synthesis. The eleven included studies encompassed prospective cohort studies, retrospective cohort evaluations, case-control analyses, and extensive healthcare registry assessments conducted across Europe, North America, East Asia, and South America. Sample sizes displayed notable breadth, spanning from 146 participants in specialized clinical cohorts to more than 21,000 individuals within national health databases. Viral infection was substantiated through reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction assays, rapid antigen tests, serological testing, or validated diagnostic codes. Comparator arms utilized within-person pre- versus post-infection records, concurrent uninfected cohorts of people with asthma, or integrated population benchmarks. Post-acute evaluation intervals commenced at least four weeks following acute diagnosis, with monitoring timeframes extending from approximately one single month to three full years across individual research protocols, providing both immediate post-acute snapshots and longitudinal surveillance of chronic airway trajectories. When evaluating post-acute exacerbation events, the systematic review identified a distinct, consistent divergence dictated by initial illness severity. Large electronic health record databases and population-based cohorts revealed that asthma patients hospitalized during acute COVID-19 faced markedly heightened post-acute exacerbation hazards compared with uninfected individuals with asthma, reporting adjusted hazard ratios ranging from 2.78 to 5.12. In contrast, patients who experienced mild or outpatient infections demonstrated much lower and more variable increases in exacerbation hazards, with reported hazard ratios hovering around 1.8 to 2.1 in some cohorts while remaining completely null in others. Several studies focusing specifically on mild or moderate disease reported no statistically significant elevation in exacerbation frequency over post-acute observation windows, particularly when utilizing unadjusted models or restricted follow-up durations, demonstrating that acute infection severity strongly modulates downstream clinical risk. In contrast to the clear risk gradient identified for acute exacerbations, findings concerning overall asthma control revealed substantial clinical heterogeneity across pediatric and adult cohorts. Multiple pediatric investigations recorded short-term decrements in disease control, noting reduced Childhood Asthma Control Test scores and greater proportions of uncontrolled or partially controlled asthma approximately one month following acute infection. Similarly, certain adult studies observed increased odds of clinically meaningful declines in Asthma Control Test scores, characterized by drops of three points or greater following mild-to-moderate infection. However, these deteriorations proved predominantly transient. Larger longitudinal registry studies utilizing repeated within-person assessments found that mean test scores stabilized over extended observation, with substantial numbers of patients experiencing partial or complete recovery, showing no consistent evidence of sustained or irreversible impairment across long-term follow-up. Beyond standardized control questionnaires and exacerbation tallies, several included reports documented transient physiologic and management alterations. Pediatric investigations identified short-term reductions in spirometric parameters, including forced expiratory volume in one second and the ratio of forced expiratory volume in one second to forced vital capacity, alongside measurable increases in fractional exhaled nitric oxide indicating temporary airway inflammation. Protracted respiratory complaints, notably persistent cough lasting beyond four weeks, were documented across multiple observational cohorts. Concurrently, clinicians observed frequent management adjustments, including pharmacological therapy escalation and changes in patient adherence patterns following viral exposure. Nevertheless, extended longitudinal datasets indicated that both spirometric airflow measurements and symptomatic control generally rebounded over time, confirming that post-acute respiratory perturbations typically represent self-limiting disruptions rather than permanent declines in intrinsic pulmonary function. The review highlighted multiple biological and behavioural pathways that plausibly underpin the clinical outcomes documented across studies. Simultaneously, behavioural factors and shifts in medical utilization exerted measurable influences. Alterations in controller medication compliance, parental management adjustments in pediatric groups, physician prescribing patterns, and deferred outpatient follow-up during infection recovery all shaped documented control metrics. The observed recovery of clinical metrics across extended longitudinal follow-ups supports the interpretation that post-acute detriments stem primarily from reversible physiological stress rather than enduring modifications to underlying asthma pathophysiology. Quality appraisal of the included literature using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale showed overall methodological rigor ranging from moderate to low risk of bias. Retrospective designs, partially adjusted models, short follow-up periods, and diverse outcome definitions constituted common limitations among smaller cohorts, whereas large registry analyses with multivariable adjustment demonstrated higher methodological robustness. Substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity precluded quantitative meta-analysis, and the authors omitted formal Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation scoring due to observational design constraints. From a clinical perspective, the authors emphasize that routine escalation of asthma therapy following mild coronavirus infection is unsupported by current evidence, whereas individuals recovering from severe hospitalizations warrant closer proactive monitoring. Future research must prioritize prospective longitudinal investigations examining vaccination status, viral reinfection, biological therapy, and standardized outcome frameworks to refine long-term clinical care pathways. Subject of Research: Post-acute asthma control and exacerbation risk following SARS-CoV-2 infection Article Title: Asthma control and exacerbation risk following SARS-CoV-2 infection in the post-acute COVID-19 phase: a systematic review Article References: Alhumaid, S., Sabr, Z., Alshehri, S. The Ministry of Health is monitoring the situation, the Republican Centre for Hygiene, Epidemiology and Public Health reported. PJ.2.1 belongs to the Omicron lineage. According to the centre, it was first detected in Canada in early May. The variant was later identified in the United States, Spain, Australia and Singapore. There is currently no evidence that PJ.2.1 causes more severe COVID-19 or increases the risk of hospitalization or death. The incidence of acute respiratory infections in Belarus remains low and, according to the centre, continues to decline. It is 13% lower than at the same time last year. Children account for 63.7% of cases. Rhinoviruses, parainfluenza viruses and bocaviruses are the most frequently detected pathogens. Sporadic cases of influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 and COVID-19 are also being reported in the country. According to the World Health Organization, the global influenza test positivity rate remained below 10% in the week ending October 25. Influenza A was the predominant type among the viruses detected. The proportion of positive SARS-CoV-2 tests increased slightly but remained low. On November 6, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control reported that influenza activity in EU and European Economic Area countries remained low, although it was increasing in several countries. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 16, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health SARS-CoV-2 Infection in Pregnancy Linked to Reduced Placental Histone H3K4me3 Levels by November 13, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 SARS-CoV-2 Infection in Pregnancy Linked to Reduced Placental Histone H3K4me3 Levels Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Placental tissue from women who experienced SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy exhibits significant alterations in epigenetic markers, specifically showing reduced levels of trimethylated histone H3K4me3 in the syncytiotrophoblast. In an examination of placental specimens collected from 60 patients, researchers found that H3K4me3 levels in the syncytiotrophoblast were significantly reduced in both SARS-CoV-2-exposed patient groups when compared to unvaccinated control subjects. The observed reduction in this histone mark occurred in women with acute infection present at the time of delivery and in women with prior infection during gestation, with the most pronounced decrease recorded in those who had contracted the virus earlier in gestation. The investigation was designed to address how viral exposure correlates with chromatin architecture, given that histone modifications play a key role in chromatin organization and transcriptional regulatory potential. Previous research had observed reduced levels of trimethylated histone H3K4me3 and acetylated histone H3K9ac in placental tissue obtained from women with preeclampsia. Building directly upon those findings, the authors sought to determine whether maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy or at delivery is similarly associated with measurable changes in placental histone modifications across specific tissue compartments. To test this question, researchers performed laboratory analyses on placental tissue sections derived from 60 patients stratified across four distinct study groups. These cohorts comprised women with acute SARS-CoV-2 infection at delivery, women with documented prior infection during gestation, vaccinated controls, and unvaccinated controls. The experimental evaluation combined three laboratory techniques: immunohistochemical staining, exploratory western blot analysis, and qualitative immunofluorescence to assess histone modifications across the placental tissue specimens. Discover more Study Biology Track Pregnancy Infection Check Symptoms infection While syncytiotrophoblast H3K4me3 levels were significantly altered in the infected groups relative to unvaccinated controls, levels of acetylated histone H3K9ac showed no statistically significant differences between any of the four groups in any placental compartment after correction for multiple comparisons. In addition, the investigators analyzed potential confounding factors and detected no significant associations between syncytiotrophoblast H3K4me3 levels and maternal age, gestational age, or birthweight. To test the reliability of their observations, the team conducted a sensitivity analysis excluding patient cases with additional placental pathologies, which confirmed the robustness of the primary findings. Despite the clear identification of reduced syncytiotrophoblast H3K4me3, the authors emphasized important limitations regarding the interpretation of their results. Because no gene expression profiling was performed in the study, functional or transcriptional consequences of the observed H3K4me3 alterations cannot be inferred. The researchers noted that these findings remain descriptive and do not establish downstream molecular effects. They concluded that further investigations integrating both epigenetic and transcriptomic approaches are warranted to clarify the functional relevance of these histone changes for placental biology and pregnancy outcomes. 数学建模在理解传染病传播动力学与设计控制策略方面具有有效性,但暴发期间个体的行为反应常被忽视。传染病传播机制受恐惧、焦虑及行为改变的影响。基于上述挑战,研究人员提出了一种纳入恐惧动力学的新型传染病模型。研究人员对模型开展了理论分析,包括基本再生数(R0)与稳定性分析。通过敏感性分析识别出影响疾病传播的最关键流行病学参数。此外,研究人员采用最优控制理论确定具有成本效益的干预策略,以在减少实施成本的同时最小化感染人数。模型仿真借助计算工具MATLAB完成。同时,研究人员采用基于PyTorch深度学习库的人工神经网络(ANN)框架进行计算逼近与预测。各仓室的决定系数(R2)均接近1,且其他误差指标数值较低。这保证了神经网络框架具有较高的预测能力与逼近精度。仿真结果表明,疫苗接种、预防与隔离的联合策略可显著降低疾病传播。敏感性分析显示,传播参数对疾病扩散具有正向影响,而疫苗接种率、隔离率与康复率对疾病缓解贡献显著。所提出的混合数学-计算框架的整合为传染病控制中的疫情预测与公共卫生决策提供了高效可靠的工具。 论文主体解读: 研究背景与问题:数学建模已成为理解传染病传播动力学与设计有效干预策略的重要工具,仓室模型被广泛用于分析疾病扩散、估计阈值量并评估公共卫生措施的影响。然而,疫情暴发会引发恐惧等心理反应,这些反应通过社交距离、自我隔离、减少流动和增加防护措施等途径影响传播机制,可能降低感染率,但过度恐惧也会带来严重的社会与心理后果。既有研究存在明显缺口:许多流行病学框架忽视心理行为因素,另一些研究仅聚焦经典数值模拟而未整合人工智能方法,且将数学建模与基于ANN的疫情仿真结合于高维疾病系统的研究有限。因此,研究人员提出一个纳入易感者、无症状感染者、有症状感染者、恐惧感染者、恐惧相关者、疫苗接种者、隔离者与康复者共八个仓室的可控流行病学模型,旨在构建统一建模结构下整合流行病学控制措施、恐惧动力学与机器学习预测的综合计算框架。 研究开展与结论:研究人员通过数值求解器对系统进行仿真,并构建ANN框架学习与预测受控与非受控疫情行为,同时开展受控与非受控情景的对比分析以考察干预措施的有效性,并以均方根误差(RMSE)、平均绝对误差(MAE)及相对误差等统计误差指标验证ANN框架的性能与精度。结论表明,疫苗接种、预防与隔离联合策略可显著降低疾病传播;传播参数正向影响疾病扩散,而疫苗接种、隔离与康复率显著促进疾病缓解;所提出的混合数学-计算框架为疫情预测与公共卫生决策提供了高效可靠工具。 关键技术方法:一是构建含恐惧动力学的八仓室常微分方程(ODE)模型,采用下一代矩阵法计算基本再生数(R0)并开展稳定性与归一化前向敏感性分析;二是运用最优控制理论,基于Pontryagin最大值原理(PMP)推导伴随系统与三种控制变量(疫苗接种u1、预防u2、隔离u3)的最优性条件;三是使用MATLAB的ode45求解器进行数值仿真;四是以Python的SciPy中solve_ivp生成数据,基于PyTorch构建前馈神经网络(输入1个神经元、3个隐藏层各64个神经元、输出8个神经元,隐藏层用Tanh激活、输出层线性,Adam优化器、学习率10-3、MSE损失、3000轮训练)进行逼近与预测。 研究结果: 3.1 平衡点分析:设定无感染状态得到无病平衡点(DFE)E0及其总人口与易感者比例的表达式;同时给出地方病平衡点(EE)各仓室的稳态表达式,代入SH*与感染力κ*的平衡方程后形成非线性系统,其正解决定地方病平衡点。 3.2 解的正性:通过定理3.1与比较定理证明,在初始条件非负时各状态变量对所有t≥0保持非负,解轨迹不穿越坐标平面。 3.3 解的有界性:通过定理3.2、对全部方程求和并应用Gronwall不等式,证明在任意有限仿真区间[0,200]天内所有变量有界,可行域Ω正不变且吸引所有解。 3.4 基本再生数:以感染仓室(IA, IC, ICF)构建新感染矩阵F与转移矩阵V,由下一代矩阵K=FV-1的谱半径得到R0的显式表达式。 3.5 R0敏感性分析:以归一化前向敏感性指数计算各参数影响,结果显示传播参数η1、η2、η3为正向,其中η1影响较强;进展率α呈轻微负向;比例参数ρ的方向取决于η1与η2的相对大小;康复率λA、λC、λCF、隔离率γ1、γ2与疫苗接种率β均为负向;免疫消退参数τ可能提高R0。 4 最优控制分析:引入有界可测控制u1(疫苗接种)、u2(预防)、u3(隔离),建立受控系统与含感染人数与控制成本的二次型目标泛函,借助Pontryagin最大值原理构造Hamiltonian,推导八个伴随方程及终端横截条件,并由Hamiltonian对各控制的严格凸性与驻点条件,经投影得到三个最优控制的显式表达式。 5 数值仿真:使用MATLAB的ode45求解受控与非受控系统,结果显示受控情形下有症状感染者IC与恐惧感染者ICF显著下降,隔离仓室QH上升,接种仓室VH增加而SH下降,预防措施降低感染力并减缓传播;三种控制联合实施的抑制效果优于单一干预。 6 ANN框架:给出数据生成、数据集准备(归一化与70–80%训练/20–30%测试划分)、网络结构设计、MSE损失、Adam训练(1000–5000轮)、模型评估与可视化等完整算法流程,并以PyTorch实现;结果显示各仓室MSE、RMSE、MAE均较低,IC与ICF误差最小,易感与接种仓室绝对误差略高但相对误差低于0.5%,R2接近1,表明ANN能准确复现受控与非受控动态,可作为可靠的代理模型。 讨论与结论总结:讨论指出,正性与有界性分析验证了模型的数学与生物学适定性;平衡点结果表明感染持续依赖传播参数、进展率与恐惧行为动力学,恐惧感染仓室通过行为交互额外促进传播持续;阈值行为为R0<1时无病平衡点局部渐近稳定、疾病最终消失,R0>1时地方病平衡点存在且疾病持续。非受控仿真显示感染人群早期快速上升、易感者持续下降、康复者渐增,无症状者因未被识别而持续传播,恐惧相关仓室随疾病严重程度上升;受控仿真显示三种干预联合实施显著抑制传播并降低恐惧相关仓室,说明控制感染流行可间接稳定人群行为反应。ANN结果与数值解高度一致,受控系统因含时变控制函数而R2略低但仍具优异预测性能。结论部分译文如下:本研究构建并分析了一种纳入恐惧诱导行为动力学的新型流行病学模型,数学分析确立了正性、有界性、平衡点存在性及基于下一代矩阵法导出的基本再生数等重要理论性质,证明了R0<1时无病平衡点局部渐近稳定、R0>1时疾病持续;敏感性分析表明传播参数显著增加疾病扩散,而疫苗接种、康复与隔离措施有效促进疫情控制,强调降低有效接触率与强化干预策略的重要性;纳入疫苗接种、预防与隔离控制的最优控制框架成功减少感染人群并抑制疫情进展,数值仿真证实控制策略联合实施可大幅降低有症状与恐惧相关感染并改善康复动态、增加接种人群;ANN实现展现出优异预测能力,各流行病学仓室误差极低且决定系数接近1,所提出的基于ANN的框架为疫情预测、干预评估与实时公共卫生决策提供了计算高效的代理建模策略。总体而言,该混合框架为研究存在恐惧诱导行为反应的疫情传播动力学提供了综合方法,未来研究可纳入分数阶导数、随机效应、空间扩散、真实流行病学数据及先进深度学习架构以进一步提升真实性与预测能力。 supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Monday, November 16, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Pre-Pandemic Malaria Exposure Linked to Cross-Reactive SARS-CoV-2 Antibodies in Mozambique by November 14, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 Pre-Pandemic Malaria Exposure Linked to Cross-Reactive SARS-CoV-2 Antibodies in Mozambique Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A sero-epidemiological study conducted in Mozambique and Spain has identified serological cross-reactivity between antibodies targeting Plasmodium falciparum and SARS-CoV-2 in pre-pandemic African plasma samples. The cross-sectional investigation examined whether prior exposure to the malaria parasite influenced subsequent SARS-CoV-2 infection rates, antibody profiles, or COVID-19 clinical outcomes in co-endemic environments. The pathogens SARS-CoV-2 and Plasmodium falciparum coexist across the African continent, prompting scientific questions regarding potential immunological interactions between them and whether such interactions could have shaped the dynamics of the COVID-19 pandemic in Africa. Prior to this study, few empirical evaluations had directly assessed the relationship connecting historical malaria exposure with SARS-CoV-2 infection, patient symptomatology, and humoral cross-reactivity. Discover more Donate to Research Study Anatomy infection To evaluate these potential immune interactions, researchers analyzed plasma specimens collected across Mozambique and Spain between 2001 and 2022. Baseline immunoglobulin G cross-reactivity was determined using pre-pandemic archival samples, which included 175 specimens from Mozambique and 35 specimens from Spain. To assess post-pandemic dynamics, the research team analyzed blood samples from 2,576 individuals living in Manhiça, Mozambique, gathered between 2021 and 2022. Discover more Check Symptoms Study Biology Read Med Journals Get Allergy Relief Investigators measured immunoglobulin G, immunoglobulin M, and immunoglobulin A responses against blood-stage Plasmodium falciparum antigens as well as the spike and nucleocapsid antigens of SARS-CoV-2 using a multiplex suspension array assay. The quantitative assay demonstrated diagnostic accuracy for identifying SARS-CoV-2 seropositivity, recording specificity greater than 93 percent, an immunoglobulin G sensitivity of 85 percent, and an immunoglobulin A sensitivity of 75 percent, with the strongest performance observed against spike and receptor-binding domain antigens. Evaluation of the pre-pandemic cohorts revealed that African plasma samples exhibited significantly higher baseline anti-SARS-CoV-2 immunoglobulin G reactivity than European samples, a difference confirmed with high statistical significance (p < 0.0001). Furthermore, moderate positive correlations emerged between anti-Plasmodium falciparum and anti-SARS-CoV-2 immunoglobulin G levels in these pre-pandemic samples, illustrated by a significant correlation between antibodies against the receptor-binding domain and the malaria antigen EBA-175 (r = 0.41, p < 0.001). In the post-pandemic cohort of 2,576 participants from Manhiça, Mozambique, these observed antibody correlations progressively weakened as local SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence increased over the 2021 to 2022 observation period. Individual malaria exposure among participants was quantified using a composite malaria immunoglobulin G score and evaluated through statistical methods including Student t-tests, Spearman rank correlations, and unadjusted logistic regression models. Despite the detection of serological cross-reactivity in pre-pandemic plasma, statistical analysis established that prior exposure to Plasmodium falciparum was not associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection, SARS-CoV-2 seropositivity, or COVID-19 symptomatology. after the COVID-19 pandemic: decline of functional independence and frailty 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月15日 来源:Respiratory Investigation 2.1 编辑推荐: 背景:流行性感冒(influenza)对老年人仍构成沉重负担,且该形势已受到COVID-19大流行的影响。本研究旨在明确COVID-19大流行后老年流感住院患者的结局。方法:研究人员收集了2023年9月至2026年3月(COVID-19大流行后3个流感季)期间 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Open access 背景:流行性感冒(influenza)对老年人仍构成沉重负担,且该形势已受到COVID-19大流行的影响。本研究旨在明确COVID-19大流行后老年流感住院患者的结局。方法:研究人员收集了2023年9月至2026年3月(COVID-19大流行后3个流感季)期间在单一中心因重症流感需住院治疗的65岁及以上患者的临床资料,并对其结局、功能独立性与衰弱状况进行分析。结果:共纳入210例老年患者,中位年龄为79岁,入院前经临床衰弱量表(CFS)判定为轻度及以上衰弱者32例。肺炎为最常见的住院病因,其次为一般状况差和心力衰竭。中位住院时间为13天,院内死亡17例(8.1%)。60例因需进一步治疗或日常生活活动能力(ADL)恶化而转院,37例(17.6%)即使经过康复,功能独立性评定(FIM)仍低于70分。出院时19例(9.0%)CFS恶化。结论:COVID-19大流行后,流感感染在老年人中仍构成沉重负担。老年患者在急性疾病康复后仍易丧失功能独立性并陷入衰弱。为老年人采取包括疫苗接种在内的流感预防措施以避免住院将至关重要。(Influenza Internet Survey,UMIN000015989) 研究背景与问题 流行性感冒(influenza)每年冬季在全球引起流行,与高死亡率和高患病率相关,在老年人群中尤为突出。日本在COVID-19大流行前,流感相关死亡估计为每年3000至10000例,老年人超额死亡一直是严重问题。在日本,流感患者数在COVID-19期间有所下降,但自2023—2024年流感季起已回升至大流行前水平。已有报告显示,成人流感住院患者的临床表现在大流行前后存在差异,然而大流行后老年流感住院患者的临床病程尚不明确。基于此,研究人员开展了本研究,旨在明确COVID-19大流行后老年流感住院患者的结局。 研究方法 本研究为日本呼吸学会(JRS)流感互联网监测(Influenza Internet Survey)的子分析。研究人员纳入2023年9月至2026年3月期间诊断为流感且需住院的15岁以上患者,由日本全国JRS正式成员及协作成员登录互联网监测系统登记患者数据。流感诊断依据鼻咽拭子或痰标本快速抗原检测、聚合酶链反应(PCR)或临床诊断。研究人员从总数据中提取仓敷中央医院(Kurashiki Central Hospital)收治的患者数据,分为65岁及以上组与65岁以下组进行分析。对接受康复治疗的老年患者,由物理治疗师(PT)序贯计算功能独立性评定(FIM),比较康复介入时与出院时的FIM;临床衰弱量表(CFS)由PT根据访谈获得的入院前稳定状态及出院时状态进行评估。数据分析采用StatMate?软件Ver.6,连续数据以中位数及四分位距(IQR)表示,组间比较采用Mann-Whitney U检验,分类数据采用卡方检验,P<0.05为差异有统计学意义。本研究注册于UMIN(UMIN000015989),并经仓敷中央医院机构伦理委员会批准(No.4936,2026年6月9日)。 研究结果 3.1 患者特征:仓敷中央医院研究期间共登记65岁及以上患者211例、65岁以下患者66例。老年患者中位年龄79岁(IQR 73–85),男性占59.2%;实验室确诊甲型流感188例、乙型流感12例,另10例依据临床表现诊断。主要基础疾病为慢性肺疾病(68例,32.4%)、糖尿病(47例,22.4%)、恶性肿瘤(40例,19.0%)和慢性心脏病(37例,17.6%),21例(10.0%)接受免疫抑制治疗。65岁及以上人群中,仅16.7%可确认有流感疫苗接种史,10.5%有肺炎球菌疫苗接种史。 3.2 住院原因:肺炎为最常见住院原因,占34.3%;其次为流感感染本身所致一般状况差(21.9%);其他原因包括基础慢性呼吸疾病(慢性阻塞性肺疾病[COPD]、间质性肺炎、支气管哮喘等)急性加重、心力衰竭、肾功能衰竭等。 3.3 结局:65岁及以上患者中位住院时间13天(IQR 7–22),65岁以下为9天(IQR 6–11),两组差异无统计学意义(P=0.48)。195例(92.9%)入住普通病房,15例(7.1%)入住重症监护病房(ICU)。65岁及以上患者院内死亡率为8.1%,65岁以下为4.5%,两组差异无统计学意义(P=0.37)。死亡首位病因为肺炎(12例),其次为基础疾病恶化(3例:淋巴瘤、骨髓增生异常综合征、肝硬化)和心力衰竭(2例)。存活者中60例因需进一步治疗或日常生活活动能力(ADL)恶化而转院。105例(50.0%)住院期间接受康复治疗;65岁及以上康复患者中72例(68.6%)出院时FIM较康复介入时升高,但37例FIM未达到70分;65岁以下康复患者10例中9例出院时FIM≥70分。接受康复的患者中,32例入院前经CFS判定为轻度及以上衰弱(CFS≥5);出院时19例CFS较入院前恶化,1例改善。 讨论与结论 讨论指出,流感在全球尤其是老年人群中仍构成沉重临床负担。日本报告显示,重症流感(需ICU治疗或机械通气或导致死亡)发生率在60岁后急剧上升;流感住院患者死亡率在65–74岁为5.4%、75–84岁为7.4%、85岁及以上为12.2%,其中半数以上死亡发生在出院后。COVID-19大流行后流感再次成为重大问题:北半球2020年流感流行水平特别低,但2022年初开始回升。研究人员前期研究显示,大流行后住院患者数高于大流行前/期间,死亡率为7.9%,高于大流行前/期间的2.3%,可能归因于大流行期间人群流感免疫力减弱。本研究中老年患者院内死亡率为8.1%,高于本院2014—2019年的4.6%,但差异无统计学意义(P=0.15);作者认为大流行期间流感发病率显著下降导致人群水平群体免疫下降,易感人群增加,加之疫苗接种人数减少,以及2025—2026流感季全球出现的新变异株A(H3N2) subclade K导致疫苗效力降低,这些现象共同促成老年人群住院与死亡增加。肺炎为首位死因,与既往报告一致;日本65岁及以上成人23价肺炎球菌多糖疫苗接种覆盖率仍低至37.8%,需进一步努力提高接种率。老年患者住院时间较非老年患者有延长趋势,但差异未达统计学意义,可能与样本量有限、统计效能不足有关。老年住院患者中60例(28.4%)虽从流感相关急性疾病中恢复,仍无法直接回家而转往其他医院接受进一步治疗或康复。本研究最具影响的结果是ADL恶化导致衰弱:即使经过康复,37例(全部住院病例的17.5%、存活者的19.1%、康复者的35.2%)FIM未升至70分。日本临床实践中常用FIM≥70作为功能独立性指标,但其证据基础尚无文献明确确立;有研究报告区分社区出院与机构出院的最佳截断值为FIM 78分,可作为密切相关的参考。CFS在存活者中9.8%、康复者中18.1%恶化,提示流感感染可导致部分老年人短期衰弱加重。已有报告显示,28.6%的急性内科疾病存活住院老年患者出院时ADL功能差于基线;本文作者在另一研究中亦报告老年患者出院时ADL下降可长期持续。关于呼吸道感染后躯体与社会功能恶化,Torres等分析老年社区获得性肺炎住院患者,发现23%的存活者出现功能下降,且为短期和长期死亡的独立预测因素;Kato等报告三分之一护理与医疗保健相关肺炎住院患者出现躯体功能下降。就流感而言,Andrew等利用Barthel指数和衰弱指数分析65岁及以上流感及其他急性呼吸道感染(ARI)住院患者,流感患者功能下降发生率为20.2%、其他ARI为16.9%,8.2%出现持续性中度功能下降,9.9%出现灾难性失能。本研究证明,即使在COVID-19大流行后,流感感染在老年人群中仍构成沉重负担;死亡率较大流行前呈较高趋势,但差异无统计学意义;老年患者即使从流感急性疾病中恢复也易陷入衰弱。在老年人群中,即使发生流感,最重要的优先事项仍是预防进展为重症和避免住院。由于缺乏疫苗状态信息,本研究未直接分析疫苗接种状况,但研究结果凸显了疫苗接种的潜在影响;老年人流感疫苗效力已知会降低,三价流感疫苗虽可有效预防老年人住院,但其效力随衰弱程度增加而下降;近期针对老年人开发的高剂量流感疫苗已显示较标准剂量疫苗显著减少流感或肺炎相关住院;据2022年经济合作与发展组织(OECD)调查,日本65岁及以上人群疫苗接种覆盖率为58%,并不特别高,必须努力促进老年人流感疫苗接种。研究局限性包括:第一,研究在仓敷中央医院单一机构开展,但该院为地区核心医疗中心,提供从初级到三级急诊的广泛患者诊疗,且登记的JRS流感互联网监测病例数最多,故患者人群可合理反映全国医院真实临床实践,且因数据来自本院可详细考察患者躯体功能信息;第二,CFS未在所有患者中测量,且CFS为依赖PT总体印象的判断性主观工具,但其与临床结局的关联已广为人知;第三,仅在出院时评估患者状况,无法进行出院后长期随访,未来需开展流感感染后长期随访研究;第四,疫苗接种史在许多病例中未知,无法按疫苗接种状态进行亚组分析;第五,因研究性质为从监测数据中提取研究人群,仅使用FIM和CFS评估患者状态,这些工具是否合适尚不确定,今后可能需要多方面的评估方法。 结论:总之,即使在COVID-19大流行后,流感感染在老年人群中仍构成沉重负担。因流感相关疾病住院的老年患者即使从流感急性疾病中恢复,也倾向于功能独立性下降并陷入衰弱。避免老年人因流感住院十分重要,因此包括疫苗接种在内的老年人流感预防措施将至关重要。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 2000+篇,学术前沿动态全时追踪! supplementary_news.content: 妊娠期SARS-CoV-2感染相关合体滋养层H3K4me3水平降低的表观遗传改变研究 《Archives of Gynecology and Obstetrics》:Epigenetic alterations in the placenta associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月15日 来源:Archives of Gynecology and Obstetrics 2.6 编辑推荐: 组蛋白修饰在染色质组织及转录调控潜能中发挥关键作用。既往研究在子痫前期患者的胎盘组织中观察到三甲基化组蛋白H3第4位赖氨酸(H3K4me 3 )与乙酰化组蛋白H3第9位赖氨酸(H3K9ac)水平降低。基于上述发现,研究人员探讨了妊娠期或分娩时 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Research Open access 组蛋白修饰在染色质组织及转录调控潜能中发挥关键作用。既往研究在子痫前期患者的胎盘组织中观察到三甲基化组蛋白H3第4位赖氨酸(H3K4me 3 )与乙酰化组蛋白H3第9位赖氨酸(H3K9ac)水平降低。基于上述发现,研究人员探讨了妊娠期或分娩时SARS-CoV-2感染是否与胎盘组蛋白修饰的改变相关。他们对来自60例患者的胎盘切片进行免疫组织化学染色(IHC)、探索性蛋白质免疫印迹(WB)分析及定性免疫荧光(IF)染色,患者被分层为四组:分娩时急性SARS-CoV-2感染组、妊娠期既往感染组、接种疫苗对照组以及未接种疫苗对照组。与未接种疫苗对照组相比,两组SARS-CoV-2暴露组合的合体滋养层(SCT)H3K4me 3 水平均显著降低,其中妊娠期既往感染组的降低最为显著。经多重比较校正后,任何区室的H3K9ac水平在组间均无显著差异。SCT H3K4me 3 水平与母亲年龄、孕龄或出生体重之间未发现显著关联,且排除合并其他胎盘病变病例的敏感性分析证实了研究结果的稳健性。由于未进行基因表达谱分析,无法推断所观察到H3K4me 3 变化的基因转录后果。这些描述性发现提示,有必要进一步整合表观遗传学与转录组学方法,以阐明其对胎盘生物学和妊娠结局的功能学意义。 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(SARS-CoV-2)引发的2019冠状病毒病(COVID-19)大流行对全球医疗体系,尤其是孕妇及其胎儿等脆弱群体构成了前所未有的挑战。尽管一般人群的临床表现和流行病学特征已得到广泛研究,但其对孕妇的影响仍需深入阐明。妊娠期是一种独特的免疫状态,以深刻的生理变化为特征,旨在容纳半同种异体胎儿,现有证据提示孕妇可能对SARS-CoV-2感染产生不同的免疫应答,更易出现严重结局。此外,病毒是否存在母体-胎儿垂直传播,以及母亲感染对胎盘健康和胎儿发育的潜在影响,仍是重要的未解问题。表观遗传机制,包括组蛋白修饰,在妊娠期间对基因表达和染色质结构的调控至关重要。既往研究表明,三甲基化组蛋白H3第4位赖氨酸(H3K4me 3 )和乙酰化组蛋白H3第9位赖氨酸(H3K9ac)在子痫前期患者的胎盘组织中水平显著降低,提示表观遗传改变可能与该妊娠并发症的病理生理过程相关。鉴于子痫前期与COVID-19相关妊娠并发症在内皮功能障碍和炎症反应等方面存在病理生理重叠,研究人员假设SARS-CoV-2感染可能诱导胎盘组织产生类似的表观遗传改变,据此开展了本研究。 研究人员对60例孕妇的胎盘组织进行染色质免疫学分析,以探究妊娠期或分娩时SARS-CoV-2感染是否与胎盘H3K4me 3 和H3K9ac水平变化相关。样本按感染及接种状态分为四组。研究得出,SARS-CoV-2暴露组(包括急性感染和既往感染)的合体滋养层(SCT)H3K4me 3 免疫反应评分(IRS)较未接种疫苗对照组显著降低,且既往感染组降低最为明显;而H3K9ac水平在各组间差异无统计学意义。该发现为整合表观遗传学与转录组学的后续研究奠定了基础。 本研究主要技术方法包括免疫组织化学染色(IHC)、探索性蛋白质免疫印迹(WB)分析以及定性免疫荧光(IF)染色。研究队列来源于德国慕尼黑路德维希-马克西米利安大学(LMU)医院妇产科2017年8月至2022年7月期间收集的胎盘组织,最终纳入60例,分为四组:分娩时急性SARS-CoV-2感染组(n=15)、妊娠期既往感染组(n=16)、接种疫苗对照组(n=13)和未接种疫苗对照组(n=16)。染色评估采用半定量IRS,整合染色强度与阳性细胞比例;统计分析采用Kruskal-Wallis检验配合Dunn's事后检验及Bonferroni多重比较校正,并使用Spearman秩相关分析评估IRS与临床变量的关联。 研究结果: 描述性统计:四组患者在母亲年龄、出生体重及分娩孕周方面基本可比,急性感染组中有4例发生严重感染,2例需要插管;既往感染组大部分(75%)在妊娠34周前感染。 H3K4me 3 与H3K9ac在SARS-CoV-2暴露胎盘中的蛋白质免疫印迹分析:鉴于样本量限制,未接种疫苗对照组、接种疫苗对照组和既往感染组各纳入3例,急性感染组纳入2例。结果显示,既往感染组β-actin标准化的H3K4me 3 水平较未接种疫苗对照组呈降低趋势;H3K9ac则未见明确方向性模式。各指标样本间变异度大,仅作探索性展示。 COVID胎盘合体滋养层H3K4me 3 降低:IHC分析显示,与未接种疫苗对照组相比,急性感染组(p=0.0308)和既往感染组(p=0.0002)SCT区H3K4me 3 IRS均显著降低,且既往感染组低于接种疫苗对照组(p=0.0029)。两组对照之间以及急性与既往感染组之间差异无统计学意义(p>0.999)。绒毛外滋养层(EVT)和蜕膜基质区均未发现显著组间差异。 SARS-CoV-2暴露胎盘中乙酰化组蛋白H3K9ac:在SCT区,各感染及接种组中H3K9ac IRS中位数数值上低于未接种疫苗对照组,但经多重比较校正后,任何区室的组间两两比较均无统计学显著差异(校正后p>0.999),EVT和蜕膜基质区亦无显著差异。 相关性分析:Spearman分析显示,母亲年龄与所有区室的IRS评分均无显著相关;分娩孕周与蜕膜基质及EVT的H3K4me 3 IRS、以及EVT的H3K9ac IRS呈弱正相关,提示更早产可能与蜕膜区组蛋白修饰水平较低相关;出生体重与EVT的H3K9ac IRS弱相关。SCT IRS与任何临床变量均无显著相关。探索性免疫荧光染色显示,急性感染与既往感染组的组蛋白修饰信号相对于细胞核(DAPI)染色比率均视觉上降低,与IHC结果方向一致。 讨论部分指出,本研究属于描述性、假设生成性分析,而非位点特异性或功能性表观遗传研究。主要发现是急性感染与既往感染组SCT的H3K4me 3 IRS较未接种疫苗对照组显著降低,且既往感染组降幅最大;H3K9ac则在经多重比较校正后未见显著改变。H3K4me 3 通常富集于活跃转录基因的启动子区域,然而由于本研究未进行基因表达谱分析,无法将观察到的H3K4me 3 差异解读为转录活性改变的证据。病毒可通过炎症信号和细胞应激反应影响表观遗传调控机制,但所观察到的SCT H3K4me 3 改变的生物学意义仍不清楚,有待深入研究。 研究还指出,由于分析基于全组织切片,所观察值为跨细胞群的平均信号,可能低估细胞类型特异性效应。研究存在多项局限:未对血管内皮生长因子(VEGF)和胎盘生长因子(PlGF)等功能相关基因的调控区进行位点特异性组蛋白分析,亦无基因表达数据;WB样本量极小(n=2-3),仅为探索性;无法排除接种疫苗对照组中存在无症状或未诊断的既往感染;少数合并子痫前期、前置胎盘或胎盘植入的病例分布于各组,可能构成混杂因素,但敏感性分析显示排除这三例后,SARS-CoV-2暴露组SCT H3K4me 3 IRS较未接种对照组降低的模式仍然维持且略有增强(未接种对照组 vs. 急性感染:p=0.0095;未接种对照组 vs. 既往感染:p=0.0002),H3K9ac仍无显著性;分娩孕周与蜕膜区室组蛋白修饰水平呈弱相关,鉴于急性感染组平均分娩孕周较低,孕周对蜕膜区室发现可能存在部分混杂作用。此外,既往感染的详细孕周及感染-分娩间隔时间无法在部分病例中获取。 最后,研究结论强调,这些观察结果不应被解读为反对疫苗接种的证据,因为接种疫苗的对照组未表现出病理性胎盘组蛋白修饰模式,且疫苗接种与活动性感染在免疫学上发挥根本不同的作用。综上所述,本描述性研究证实,妊娠期SARS-CoV-2感染与合体滋养层H3K4me 3 水平显著降低相关,且该发现对排除额外胎盘病理病例具有稳健性;未来需更大队列并整合Bulk或空间转录组学方法,以明确这些表观遗传改变是否与胎盘基因表达变化及妊娠结局相关。 严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(SARS-CoV-2)引发的2019冠状病毒病(COVID-19)大流行对全球医疗体系,尤其是孕妇及其胎儿等脆弱群体构成了前所未有的挑战。尽管一般人群的临床表现和流行病学特征已得到广泛研究,但其对孕妇的影响仍需深入阐明。妊娠期是一种独特的免疫状态,以深刻的生理变化为特征,旨在容纳半同种异体胎儿,现有证据提示孕妇可能对SARS-CoV-2感染产生不同的免疫应答,更易出现严重结局。此外,病毒是否存在母体-胎儿垂直传播,以及母亲感染对胎盘健康和胎儿发育的潜在影响,仍是重要的未解问题。表观遗传机制,包括组蛋白修饰,在妊娠期间对基因表达和染色质结构的调控至关重要。既往研究表明,三甲基化组蛋白H3第4位赖氨酸(H3K4me)和乙酰化组蛋白H3第9位赖氨酸(H3K9ac)在子痫前期患者的胎盘组织中水平显著降低,提示表观遗传改变可能与该妊娠并发症的病理生理过程相关。鉴于子痫前期与COVID-19相关妊娠并发症在内皮功能障碍和炎症反应等方面存在病理生理重叠,研究人员假设SARS-CoV-2感染可能诱导胎盘组织产生类似的表观遗传改变,据此开展了本研究。研究人员对60例孕妇的胎盘组织进行染色质免疫学分析,以探究妊娠期或分娩时SARS-CoV-2感染是否与胎盘H3K4me和H3K9ac水平变化相关。样本按感染及接种状态分为四组。研究得出,SARS-CoV-2暴露组(包括急性感染和既往感染)的合体滋养层(SCT)H3K4me免疫反应评分(IRS)较未接种疫苗对照组显著降低,且既往感染组降低最为明显;而H3K9ac水平在各组间差异无统计学意义。该发现为整合表观遗传学与转录组学的后续研究奠定了基础。本研究主要技术方法包括免疫组织化学染色(IHC)、探索性蛋白质免疫印迹(WB)分析以及定性免疫荧光(IF)染色。研究队列来源于德国慕尼黑路德维希-马克西米利安大学(LMU)医院妇产科2017年8月至2022年7月期间收集的胎盘组织,最终纳入60例,分为四组:分娩时急性SARS-CoV-2感染组(n=15)、妊娠期既往感染组(n=16)、接种疫苗对照组(n=13)和未接种疫苗对照组(n=16)。染色评估采用半定量IRS,整合染色强度与阳性细胞比例;统计分析采用Kruskal-Wallis检验配合Dunn's事后检验及Bonferroni多重比较校正,并使用Spearman秩相关分析评估IRS与临床变量的关联。研究结果:描述性统计:四组患者在母亲年龄、出生体重及分娩孕周方面基本可比,急性感染组中有4例发生严重感染,2例需要插管;既往感染组大部分(75%)在妊娠34周前感染。H3K4me与H3K9ac在SARS-CoV-2暴露胎盘中的蛋白质免疫印迹分析:鉴于样本量限制,未接种疫苗对照组、接种疫苗对照组和既往感染组各纳入3例,急性感染组纳入2例。结果显示,既往感染组β-actin标准化的H3K4me水平较未接种疫苗对照组呈降低趋势;H3K9ac则未见明确方向性模式。各指标样本间变异度大,仅作探索性展示。COVID胎盘合体滋养层H3K4me降低:IHC分析显示,与未接种疫苗对照组相比,急性感染组(p=0.0308)和既往感染组(p=0.0002)SCT区H3K4meIRS均显著降低,且既往感染组低于接种疫苗对照组(p=0.0029)。两组对照之间以及急性与既往感染组之间差异无统计学意义(p>0.999)。绒毛外滋养层(EVT)和蜕膜基质区均未发现显著组间差异。SARS-CoV-2暴露胎盘中乙酰化组蛋白H3K9ac:在SCT区,各感染及接种组中H3K9ac IRS中位数数值上低于未接种疫苗对照组,但经多重比较校正后,任何区室的组间两两比较均无统计学显著差异(校正后p>0.999),EVT和蜕膜基质区亦无显著差异。相关性分析:Spearman分析显示,母亲年龄与所有区室的IRS评分均无显著相关;分娩孕周与蜕膜基质及EVT的H3K4meIRS、以及EVT的H3K9ac IRS呈弱正相关,提示更早产可能与蜕膜区组蛋白修饰水平较低相关;出生体重与EVT的H3K9ac IRS弱相关。SCT 既往感染:p=0.0002),H3K9ac仍无显著性;分娩孕周与蜕膜区室组蛋白修饰水平呈弱相关,鉴于急性感染组平均分娩孕周较低,孕周对蜕膜区室发现可能存在部分混杂作用。此外,既往感染的详细孕周及感染-分娩间隔时间无法在部分病例中获取。最后,研究结论强调,这些观察结果不应被解读为反对疫苗接种的证据,因为接种疫苗的对照组未表现出病理性胎盘组蛋白修饰模式,且疫苗接种与活动性感染在免疫学上发挥根本不同的作用。综上所述,本描述性研究证实,妊娠期SARS-CoV-2感染与合体滋养层H3K4me水平显著降低相关,且该发现对排除额外胎盘病理病例具有稳健性;未来需更大队列并整合Bulk或空间转录组学方法,以明确这些表观遗传改变是否与胎盘基因表达变化及妊娠结局相关。
